# tmDataQualityAnalyzer - changelog

What changed in each release, and in each step of the move from Qt to Avalonia, newest first: the developer's record.
The user's is `deploy/RELEASENOTES.txt`. Work that has landed but not shipped goes under **Unreleased**, and is folded
into the release's section when it is cut (`eng\check_release_consistency.ps1 -ReleaseMode` refuses a release
with an Unreleased section left).

Until plan step 6.5 this history was the Version History section of `docs/claude.md`, and it is kept as it was written:
the paths, class names and baselines in an entry are the ones of its day. Two moves since: the migration plan
(`docs/dotnet-migration/avalonia-plan.md`, which the "plan step" numbers below refer to) was deleted in 6.5, its steps
recorded here; and the parity review and soak records moved from `docs/dotnet-migration/` to `docs/records/`.

### Unreleased

#### The pre-release sweep: three small fixes, duplication folded, dead code and stale text removed

A read-only review of the whole tree before the release (the core, the binding, the app's models and views, the tests and
tooling, and the docs against the code) found no dead product code, no layering breach and no event-handler leak; what it did
find is here.

**Fixed:**
- **Customize View, a Frame Sync Lock stream given an empty name:** OK renamed its series to "" (a series with no name has no
  CSV header). Its name is now trimmed and an empty one changes nothing, as #418 made a Receiver SNR stream's
  (`CustomizeViewModel.Apply`; `CustomizeViewStateTests.AFrameSyncStreamGivenAnEmptyNameKeepsItsNameAndANameIsTrimmed`).
- **Recent Files and a path's case:** the same recording opened as `C:\x.ch10` from a dialog and as `c:\X.ch10` from a drop
  took two of the five slots. Paths are compared without case now (`RecentFiles.Add`). `PreferencesTests` pinned the old,
  case-sensitive behaviour (v2.x's), and now holds the new one.
- **The crash reporter's promise that writing never throws:** the report's text was built inside a `try` that caught only file
  errors, so an object whose `ToString` throws escaped the crash handler. The text is built in `CrashReporter.Describe`, which
  names such an object by its type (`CrashReportTests.AnObjectWhoseTextThrowsIsNamedByItsTypeAndTheReportIsStillWritten`).

**Folded:** a receiver's channel colour, written three times (first drawn, Auto-Color, a receiver's swatch), is
`PlotColors.ChannelColor`; the time shift of every series, written twice in `PlotViewModel`, is `ShiftTimes`; the CSV file
type `StorageDataFilePicker` defined twice is one.

**Removed or narrowed:** the unused `dataPath` in `test_abi_support.h`; `SelfDisposingObserver.FinishedAfterDispose`, which
no test read (whether the end comes after the dispose depends on whether the run reported progress, so it cannot be asserted);
`StreamResultHandle`'s parameterless constructor (no function returns one); `WithSnrStreamName` private; the Customize View
group constructors internal, without the defaults nobody used. Native includes: `textfile.h` from `calibrationrequest.cpp`,
`<string>` from `stepdetector.h`, `constants.h` from `framesetup.h` (checked by a `-Rebuild`) and unused ones from three test
files; `<cstddef>` added to `abi_run.cpp` and `<utility>` to `frameprocessor.cpp`, which use them; the project headers of nine
files in alphabetical order (`doctest.h` among them, as the guide says). `iTrackNumber` in `Ch10PacketReader::prepare` is
`trackNumber`, and the series `buildEnabledParams` makes is moved, not copied.

**Stale text corrected:** "a colour, a name" in Customize View (the rename prompt went in #418), "Help is the window's", the
items `PlotCommands` says ask the user, `LastFolder` as where Export writes, the legend returning "to the top right", the CSV
writer's "one row per distinct millisecond" (`CsvFile.Write`, `tmdq_abi.h`; each column has been on its own sample grid since
#380), the handles comment (six scoped handles stay `IntPtr`), `Startup`'s exit codes and `TemplateFile.Read`'s exceptions.
`docs/guide.md`: US4.0's menu list gains Auto-Color and Reset Colors, its "beyond the three primaries / first four" criterion
says what `PlotColors.Weakness` does, US9.0's "primaries", the renamed SNR stream in the legend, and the test catalog's "six

#### Auto-Color Visible Series and Reset Colors, on the plot's context menu (US4.0)

**Auto-Color Visible Series** recolours what is drawn so its streams are as easy to tell apart as the palette allows.
`PlotViewModel.AutoColorVisible` groups the series into the units Customize View colours as one (a recording's Frame Sync
Lock stream with both its metrics; a Receiver SNR receiver or antenna channel), and each unit with a series drawn
(`EffectiveVisible`, so Plot File's choice counts) takes the next of `PlotColors.AutoColorHues` in plot order: its combined
channel the hue, its others `Shade`'s tints of it, solid and dotted as before. A unit with nothing drawn keeps its colours,
and two recordings' streams of one number, which are first given one colour (it goes by stream number), become two units.
The hues are the palette's 15 less the gold, ordered farthest first: the red, then each time the hue whose least OKLab
distance to those taken is the greatest (red, sky, forest, purple, lime, orange, ...), so a plot of a few streams gets the
most different of them; the 15th unit takes the first again. The gold is left out because it is 1.8 to 1 on the light
theme's white, under the 2.0 `ChartPalette.MinSeriesContrast` holds a series to, and would be drawn darker than given; every
other hue is at least 2.0 on both themes' backgrounds, so a theme switch never needs it run again. The user chose the
palette over computed colours, visible series only, and both themes. **Reset Colors…** asks (`ChooseAsync`, one entry,
chosen) and gives every series, shown or not, the colour `PlotColors.Assign` gives a plot of those series, replacing what
Customize View, a template or Auto-Color set. Both items sit under Customize View…; Auto-Color asks nothing and is
available while a series is drawn. `PlotSeries.Dotted`'s summary still described the dotted second 15 of v2.x and now says
what is dotted.

Checked: `AutoColorTests` (new, 10 cases: the order, each hue the farthest from those before it checked from the
definition, contrast on both themes, units, Plot File, stacked recordings, nothing drawn, the commands, Reset and its
Cancel) and `ChartViewTests`' menu cases. The mutation check: 18 new mutants in `eng\mutants\series-colours.json`
(A1-A18), all 18 caught. A17 (Auto-Color left out of the commands told when the plot changes) first survived: the menu
asks a command again when it opens, so no menu case saw it; the commands test now holds both new commands to being told. The manual's context-menu section and the Main Context Menu figure, the README and US4.0/US4.1
say it. App baseline: 925 to 935 passed (`Total: 969`, 34 not run).

#### Export remembers its folder; a Receiver SNR receiver is recoloured as one, and a stream can be renamed

**Export's folder.** Export proposed the folder a recording, CSV or template was last opened from, so after exporting to
another folder the next Export went back to the recording's. It now proposes the folder it last wrote a file to in the
session (the first file written: the data, else the image, else the log; an export that wrote nothing leaves it), then the
last folder opened from, then the application's root as before. It is not a preference: a new session starts as before.
`SessionExport.WriteAsync` returns the first file written; `MainWindowViewModel.LastExportFolder` holds its folder.

**A receiver's colour.** Customize View's Receiver SNR tab recoloured each channel (L, R, C) on its own, from a menu on its
box, which broke the receiver's family of shades. A swatch beside each receiver now sets the receiver's colour: C takes
it, and L and R the lighter shades a receiver is first drawn with (`PlotColors.Shade`, `Weakness`). The channels' menu
(Rename series…, Change color…) is gone; the receiver's text and swatch are in its full colour (C's), where the text was
L's.

**A stream's name.** A Receiver SNR rename set the series' name, but the legend never showed it (its rows are built from
numbers, `CH<id> <L|R|C>_RCVR<n>`), and it was one channel at a time. The tab now has **Stream name** under the stream
list: OK replaces only the stream's part of each of its series' names, `<channel id> - <stream name> <channel name>`
(`PlotViewModel.RenameSnrStream`, split as the core's CSV import splits a header: the channel name after the last space),
so an exported CSV's columns carry the name, as a Frame Sync Lock rename's always did, and still read back as SNR of their
receivers; the legend shows the name in place of `CH<id>`. A series keeps the name it was made with (`PlotSeries.OriginalName`),
which is how a renamed stream is told (`IsSnrStreamRenamed`), so a template, which puts each series' name back, renames the
stream too. Nothing is reordered: the plot, the legend and the CSV keep the recording's order. An empty name renames
nothing; an antenna's stream (US10.0) keeps its unit's name. The soak's exports are untouched: it renames nothing.

**How it was checked.** New tests: `ExportProposesTheFolderItLastWroteToForTheRestOfTheSession`,
`RenamedSnrStreamsAreExportedInTheirPlacesAndReadBackAsSnrOfTheirReceivers` (names that sort the other way round, one with
" - " and digits; the read-back's metric, stream, receiver, channel and samples, and a byte-for-byte second export),
`ARenamedStreamIsShownByItsNameAndKeepsItsPlace`, `AStreamNamedByATemplateIsShownByThatName`,
`AStreamLeftAloneOrGivenAnEmptyNameIsNotRenamed`; the Customize View tests that used the channels' menu now drive the
receiver's swatch and the name box, and `CustomizeViewReadsTheAntennasStreamsWithHVAndCAndNotAsReceivers` holds that an
antenna's stream is not renamed. Mutation check: 13 new mutants, SA1 to SA6 in `csv-export-async.json` (the folder
proposed, the first file written, a failed file, the trim, the split at the last space, the CSV's columns sorted by name),
SA7 to SA10 in `hand-written-properties.json` (the shades, an emptied name, the stream renamed, an antenna's rename) and
SA11 to SA13 in `plot-zoom-and-legend.json` (the legend's name, how a rename is told, the legend sorted by name): all 13
CAUGHT. SA10 first SURVIVED (nothing held an antenna's stream unrenamed: the test above now does) and SA5 first failed to
compile (CA1307 on `IndexOf(char)`: written with `StringComparison.Ordinal`). Re-anchored for moved text and run again,
all CAUGHT: `calibration-observer.json` S1, `csv-export-async.json` C3 and C4, `accessible-names.json` N16;
`hand-written-properties.json` C3 now mutates the receiver's swatch (the channel's Change color is gone). The 18 kept
lists the change reaches (`eng\mutants_affected.ps1 -Base main -Run`, 283 mutants) gave every verdict as recorded but
`accessible-names.json` N17, which SURVIVED: with the receiver's header a panel (its box and its swatch), a receiver's
open/close toggle left without its style is read as "RCVR 1", a name unique and speakable, so the general rules passed it.
`AccessibleNamesTests` now holds the toggles' names ("Open or close RCVR n"), and N17 is CAUGHT. Baselines: the
application's suite **925 passed** / 0 failed / 0 skipped, 34 not run (`Total: 959`; was 920 and 954); the library's
unchanged.

### v3.5.1 — The deep dive after v3.5.0: placement after an import, the batch's Cancel, a faster export

A patch release (2026-11-27), the v3.5.1 plan's four PRs (`docs/future_plans/v3.5.1.md`). What the user sees: a recording opened after an imported antenna log or CSV is placed by its clock instead of decades later, Zoom Back is right after a recording that starts earlier is stacked, an out-of-order CSV is shown to its end, an unreadable CSV says so, the cursor's label carries a rounded-up fraction, Process Multiple Files says it clears the plot and its Cancel stops the batch (#415), the CSV export is about twice as fast (#415), the Receiver SNR tab is named for a screen reader (#415), and the manuals read against v3.5.0 (#414). Underneath: Avalonia 12.2.0 (xunit stays on 3.2.2), figures that render the same twice, the kept-mutant run in reach of every change (`eng\mutants_affected.ps1`) and all 734 run again (#416). The release PR itself carries the version, the notes and the re-rendered figures alone.

#### Every kept mutant run again on Avalonia 12.2: every verdict as recorded (v3.5.1, PR 3)

`eng\mutants_affected.ps1 -All -Run`, in two parts in two worktrees: the 61 lists in `eng\mutants\`, 734 mutants. 699 CAUGHT, 32 SURVIVED, 3 COMPILE, none without a verdict, and each SURVIVED and COMPILE carries that `expect` (an equivalent mutant or one the compiler refuses, as recorded when it was kept), so both parts exit 0 and no list needed re-anchoring or a new test.

Also here: seven `\b` sequences in this changelog (`eng\build_manual.ps1`, `deploy\build_package.ps1`, `eng\build_core_dll.ps1`), lost to a backspace character by an earlier edit, are written back; nothing else in the tree had one.

#### The manual's figures render the same twice: the run log's progress lines are set to one set (v3.5.1, PR 3)

**What was unsteady.** The reader logs "NN% read..." at the first time-gated progress check past each tenth of the file, so a fast run skips tenths: one render's log read 21, 41, 61 and 81 %, the next 21, 51 and 81 %. `ManualFiguresTests` already set each line's digit to the tenth ("42%" to "41%") and the racing threads' lines in one order, but not which lines there were, so three run-log figures changed on a re-render with nothing in them changed (seen in PR 2).

**What changed.** `Steady` puts the canonical four (21, 41, 61, 81 %) in place of whatever percentages a run logged, in the reader's place among the racing lines; `SteadyLog` writes back a log that may now be longer or shorter. The core's log is untouched: it says what one run did. `walk-fs-04-processing.png` and `walk-theme-01-light-plot.png` were re-rendered with the canonical set (`walk-err-01-log-error.png` already showed it).

**How it was checked.** `TheLinesOfTheThreadsThatRaceAreSetInOneOrderEachStreamKeepingItsOwn` now also holds that another run's tenths (21, 51, 81) give the same lines. `eng\build_manual.ps1` run twice in a row: every figure identical but `walk-cust-02-snr-tree.png`, the checkbox edge known to vary about one render in four (as does `walk-csv-03-customize.png`'s; both left as committed).

**The flake hunt.** The application's suite run twelve times (eight free, four pinned to 4 logical cores as the hosted runner has): 920 passed, 0 failed, every time; none of the failures seen once before (`ChartPlotStateTests`, the CSV memory guard, `PackageLicenceTests`, the figure fixture's cleanup) came back.

#### xunit stays on 3.2.2: Avalonia's headless test runner does not run on xunit 4 (v3.5.1, PR 3: tried)

**What was tried.** xunit.v3 3.2.2 to 4.0.3 (the plan's PR 3). The library's suite ran on it (438 passed; the In-Process Runner v4.0.3), but in the application's suite every Avalonia test (`[AvaloniaFact]`, `[AvaloniaTheory]`) failed at discovery with `MissingMethodException: Xunit.v3.TestIntrospectionHelper.GetTestCaseDetails(...)`: `Avalonia.Headless.XUnit` 12.2.0, the latest release, is built against xunit 3.2.2's extensibility API, which 4.0 changed. No release or prerelease of it depends on xunit 4 yet (all of 12.1.4 to 12.2.0 name `xunit.v3.extensibility.core` 3.2.2).

**What stays.** Both test projects on 3.2.2: running the library's tests on 4.x alone would need a second xunit version in `Directory.Packages.props`, against its one-version rule, for no measured gain (the plan's measurement: a mutant's time is its build, so xunit 4 cannot speed the mutation check, and its `all` parallel mode is measured only once the app suite can run on it). `Directory.Packages.props` says why beside the pin; move when an `Avalonia.Headless.XUnit` built for xunit 4 ships.

#### Avalonia 12.1.4 to 12.2.0 (v3.5.1, PR 3)

A minor release of the UI framework, taken alone so that anything it moves is its own. `AvaloniaVersion` in `Directory.Packages.props` moves every Avalonia package together (the app's, the headless test host's).

**Checked:** the app suite, Release: 920 passed, 0 failed, 34 not run (the soak's explicit cases), every pixel-reading test included; the package licence check passes on the resolved packages (46 for the app, 27 for the tests), so no new licence came with it.

#### The CSV export is about twice as fast: an exact tie is found from the binary value, not by printing 1100 places (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**Measured first (the user's bar: change it only for about 20 % or more on a large export).** A throwaway timing of a 56-column export of 2,268,000 cells (the size of the #345 case): about 835 ms in all, of which the cell sort was about 73 ms (9 %, so the sort stays as it is) and the number formatting about 690 ms, where plain `std::format` of the same values takes about 174 ms. The difference was `textformat::isExactTie`: for about one value in ten (a 5 in the seventh place) it printed the value to 1100 decimal places to see whether the 5 was exact.

**What changed.** `isExactTie` decides from the binary value: written as m * 2^f with m odd, a value is a tie at d places exactly when f = -(d+1) (then 2 * 10^d * value = m * 5^d is an odd integer). No text is made; the output is the same by construction. A suggestion to parse the shorter text back and compare was not taken: it calls the double nearest a tie a tie, which changes the output.

**After:** the same export about 397 ms, 52 % less.

**How it was checked.** The old 1100-place test is kept in `test_textformat.cpp` as the oracle, and a new case holds the two equal over 40,080 values: ties (odd multiples of 2^-(d+1)) at ten precisions, one step either side of each, the same ties one precision finer, even multiples, arbitrary values from 2^-60 to 2^60, subnormals and the largest doubles. The v2.14 sweep digests and every CSV byte-for-byte test pass unchanged (native 579 cases). Mutants K6 to K8 of `eng/mutants/csv_export_grid.json` CAUGHT (the power one place off, the trailing zeros not counted, the mantissa a bit short).

#### Scripts that could report a run that did not happen (v3.5.1, PR 2)

From the sweep:
- **`eng\build_manual.ps1`** deleted the tracked figures before it checked that the core was built and the tests compiled, so a failed run left them gone; it checks first now, clears the variables it set in a `finally`, and runs the embedder from the repository's root (`eng\embed_manual_images.py` reads relative paths, so started from another folder it failed or wrote another checkout's manual; `deploy\build_package.ps1` reaches it through this script).
- **`eng\run_soak.ps1`** called a run "same" whenever the test exited 0, even if no result was written (a renamed class, a filter that matched nothing); it deletes the last run's `result.json` first and calls a run with none "NOT RUN", a failure.
- **`deploy\sandbox\run_sandbox_test.ps1`** could find the last run's `results.txt` (left by a delete that a Sandbox window blocked) and report it at once as this run's; it stops and says why instead.
- **`deploy\build_msi.ps1`** read its WiX version from a literal beside a comment saying it matched `dotnet-tools.json`; it reads it from there.
- **Comments:** `build_package.ps1` called the MSI per-machine (it is per-user or per-machine since #412); `test_dotnet.ps1` gave the library a DLL search that is the tests' (`Support\Env.cs`).

**The figures:** `build_manual.ps1` (full) re-rendered `walk-batch-02-apply-dialog.png` for the batch confirmation's new note. Five other figures came out different only in run-to-run noise and were put back: the run log's time-gated "NN% read" lines in three (21/41/61/81 % one run, 21/51/81 % the next) and a checkbox edge in the two Customize View figures. The progress lines were thought steady since #296; that they are not is for PR 3's flake hunt.

#### Open reads the plot again after Configure Streams, and reports a core error instead of crashing (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** Found by the sweep. `LoadAsync` decided whether the recording is added beside what is shown (`keep`) before it opened the file, but the plot's menu stays live meanwhile: a plot emptied by Clear Plot or Remove File while Configure Streams was up was still treated as one to add to (no title, a "(2)" name). And a `TmdqException` from building a stream's series escaped the command to the crash report (a dropped file goes through it too).

**What changed.** `keep` is read again once Configure Streams has answered; a `TmdqException` is reported in the status and the log ("ERROR: <file> could not be shown: ..."). The drop handler stays `async void`, as an event handler must be: with this catch, what it awaits reports its own errors. The same window in Import CSV (the parse is short and has no dialog) is left.

**How it was checked.** `OpenStacksTests.APlotClearedWhileConfigureStreamsIsUpIsWhereTheRecordingStarts`; mutant A14 of `eng/mutants/processing-flow.json` CAUGHT. The `TmdqException` catch has no test: no input makes the core refuse a stream's series it has just built.

#### A packet reader prepared again forgets the earlier prepare's queues (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** Found by the sweep (latent: the application makes one reader per run). `Ch10PacketReader::prepare` may be called again (it gives its earlier handle back and clears its channel table) but kept `m_routing` and `m_all_queues`, so a run fed and ended the earlier call's queues too: queues of streams that, in a host, may already be destroyed.

**What changed.** `prepare` clears both with the channel table.

**How it was checked.** `Ch10PacketReader: a reader prepared again routes only to the queues of its last prepare` (the last prepare's queue gets every packet and one end marker; the first gets nothing). Mutants L90 (routing kept) and L91 (queues kept) of `eng/mutants/reader-lifetime.json` CAUGHT, L90 by a hang: the earlier queue fills, nothing drains it, and the reader blocks, which the harness counts as caught.

#### An imported CSV whose rows are out of time order is shown to its latest time; a first stamp below zero is a first row (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** Found by the sweep. The CSV reader took the span (`xMax`) from each column's last row, and the plot took a series' end from its last sample (`SpanOf`, `SetVisibleSource`), so a file whose rows are not in time order (a clock that stepped back, a file edited by hand) was cut short at the view's end. And the reader used a negative first time as its "no first row yet" mark, so a first stamp that reads below zero (`001:00:-1:00.000`) re-seeded the base on the next row and both rows read 0.

**What changed.** `CsvSeriesParser` takes the largest time for the span and a flag for the first row. `PlotViewModel` finds an out-of-order series' earliest and latest time by a pass (`Extent`; a series in order still reads its two ends). Rows before the first row's time still read below zero and stay outside the view, as before; that part is unchanged.

**One departure from v2.14.2, on purpose:** the v2.14.2 import digest (`csvseries: the core reads every generated file as the code it replaced did`) is re-pinned. Of its 400 generated files, the 76 with rows out of time order now have a larger `xMax`; recomputed with `xMax` taken the old way, the digest is exactly the recorded one, so nothing else moved (checked with a throwaway comparison, not kept).

**How it was checked.** A native case for both (an out-of-order file spans to its largest time; a first stamp of -60 s is the base and the next row is at 60 s), `PlotTests.ASeriesWhoseTimesAreOutOfOrderIsShownToItsLatestTimeAndFromItsEarliest`; mutants K4 and K5 of `eng/mutants/csv_export_grid.json` and Z6 of `eng/mutants/plot-zoom-and-legend.json` CAUGHT.

#### Process Multiple Files says it clears the plot, and its Cancel stops the batch (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**The user's decisions (2026-11-27):** the batch keeps clearing the plot (it is the one action that does not stack) but says so, and Cancel in the progress dialog stops the whole batch instead of skipping one file.

**What changed.** The confirmation window states that the plot is cleared first and what Cancel does (`BatchApplyViewModel.ClearsThePlot`, the `ClearsNote` text). `BatchRunner`: Cancel skips this file and every one after it ("Batch cancelled at <file>: the files after it were not processed."), keeps the files processed (they stay on the plot and are what Save Template captures), still exports those when a folder was chosen, and ends "Batch cancelled: N processed, M skipped.", logged as a warning (`BatchResult.Cancelled`). A `TmdqException` or `IOException` from a file's run is now skipped like a failed file instead of escaping the batch, which left its kept files unrecorded; no test provokes one (the core gives no way to), so that part is unchecked. The manual, the walkthrough and the guide say both.

**How it was checked.** `TemplateBatchTests`: Cancel at the second of three files stops the batch (the progress dialog is shown twice, not three times), the first file stays with the template's names and colours, the status and the log; the confirmation window's note, word for word. Mutants B8 to B11 of `eng/mutants/apply-template-busy.json` CAUGHT (Cancel no longer stopping, the headline, the log level, the note). The confirmation's manual figure changes with the note: re-rendered at the end of this PR.

#### Customize View's Receiver SNR tab names each channel for a screen reader (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** Found by the sweep: on the Receiver SNR tab each receiver's channel boxes read "L", "R" and "C", so a screen reader heard three receivers' "L" alike, and each receiver's open/close toggle took the same name as the receiver's box inside it. `AccessibleNamesTests` showed Customize View on its first tab only, so the receivers were never in the tree it read.

**What changed.** A channel's box is named "L of RCVR 3" (`ChannelItem.AccessibleName`; "H of Stream 3" for an antenna's log), a receiver's box "All channels of RCVR 3", and its toggle "Open or close RCVR 3" (a style scoped to the receivers' expanders). What the boxes show is unchanged.

**How it was checked.** `AccessibleNamesTests.TheRowsAndTheSetupDialogsOfARecordingAreNamed` now opens the Receiver SNR tab with every receiver expanded (nine channel boxes) and failed before the change on the duplicated names; mutants N15 to N17 of `eng/mutants/accessible-names.json` CAUGHT.

#### A CSV that cannot be read says so, not that it is of the wrong layout (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** `PlotCsv.Parse` turns every reader error into "neither layout", so a stale Recent Files entry, or a file another program holds open, was reported as "not a recognized CSV ... Nothing was imported".

**What changed.** Import CSV first opens the file for reading (sharing it, as the readers do); a file that is not there reads "could not be read: the file is not there.", one that is held gives the system's reason, and only a file that opens and fits neither layout gets the layout message.

**How it was checked.** `PhasedArrayImportTests.AFileThatIsNotThereOrIsHeldElsewhereIsSaidToBeUnreadableNotOfTheWrongLayout`; mutants O26 and O27 of `eng/mutants/antenna-overlay.json` CAUGHT.

#### The cursor's time label carries a fraction that rounds up to a whole second (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** `clocktime::format` (the cursor readout's label, through `tmdq_clock_time_format`) split the fraction off after the day, hour, minute and second fields, so a time of 3600.9996 s read `01:00:00.1000`: the fraction rounded up to 1000 ms and did not carry. v2.14.2 did the same. The CSV's time column uses `formatMilliseconds` and was never affected.

**What changed.** The fraction is rounded first; at 1000 ms it carries into the seconds, and on into the minutes, hours and day. Every other stamp is unchanged, tie for tie: a first attempt that rounded the whole time to milliseconds first changed three of the 16,000 generated stamps of the v2.14 digest test by 1 ms (exact half-millisecond ties), and was dropped for this one, which leaves that digest as recorded.

**How it was checked.** A native case for the carry into the seconds, the minutes, the hours and the day, the stamps just below the half and without milliseconds; the v2.14 digest test unchanged; the managed `FormatsDigest` held one recorded stamp of exactly this case (`rounding-up`, 0.9996 s, recorded as `007:00:00:00.1000`), changed by hand to the carried `007:00:00:01.000` and said so in its header; mutants K1 to K3 of `eng/mutants/csv_export_grid.json` all CAUGHT (the boundary, the lost carry, the lost day).

#### Zoom Back no longer lands off after Open stacks a recording that starts earlier (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** Found by the sweep, read from the code and then reproduced in a test: `AddStream` moves every series later by `shift` when a recording starts before what is shown, and shows the whole span, but kept the zoom history, whose views are in the old elapsed seconds; Zoom Back landed `shift` seconds off. `ShowCsv` and `AdvanceTimeBase` already moved or cleared it; `AddStream` did neither. Stacking made it reachable.

**What changed.** `AddStream` clears the history when it shifts the series (the view is the whole span then anyway).

**How it was checked.** `OpenStacksTests.ARecordingThatStartsEarlierThanWhatIsShownLeavesNoZoomHistoryInTheOldSeconds` (an export a day later than the recording stands for the earlier-starting one); mutant O25 of `eng/mutants/antenna-overlay.json` (the clear removed) CAUGHT.

#### A recording opened after an imported log or CSV is placed by the clock (v3.5.1, PR 2)

**What was wrong.** Found by the code sweep for v3.5.1 and reproduced: import an antenna log (or an exported CSV), then Open a recording, and the recording sat at its epoch seconds, about 1.78e9 s, a lifetime after the log (the log at 0 to 2,478 s; the axis spanned 56 years). An import states a day and a time of day but no absolute time, so the time base's clock was set and its absolute seconds were not, and `AddStream` placed the recording against an absolute base of 0. Stacking made it reachable in v3.5.0; the other order (a recording, then a log) was right, because an import is placed by the clock. A second form: a file that starts before everything shown moves the clock earlier (`ShowCsv`) but left the absolute base where it was, so the next recording was placed by the old one.

**What changed.** `PlotViewModel` remembers that the clock came from an import (`_clockOnly`). The next recording added gives the base the clock's moment, in the year the recording says (an import has no year), through the existing `TimeBase.Adopt`, so no ABI changed (`AbsoluteFromClock`); an import that starts earlier moves the absolute base with the clock. `Clear` forgets the flag.

**How it was checked.** `OpenStacksTests`: a recording opened after a log lands where it lands when the log is imported after it (both orders compare equal, and the axis is under 1e8 s), and a recording opened after an import that starts a day earlier lands at the same clock time as the first. Mutants O21 to O24 of `eng/mutants/antenna-overlay.json`: all four CAUGHT (the import's clock taken for an absolute time; the call removed; the one-based day of the year; the base not moving with the clock).

#### The shared native-core test collection stays (v3.5.1, PR 1: tried and reverted)

**What was tried.** 35 of the app suite's 58 test files share `NativeCoreCollection`, so xunit runs their 726 tests one at a time, because two tests point `TMDQ_CORE_DLL` at a missing file for a moment. Moving those two into a collection of their own that runs alone, and dropping the shared one, took the suite from 53 s to 38 s on the development machine (28 cores), 0 failures in nine runs there, including four on 4 threads and three pinned to 4 logical cores.

**Why it was reverted.** On the hosted runner (4 cores) it bought nothing and cost reliability. `main`'s three latest runs took 87, 89 and 97 s of app-test time; this change took 79 and 98 s, and failed both runs with a recording "being used by another process" when a test's own `Dispose` deleted its folder (`ShortRecordings`, then `TemplateBatchTests`), the same kind of failure the notes record as rare on CI. It could not be reproduced here, so the cause is not known (a close delayed behind the irig106 setup lock, or the runner's scanner on a busier disk, are the candidates); what is known is that the gain exists only where cores are idle. A change that is faster here and flaky there is the wrong trade for a suite whose job is to be trusted, so the collection stays. **If this is tried again,** do it only with the reproduction found first (the flake hunt of PR 3), and measure the hosted run, not this machine.

#### `eng\mutants_affected.ps1`: the kept lists a change reaches (v3.5.1, PR 1)

**Why.** The kept mutant run is 708 mutants in 61 lists and costs most of a day (a mutant is about 10 s, nearly all of it the build), so a change checked its own list by hand and the rest only at a release. **What.** The script reads the change (`git diff` against `-Base`, default `main`, plus untracked files) and names every list with a mutant in a changed file, a list that changed itself, or a list that runs the class of a changed test file; `-Run` runs them in turn through `mutate.ps1` (`-Parts`/`-Part` pass through to share the run between worktrees); `-All` names every list, which is what a release runs. **Checked** by running it against this branch (27 lists, 375 mutants, for a change that touched every test class), against `HEAD~1`, and with `-All` (61 lists, 708 mutants); PSScriptAnalyzer is clean.

#### The wizard's "Launch tmDataQualityAnalyzer" starts the application after an install "only for me"

**What was wrong.** Found by the user, installing a v3.5.0 candidate per-user: the Finish page's "Launch tmDataQualityAnalyzer" box did nothing. The install log showed the launch action ran and failed (return value 1631). It started the exe by its File row (`FileRef="AppExe"`), whose path the wizard resolves when it starts, to the per-machine folder; the scope page's "only for me" changes the `APPLICATIONFOLDER` property (and the install itself goes there) but not that resolved path, so the launch looked for `C:\Program Files\tmDataQualityAnalyzer\tmDataQualityAnalyzer.exe`, which a per-user install does not have.

**What it does now.** Finish runs two actions, in order: `SetLaunchApplicationExe` sets `LAUNCHAPPLICATIONEXE` to `[APPLICATIONFOLDER]\tmDataQualityAnalyzer.exe`, and `LaunchApplication` (type 50) starts the exe that property names, without waiting. The property has no trailing separator after the scope page sets it and has one otherwise; the doubled separator that gives is harmless in a Windows path. No new WiX extension.

**How it was checked.** The two actions run through the Windows Installer engine against a test build: the path resolves to the folder in both forms (with and without the separator, in a folder whose name has a space); the engine's scripting session refuses to start a program ("not permitted in a restricted engine"), so the launch itself was checked by an interactive install: the user's, per-user, with the box checked, and the application opened. `RepoFilesTests.TheWizardsLaunchStartsTheExeFromTheInstallFolderPropertyNotItsFileRow` holds it (no `FileRef` launch, the property's value, the order on the Finish button); `eng/mutants/deploy-paths.json` D10 (the launch reads the File row again) and D11 (the launch before the path is set) are caught, and the list's 11 mutants all are. Managed suite 438 in all, 437 passed (440 and 439 with the wizard's pictures, below).

#### The MSI installs per-user or per-machine, and the wizard asks which

**What the user asked for.** After the per-machine MSI (the entry below) the user asked for the per-user install as well, so that a user without administrator rights can install without the portable ZIP, and US8.0's "install to a user-selected directory for users without admin privileges" has an installer that meets it. **This supersedes the entry below's "per-machine only".**

**What it does.** One MSI, `Scope="perUserOrMachine"` (it writes `ALLUSERS=2`), with the `WixUI_Advanced` wizard, which asks "for all users" or "only for me". Every registry write is `HKMU` (HKLM for an all-users install, HKCU for a per-user one), the application folder is `APPLICATIONFOLDER` (it replaces `INSTALLFOLDER`), and the defaults are `%ProgramFiles%\tmDataQualityAnalyzer` (64-bit: the wizard's own default is the 32-bit folder, so `SetProperty` rows replace it) and `%LocalAppData%\Programs\tmDataQualityAnalyzer`. The scope switch the MSI would set (`MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1`) is **deleted from the built MSI** by `build_msi.ps1` (through the installer COM object, then checked, with every COM object released and the file reopened before signing: signtool found it held otherwise): left in, a silent install by GPO, SCCM or Intune as SYSTEM would go per-user, into SYSTEM's profile. An elevated silent install is per-machine as before; a non-elevated install by a user who is not an administrator is per-user (Windows Installer's rule); an administrator who has not elevated is sent to per-machine and refused (Error 1925), and passes `MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1` for a per-user install. `ALLUSERS=1`, `MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1` and `APPLICATIONFOLDER=` are the new public switches. The `.ch10` offer, the Start menu entry and the desktop shortcut follow the install's scope (a per-user desktop shortcut is on the user's desktop). The wizard's exit page offers to launch the application.

**Also in this change.** `eng\PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` now includes `ParseError` in `Severity`: a script that does not parse is a ParseError, which the old `Error, Warning` setting did not report, so a missing closing brace in `verify_install.ps1` passed `check_scripts.ps1` and then failed to start in a clean Sandbox, twice (the check now fails on it, which was proved with the bad script). `RepoFilesTests` gains `TheMsiInstallsPerUserOrPerMachineAndEveryRegistryWriteFollowsTheInstall` (scope, wizard, no `HKLM`/`HKCU`/`HKCR` root in a write, the two folder values, the property deletion in the script). `docs/guide.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/cut-release/SKILL.md` and `README.md` describe both modes. **User-owned text not touched:** US8.0's criteria; the note in `docs/guide.md` says what the two modes are.

**How it was checked.** Windows Sandbox, as for the per-machine MSI (staged by hand, the exe, core DLL and MSI signed by the project certificate), with new steps: **8c**, an install with `MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1`, an upgrade and an uninstall run without elevation (a restricted token; first, an administrator who has not elevated and passes no switch is refused with Error 1925 and nothing is installed), then the files in `%LocalAppData%\Programs\tmDataQualityAnalyzer`, nothing in Program Files, the `.ch10` offer and ProgID in `HKCU` only, the user's Start menu, the settings (an edit survives the upgrade and the uninstall), the window opening; and **8d**, `MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1` from an elevated prompt, which must still go to the user's folder. The last run **passed all 119 checks**, the per-machine steps unchanged. It took four runs, and the first three found only faults of the test: (1) a missing closing brace in `verify_install.ps1` (twice: the Sandbox ran nothing; the analyzer's `ParseError` change above is the result); (2) the Installed apps entry of a per-user install is not in `HKCU`: **Windows Installer writes it under `HKLM`** (`ProductRegister`), with the install logged as per-user and the files in the user's folder, so the per-user steps count entries in both hives and take the install's scope from the product's registration in the user's own installer hive (`HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Installer\Products`) and the log's `Deleting ALLUSERS property`; (3) an earlier version of the restricted-token step used `runas /trustlevel`, which gives a filtered administrator, and expected a per-user install without the switch (it is refused, above). **A consequence for a user:** the per-user install's Installed apps entry is machine-wide, so another user of the machine sees it and cannot remove it. The MSI tested was built before a last comment-only edit of the `.wxs`. Managed suite 437 total, 0 failed, 2 skipped (one new case); app suite 948 total, 34 not run, 914 passed, 0 failed (`ShellTests` reads `APPLICATIONFOLDER`), both on the tree rebased onto main (#411); script analyzer clean. Mutation check `eng/mutants/deploy-paths.json`: 9 mutants, 9 caught, none survived (D6 re-anchored to `HKMU`; D7 a Start menu shortcut written to `HKLM`; D8 the build script's property deletion turned into a select; D9 the per-machine folder in the 32-bit Program Files).

**Not done.** The interactive wizard (the Sandbox drives `msiexec` silently); a per-user install by a real standard user with no switch (the Sandbox's account is an administrator, so the per-user steps use `MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1`, once under a restricted token and once elevated; a token restricted by `runas /trustlevel` is a filtered administrator, not a standard user, which an earlier version of the test took it for); and the first MSI release's notes.

#### The installer is a per-machine MSI; the Inno Setup installer is gone

**What the user asked for.** Many users are in defense and aerospace, on workstations that are being locked down and installed silently (Group Policy, SCCM, Intune), so an MSI to deploy. The user chose MSI over MSIX (Group Policy installs only MSI; MSIX fixes its options at build time and puts the install in a versioned, read-only folder, which would also move `settings\` to a writable place), WiX 6.0.2 (the Open Source Maintenance Fee applies to organizations with more than about $10,000 a year in revenue; the project has none), per-machine only (a user without admin rights has the portable ZIP, which is unchanged), no upgrade path from an Inno install (there are few installs), and the removal of the Inno installer once the MSI passed signed.

**What it does.** `deploy/tmDataQualityAnalyzer.wxs`, built by `deploy/build_msi.ps1` (called by `build_package.ps1`), makes `tmDataQualityAnalyzer-vX.Y.Z_setup.msi` from the staged application, in place of the Inno installer. The Inno tasks became features (`FileAssoc`, `Manual`, `DesktopShortcut`, the last off by default) and an administrator's switches are public properties (`ASSOCIATE_CH10=0`, `FULLMANUAL=0`, `DESKTOPSHORTCUT=1`, `INSTALLFOLDER`). The `FileAssoc` feature **offers the application for `.ch10` and never takes the association**: it registers the ProgID and lists it under `.ch10\OpenWithProgids`, and does not write `.ch10`'s default value, because a ProgId with an Extension would, and Windows Installer's uninstall (and the upgrade that removes the older product) deletes every value a package wrote whoever's it has become, which deleted an association another application had taken (found by the Sandbox test, step 8b). Windows therefore asks once which application to use on a machine with no association, instead of opening a `.ch10` file straight in this one; an administrator who wants it the default uses a default-associations file (`DISM /Import-DefaultAppAssociations`). `settings\` is generated into a fragment, one never-overwritten (`NeverOverwrite`), never-removed (`Permanent`) component per file. A major-upgrade rule replaces an older MSI and refuses a downgrade; a launch condition refuses to install beside an Inno install (its uninstall key) and says to uninstall that first. WiX is a repo-local dotnet tool (`dotnet-tools.json`, version pinned); its UI extension is fetched into the gitignored `.wix\` cache on first use. A silent uninstall with the application running closes it (Windows Installer's Restart Manager) rather than hanging on it.

**What was removed or changed with it.** `deploy/tmDataQualityAnalyzer.iss`, the Inno step of `build_package.ps1` (Inno Setup 6 is no longer needed to build) and its upgrade-from-v2.x test. `deploy/sandbox/verify_install.ps1` is now the MSI's clean-machine test, driven silently (the wizard is not exercised), and keeps what the Inno test checked: Smart App Control on, an unsigned control blocked, the application launched on the PRN sample, the native core loaded, Code Integrity's events and the portable ZIP. `run_sandbox_test.ps1` builds a newer, unsigned MSI for the upgrade, and notices a test that has stopped (no progress for 10 minutes) instead of waiting out its timeout. `RepoFilesTests`' `*.iss` checks now hold the MSI source: every `$(RepoRoot)\...` path it names exists and every variable it uses is one `build_msi.ps1` defines; the full-manual test in `ShellTests` reads the MSI source. `eng/mutants/deploy-paths.json` is re-anchored (D1-D3 on the MSI source and script, D4 as it was, D5 new). `docs/guide.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `README.md` and the `cut-release` skill describe the MSI. **User-owned text not touched:** US8.0's criteria, of which "the installer can install to a user-selected directory for users without admin privileges" is not met by a per-machine MSI (the portable ZIP is that user's) and another names Inno's `onlyifdoesntexist` and `uninsneveruninstall`; the note in `docs/guide.md` leaves them for the user to reword.

**How it was checked.** Windows Sandbox, Windows 11 Enterprise, the real staged application (staged by hand: the release gate refuses while this section exists), the exe, the core DLL and the release MSI signed by the project certificate. The runs found three defects: (1) the Windows-version launch condition (`VersionNT64 AND WindowsBuild >= 17763`) refused the install on Windows 11, because Windows Installer reports a package that does not claim newer Windows as Windows 8.1 (VersionNT 603, build 9600); it now reads the real build from the registry and refuses only when it is known and too low. (2) The verifier's Installed apps list returned one object, not an array, so `.Count` was empty. (3) The verifier loaded `tmdq_core.dll` into its own process and kept it, so the uninstall's Restart Manager shut the verifier down (the uninstall itself succeeded) and the runner waited out its timeout for results never written; the verifier now frees the DLL and the runner reads the progress file. The last run, with default arguments (about 20 minutes), **passed every check**: Smart App Control on and the unsigned exe blocked; the refusal beside a real v2.14.2 Inno install (exit 1603 and the message); a fresh install of every file, one Installed apps entry at the MSI's version, `.ch10` opening the installed exe, the Start menu entry, no desktop shortcut, every PE file signed; an upgrade to a newer MSI that keeps an edited settings file; the older MSI over the newer refused; the installed application opening its window and processing the PRN sample, and `tmdq_core.dll` loading; an uninstall that clears the association and leaves the settings, the edit included; the three switches; the portable ZIP opening its window and processing the sample; and Code Integrity blocking only the unsigned control. After main was merged in (#397-#403) the baselines are managed suite 435 total, 0 failed, 2 skipped (the Debug-core case needs a Debug core, plus the child-process probe) and app suite 940 total, 34 not run, **906 passed**, both as main's, plus the one new managed case (436 total); the script analyzer is clean. The merge also added two steps to the Sandbox test for what #397 fixed in the Inno script (an upgrade that declines the association must leave no dead `.ch10` entry, and an association another application took must be left alone by an uninstall). The first found a real difference: the MSI's uninstall deleted the association another application had taken (the Inno installer's own uninstall did the same, with `uninsdeletevalue`, but #397's intent was to leave it). The MSI now offers the application under `OpenWithProgids` rather than taking the default (above); `RepoFilesTests.TheMsiOffersTheApplicationForCh10AndNeverWritesTheDefaultAnotherApplicationMayHold` and mutant D6 hold it, and the Sandbox run after the change **passed every check**, both steps included. Mutation check `eng/mutants/deploy-paths.json`: 6 mutants, 6 caught, none survived (D1-D5 by the path-and-variable test, D6, the MSI taking `.ch10`'s default, by the association test).

**Not done.** The full manual (the Manual feature shipped the base manual in these runs, because a fresh worktree has no rendered figures; a release renders the real one); the interactive wizard (the Sandbox drives `msiexec` silently); and the first MSI release's notes, which must tell anyone with the old setup-based install to uninstall it first (Settings, Apps). **One thing to watch:** in the Sandbox every `msiexec /i` of the 50 MB MSI, signed or not, spent about two minutes in "verifying the package against software restriction policy" before it started (an uninstall took one second). The same signed MSI's administrative extract (`msiexec /a`) on the development machine verified the package in under a second and finished in 2 s, so the delay belongs to the Sandbox (its disk or its scanning), not to the package; it is not measured on a locked-down workstation.

#### The mutation check's verdicts on the managed suite are the real tests' again, and Pillow is 13.0.0

**What was wrong.** `eng\mutate.ps1` applies a mutant by replacing its `old` text, and the managed suite's anchor guard (`RepoFilesTests.EveryKeptMutantStillNamesTextThatIsInItsFileExactlyOnce`) fails when a kept mutant's `old` text is not in its file exactly once - which is true of every applied mutant. So any managed-suite mutant run without a `-class` or `-method` filter that leaves `RepoFilesTests` out was CAUGHT by that guard, whatever the tests it was meant for did: a survivor could not be seen. Two lists run unfiltered (`imported-stream-orders.json`, `series-index-count.json`), and the lists filtered to `RepoFilesTests` itself ran the guard too.

**What it does now.** `mutate.ps1` sets `TMDQ_MUTATING=1` for the suite it runs, and the anchor guard skips while it is set (`Assert.SkipWhen`), so a verdict names the test that saw the mutant. A normal run of the suite is unchanged: the guard runs and the managed baseline does not move. The script's header and `docs/guide.md`'s test catalog say so. Separately, Dependabot's #398 moved `eng/requirements.txt` from Pillow 12.1.1 to 13.0.0 (used only by `eng\gen_app_icon.py`, run when the icon's artwork changes, outside CI and the app; not run under 13 here; Pillow 13 drops Python 3.10, and this machine runs 3.14).

**How it was checked.** Every managed-suite list in `eng/mutants` (11 lists, 81 mutants) run again with the guard skipped: 75 caught, each by a test the list is about, and 6 survived, every one already recorded as an expected survivor (`arena-repeats.json` R9, `safe-handles.json` H7 and H20-H23), so no verdict changed. The guard still fails a moved anchor in an ordinary run, and skips with the variable set. Managed suite 435 in all, 0 failed (unchanged).

#### The core refuses a packet whose lengths it cannot trust, keeps exceptions inside its threads, and asks for a Data Rate the TMATS lacks

**What was wrong.** A read-only review of the native core found, each confirmed in the code: (1) a packet header's data length (`ulDataLen`) was trusted. irig106 reads the packet length's worth of bytes and compares the two lengths nowhere; the run then copied `ulDataLen - 4` bytes of each PCM packet out of a buffer that holds the packet (a heap over-read on a corrupt or crafted `.ch10`, a crash at four billion), and the TMATS decoder read `ulDataLen - 4` bytes of text (under 4, four billion). (2) No exception boundary on a run's own threads: anything thrown on a stream's thread, the reader's or the calibration extractor's (a `std::bad_alloc` on a long run, the C ABI allocating a result) called `std::terminate` and took the host application with it. (3) irig106's attribute setup was not checked: a P record with no bit rate (P-x\D2) gave a bit period of 1e7 / 0, and every stream failed later with "the recording's time jumps ahead by inf s ... the time channel looks corrupt", blaming the wrong channel; a data source with no P record left the word length 0, so every receiver word read 0, silently. (4) The time ticks walked the clock by adding the step to it, and the round ticks counted their indices by adding one: with an origin far from zero (an imported CSV sets one) or a range a few units of the last place wide, the sum stopped changing and the loop never ended. (5) Smaller: the CSV import reserved at least 100 rows a column (a header of 100 000 columns reserved 160 MB up front); file-sourced ints were multiplied in int (a CSV stamp's days times 86400 and hours times 3600, a legacy frame-sync file's words times 16 - 268 435 460 words wrapped to a plausible 64 bits -, `FrameSetup::wordsInMinorFrame`'s bits + 15, the default receiver map's receivers times channels, whose wrap could pass its check and build billions of parameters); the calibration request took a frame shorter than the main run accepts; `Chapter10Reader` closed its handle on every return but not on a throw; four includes were unused; and the C header's revision list left `tmdq_chart_round_ticks` out of revision 4.

**What it does now.** (1) `ch10setup::readPacketData` refuses, before reading, a header whose packet is shorter than its own header, whose data length is past the bytes that follow the header (`bodyLength`, the secondary header counted), or under the type's channel-specific word (4 bytes, for TMATS and PCM): `PacketRead::BadLength`. The run stops with "A packet on channel N claims X bytes of data but carries Y: the recording is corrupt; aborting parsing." (as a read error stops it: the packets before are delivered, every stream gets its end marker); both readers refuse such a TMATS packet with `Failure::TmatsLength`, "The TMATS packet's data length does not fit the packet: the recording is corrupt.". (2) `containExceptions` (`exceptionboundary.h`, new) runs each thread body: a stream that throws is reported ("Stream N (label) stopped on an internal error (...); its result was dropped."), its queue closed so the others finish and deliver; a reader that throws closes every queue and drops every result not yet delivered (no stream saw the whole recording); either way the run ends with `processingFinished(false)`, and a sink that throws at the end is dropped. A `start()` that throws on the caller's thread (a path the code page cannot spell, memory, a thread that will not start) gives back what it built and its claim: `PipelineRunner::start` returns false with "The run could not start: ...", and `CalibrationExtractor::start` reports "Calibration extraction could not start: ..." then the end. Both used to keep `m_running` set, so that object refused every later start. The extractor's reader and driver threads are held the same way: the first throw is the extraction's reason, its results are cleared. The ABI's result allocation (`abi_events.h`) is owned by a `unique_ptr` and left to reach the stream's boundary, so it fails the run rather than being swallowed as a callback's failure is. (3) `prepare()` refuses a stream whose bit period is not finite and positive: "Channel N's TMATS gives no bit rate (P-x\D2): enter the stream's Data Rate."; with the Data Rate given the stream runs, and its word length is the 16 bits prepare hands the library, not read back from it. (4) Both tick functions count by index with a hard bound: the time ticks fall back to the even division when the clock cannot resolve the step (a step at least the span over n - 1 bounds the count at n + 2), the round ticks when an index passes 2^52; the ticks are bit for bit what they were everywhere else (the oracle case still compares them). (5) The CSV import reserves the file-size estimate only; the int products are formed wide (the CSV's rows and rules are unchanged, only a time that wrapped no longer does); `buildCalibrationRequest` refuses Bits/Frame below 64 with `buildStreamJob`'s words; `Chapter10Reader` keeps `m_file_open`, and a handle a throwing load left open is closed by the next load and by the destructor, under the setup lock; the unused includes are gone; the header's revision 4 names `tmdq_chart_round_ticks`. Left as they are: the linear lookups in `TomlDocument` (sections and keys), the phased-array unit search and `tmdq_file_open`'s rate per channel - each is over a few dozen entries at most (words of one frame, a log's units, a recording's channels), and an index would be more code than the time it saves.

**How it was checked.** New native cases: `Ch10Setup` (a body is what follows the header; a data length that does not fit, row by row; a TMATS packet whose data length was rewritten with its header checksum), `Ch10PacketReader` (a corrupt PCM data length stops the read with the reason; a corrupt TMATS length refused by both readers; no bit rate and no P record, refused, then run with the Data Rate), `PipelineRunner` (a stream that throws, a result that cannot be delivered, a read that throws at its start and part-way, a sink that throws at the end, a start that throws), `CalibrationExtractor` (a throw on the reader, the worker or step detection; a read that throws part-way; a sink that throws at the end; a start that throws), `ExceptionBoundary` (new file), `ChartGeometry` (ticks far from zero), `csvseries` (days and hours far apart; a wide file's reservation), `FrameSetup`, `framesyncfile` (the wide products), `CalibrationRequest` (a short frame refused; the oracle's one departure), `Chapter10Reader` (every load gives its handle back, and a destroyed reader does not close a slot it no longer owns). The part-way cases wait on what the threads do, never on time: the worker is parked on its first log line until packets wait in its queue (`PacketQueue::size`, new), then the reader is asked to report its progress at its next packet (`Ch10PacketReader::requestProgress`, new: one relaxed load per packet) instead of after its 100 ms throttle, and that report throws. The start cases use a file name with an unpaired surrogate, which `path.string()` cannot convert. The crafted recordings are `step_cal` with one header's data length and checksum rewritten (`setPacketDataLength`, `test_support.h`). Without the fixes the exception cases end the test executable and the tick case hangs. Mutation check `eng/mutants/native-robustness.json`: 43 mutants, 41 caught, 2 survived as recorded equivalents (G2: the time ticks' count bound, which the clock-resolution check before it never lets end the loop - kept as defence in depth; H3: `Chapter10Reader`'s destructor close, reached only when a load throws part-way, which no test can provoke). Four first compiled with a warning (an unused parameter or local) and were rewritten; X5 (results left after step detection threw) survived at first because the throw came on the first channel, before any result: the case now throws on the third. `reader-setup.json`'s S16 re-anchored (its text was followed by the new `BadLength` case) and run again: caught. Native suite **575 test cases** passed, 1 skipped (551 before), in Release and Debug; managed 420 passed; app 884 passed, 34 not run.

#### Two legends, the SNR colours from the palette's other end, and tighter dots

**What the user asked for.** Three changes to how a plot reads, one after the other: (1) "flip the order of the colors for SNR and FrameSync", so that channel 1 of a Frame Sync plot and receiver 1 of an SNR plot are not the same colour; (2) the dotted lines "a little bit tighter", the space between the dots smaller (of four candidates rendered on both themes, the user chose a gap as long as the dot); (3) one legend was "a little bit overwhelming" and did not say which entry was which: two legends, one titled **Framesync Series** and one **SNR Series**, the Framesync one at the top left and the SNR one at the top right, with the user story text to match (the user checked it before it was committed).

**What it does now.** (1) `PlotColors.SnrHue` takes the 15 hues from the last back to the first (receiver 1 is the 15th hue, dark green; the 16th stream is the 15th hue again), where Frame Sync Lock still takes them from the first (`StreamHues[idx % 15]`), so stream 1 of the two metrics is two colours and no stream number but the 8th, the middle hue, is one colour in both; a lock stream k and an SNR stream 16 - k do share a hue, which a plot of fewer than eight of each never shows. The tints of a receiver's L and R, the combined channel's strength and the 16th-stream cycle are as they were. (2) `PlotChart.SeriesDots` is `{ 1, 1 }` (a dot, then a gap as long, in multiples of the line's width; it was `{ 1, 2 }`), which the legend's dotted swatches follow, as they follow the line. The grid's and the crosshair's dashes are not changed. (3) `PlotView` holds two `PlotLegend`s, `FrameSyncLegend` (title "Framesync Series", `Side="Left"`) and `SnrLegend` ("SNR Series", `Side="Right"`); `PlotViewModel.LegendEntries` marks an entry `IsSnr` and the view lists the Receiver SNR series in the SNR legend and the rest (Frame Sync Lock, or the missed frames) in the Framesync one. Each is a box of its own: a title that does not scroll, its rows, its own cap (60 % of the chart's height, 45 % of its width) and scroll bar, its own drag, and it is not drawn when it has no row. Both start level at the top of the plot area (`PlotChart.LegendTop`: the area's top and a margin, so the Framesync legend does not cover the View Mode and Reset view chips in the corner above it), the Framesync one a margin inside the plot area's left edge (`LegendLeftEdge`, clear of the left axis's labels) and the SNR one a margin short of its right edge (`LegendRightEdge`, which is now always the plot area's: a plot with SNR on it always has the right axis, so the branch for none is gone); a legend dragged by the user stays where it was put. **Show Legend** (and `L`) hides or shows both together, and `PlotImageExport` draws both at their places (one `DrawLegendAsync` for each). The View Mode chip's corner and the title are as they were. The SNR legend's top moves down by the height of the plot's title and its gap (about 35 px at the default size): both legends start at the plot area, not above it.

**Reaches.** `PlotColors`, `PlotChart` (`SeriesDots`, the legend anchors), `PlotLegend` (a title, a `Side`, an anchor and a top), `PlotView.axaml` and its code-behind, `PlotImageExport`, `PlotViewModel.LegendEntry`; `docs/guide.md` (US4.0, the export stories and US10.0's criteria on the legend and the colours, the architecture paragraph and the test catalog), the README, the manual's text and the captions `eng/embed_manual_images.py` writes, and every figure that shows a legend or an SNR series, re-rendered.

**How it was checked.** `PlotTests` (the SNR hues from the last end, over 31 streams and the cycle; the dotted pixel count of the new pattern: about two thirds of a plain line's, where the old pattern is outside the range) and `ChartViewTests` (each legend's title, corner, margins and rows; the two together, side by side and level; an empty one not drawn; Show Legend for both; the cap and scroll bar of the SNR legend and the width cap of the Framesync one; the right axis's and the left axis's labels left clear; the chips left clear; each following its corner on a resize and a dragged one staying), `ExportImportTests` (an image holds each legend at its place, with only its own metric's swatch), `ShellTests` (both legends follow the theme). Mutation checks: `series-colours.json` 16 mutants, 16 caught (C6 and C11 re-anchored, C14 and C15 for the order, C16 for the dots); `plot-zoom-and-legend.json` gains G1-G13 (a legend listing the other's series, no entry marked SNR, a legend above the plot area or over an axis's labels, the corners swapped, the title not counted in the height, an export leaving a legend out, Show Legend not hiding both, a resize not followed, a title spelled otherwise), 13 caught; G4 and G5 first failed to compile (the analyzer's CA1822: a member that ignores its argument) and were rewritten to use it. App suite **944 in all, 910 passed**, 34 not run (940 and 906 before: four new cases).

#### Extract Calibration lets the operator choose the channels of the calibration recording

**What the user asked for.** A calibration recording is often a different file from the one the stream was set up on, and its step cals can be recorded on another channel. The dialog read the stream's PCM channel and Configure Streams' time channel from the calibration recording, so a recording whose step cals were on another channel failed with the core's "no such channel", with no way to say which one to use.

**What it does now.** Once a calibration recording is chosen, `ExtractCalibrationViewModel.LoadCalibrationAsync` lists its channels first (`RecordingChannels.Read`, the core's TMATS-only listing, off the UI thread) and the dialog shows **PCM Channel** and **Time Channel** under the recording's status line, as `<id> - <name>` like Configure Streams' time channel list. They start on the stream's own channels when the recording has them; a recording with no channel by that number starts on its first PCM channel and its default time channel, and a line under the lists says so (`ChannelNote`). Choosing another extracts again (`CalPcmIndex`, `CalTimeIndex`); `ToRequest` carries the selected ids to the core, which already took them, so no ABI change. A recording that will not open is a cross that names the file (it used to be the core's bare "Error opening data file.") and clears the lists. The choice belongs to the dialog alone, like the calibration profiles: it is not kept in the stream's setup or a template, and the next recording starts over on the stream's channels. The lists share the dialog's label column in one row (`Grid.IsSharedSizeScope`), so with no recording chosen the dialog is as tall as before.

**Reaches.** `Models/Processing/RecordingChannels.cs` (new), `ExtractCalibrationViewModel`, `ExtractCalibrationWindow.axaml`, `docs/guide.md` (the dialog's paragraph and the test catalog), `docs/manual/walkthroughs.html` (a paragraph) and the two figures that show the dialog (`walk-cal-01`, `walk-cal-03`), re-rendered. The user story's criteria (US5.3) were not touched by this change: they are the user's, and the criterion for this was worded and added afterwards (#388).

**How it was checked.** Seven new cases in `CalibrationChannelTests` (a stand-in for the core's listing and a runner that records its requests; one case runs the real core, on a stream whose channel the recording lacks; one the window), and two existing cases in `CalibrationDialogTests` moved with the change (the time channel reaches the request only when the recording has it; a file that is not a recording names itself). Mutation check `eng/mutants/calibration-channel.json`: 15 mutants, 15 caught, none survived (the three window ones run again after the layout moved). App suite 877 in all, 34 not run, 0 failed: **843 passed** (836 before).

#### The project's settings let the session turn on Auto-fix for a pull request

**What the user asked for.** To be able to have CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments on a pull request handed back to the session that opened it, without each request being refused. The app's `set_monitor` call, which switches that on for one PR, was denied by the permission check every time it was tried (#364-#366 and #407); the denial said a permission rule for it would allow it.

**What it does now.** `.claude/settings.json` has a `permissions.allow` list holding `mcp__ccd_pr__set_monitor`, beside the existing `deny` rules for `third_party/irig106`. There is no global setting for Auto-fix: it is switched on for one PR at a time, so the session makes the call right after opening each PR. The rule lets the call through; whether the app's separate safety check still asks for approval is not something the file controls. Auto-fix wakes the session on failures, conflicts and comments and never merges: a merge still waits for the user's word.

**How it was checked.** The file parses as JSON and keeps both `deny` rules. No test reads it. No code or baseline changed.

#### Imports stack: an exported CSV is added to the plot as an antenna's log is, and a refused file takes nothing away

**What the user asked for.** Importing two files kicked out the first ("it's not stacking imports like it used to. This is what I want."). The case was an antenna's log imported first and an exported CSV second: the log is added to what the plot shows (US10.0), but an exported CSV replaced everything (US6.3), so the second import cleared the first. Every import now stacks. The user checked the story wording before it was committed.

**What it does now.** `MainWindowViewModel.ImportCsvAsync` adds the file whenever the plot holds anything (`joins = Plot.HasData`) and passes `add: true` to `PlotViewModel.LoadCsv` / `LoadCsvAsync` (a new optional parameter; the antenna's log still always joins, so a direct `LoadCsv` of one behaves as it did). An empty plot is where an import starts: it shows the file and the title is the file's name. An added file is named for itself in Plot File and Remove File, told apart from another of the same name (`UniqueSourceLabel`: "name (2)"; the antenna's log now is too), placed by its clock time with the overlap warning and the shift the log already had, and leaves the plot's title and its colours. A file that holds several recordings (an export of a batch, columns qualified `S<n>| `) is added as several: `ShowCsv` gives each of the file's source numbers the next free one on the plot (`sourceMap`, a new optional parameter of `PlotCsv.Series`), named "file, Source n" when there is more than one, so none meets a recording already there. A file the parser refuses is now an error and nothing more: the plot was cleared before the file was read when it replaced, and is not cleared now (as a refused antenna log never cleared it).

**Reaches.** `MainWindowViewModel`, `PlotViewModel` (`LoadCsv`, `LoadCsvAsync`, `ShowCsv`), `PlotCsv.Series`; `docs/guide.md` (US6.3 gains a criterion, US10.0's sentence on a telemetry CSV (now "Every import is added the same way"), the architecture paragraph and the test catalog), the README, the manual's two paragraphs on importing. No ABI or core change.

**How it was checked.** Three cases changed with the rule: an exported CSV after an antenna's log (the user's order) now keeps both (`ACsvOfTheApplicationsOwnJoinsAnAntennasLogAndBothStay`), an exported CSV after a run keeps the run (`AnImportedCsvJoinsWhatTheRunShowedAndTheRunStays`), and a refused file leaves the plot as it was (`ACsvThatIsNotAnExportIsAnErrorAndLeavesThePlotAsItWas`). Two are new: two exports stack, each named for its file, and the same file twice is named apart (`TwoExportedCsvsStackEachNamedForItsFileAndTheFirstIsNotReplaced`), and a batch's export with recordings numbered 3 and 5 is added to a plot with one recording as 1 and 2, named "batch, Source 3" and "batch, Source 5" (`AnExportOfSeveralRecordingsAddedToAPlotTakesTheNextFreeSourcesAndKeepsWhatWasThere`). Mutation check `eng/mutants/antenna-overlay.json`: 20 mutants, 20 caught (O1, O3, O10 and O14 re-anchored on the new text; O15-O20 are new: the file's numbers kept, a repeated name not told apart, the plot not asked to add, the request ignored, the names of a batch's recordings, the numbering). App suite **946 in all, 912 passed**, 34 not run (944 and 910 before).

#### Opening a recording stacks like an import, Add Recording goes, and Clear Plot is how a plot is emptied

**What the user asked for.** "Open and stack accordingly": with imports stacking (the entry above), File > Open was the one way left to wipe a plot by accident, and Add Recording and Open were one job under two entries. Open now adds the recording beside what is shown, the Add Recording entry is gone, and a **Clear Plot** entry (the user's addition) is the deliberate way to start again. The user approved the story wording and chose to add Clear Plot in this change.

**What it does now.** `MainWindowViewModel.LoadAsync(path)` keeps whatever the plot holds (`keep = Plot.HasData`; the `add` parameter, `AddRecordingCommand`, `AddRecordingAsync` and the menu entry are gone): the recording is appended to `Sources`, numbered `Plot.NextSourceId`, named apart from the plot's others (`UniqueSourceLabel`), its series coloured without recolouring what is shown, the plot's title left alone, and a recording that fails to open or is cancelled changes nothing (it used to take the earlier run off the plot). The first recording into an empty plot starts one and titles it; the log says "Adding" for the others and "Opening" for that one. A drop and a Recent Files entry go through the same method. `ClearProcessedRun`, which removed the recordings processed before and kept the imports, could only be reached with an empty plot and is deleted (`ClearRun` is what an empty plot gets). A batch (Apply Template) still clears everything first. **Clear Plot...** (`PlotCommands.ClearPlotAsync`, the plot's right-click menu under Remove File...) asks once, as Remove File does but with nothing chosen for the operator to press Enter on ("Everything on the plot", OK waits for it), then `PlotViewModel.RemoveSources` takes every recording: the plot goes back to a new one (title, view, zoom history), `SourceRemoved` empties `Sources`, nothing on disk changes. It is unavailable with nothing on the plot. The Open menu entry says in its tooltip that it adds beside what is there.

**Reaches.** `MainWindowViewModel`, `PlotCommands`, `PlotViewModel` (a comment), `MainWindow.axaml` (the File menu), `PlotView.axaml` (the right-click menu); `docs/guide.md` (US1.0 gains a criterion, the context menu's and the File menu's criteria, US10.0's sentence on Open, the architecture paragraph and the test catalog), the README, the manual's text and the figures that show the menus, re-rendered.

**How it was checked.** `AddRecordingTests` became `OpenStacksTests` (the same cases through Open, an empty plot where one starts, the same recording opened again named apart, a failed or cancelled open and a cancelled run changing nothing, the warning naming the recording just opened); seven cases that assumed Open replaced what was processed before were rewritten for the new rule (`ImportedDataKeptTests` x4, `TemplateBatchTests`, `ProcessingTests`, `OpenToChartTests`), and the File menu's and the right-click menu's lists changed. Three new cases in `RemoveFileTests` for Clear Plot (asks once with nothing chosen and on yes empties the plot with its title, cancel changes nothing and one file is asked about in the singular, unavailable without data). Mutation checks: `processing-flow.json` re-anchored on the new text (A1, A2, A11-A13, the list's tests now `OpenStacksTests`) and two mutants of the deleted `ClearProcessedRun` removed: 26 of 26 caught; `plot-sources.json` R10 and R11 re-anchored (the label text now appears in two methods) and CP1-CP5 new (Clear Plot answering Cancel, starting chosen, removing one file, offered with nothing, the menu item bound to Remove File): 43 of 43 caught. App suite **949 in all, 915 passed**, 34 not run (946 and 912 before).

#### An imported CSV is recognised from the file: the "what kind of file is it?" question is gone

**What the user asked for.** "The two formats are so different. Can't we auto-detect which CSV we're importing?" When US10.0 was built the user chose a question over detection from the header; seeing what detection meant, they chose it, and asked for the question's text to come out of the user stories.

**What it does now.** `PlotCsv.Parse(path)` reads the file as this application's export first and then as an AV phased array antenna's log, and returns the data with what it turned out to be (`CsvKind`); each core reader refuses the other's file at its first line (`Time (DOY:HH:MM:SS.mmm)` against `Time, Name, Polarity`), so a log costs the export reader one line and there is no new ABI. `PlotViewModel.LoadCsv` / `LoadCsvAsync` lose their `kind` parameter and `MainWindowViewModel.ImportCsvAsync` its `kind` and the question; `ICsvKindDialog`, `WindowCsvKindDialog`, `MainWindowServices.CsvKinds` and `CsvKinds` (the dialog's list and titles) are deleted, and `CsvKind` stays as what the file was. A file of neither layout is one error naming both (`NotARecognizedCsv` replaces the two per-kind messages), and the plot is left as it was. #### Remove File: a recording, a batch file or an imported CSV can be taken out of the plot, and the others kept

**What the user asked for.** A way to remove the data series that are no longer of interest while keeping the ones that are. Customize View only hides a series, and Export Data writes every series, shown or hidden (US criterion in the export story). **What it does.** The plot's right-click menu has **Remove File...**, under Plot File. What is drawn is fitted again only when it changed: with the recording that was shown alone removed (every one is overlaid again) or with all of them overlaid (the window spans those left); with another one shown alone, the view the operator zoomed is left. Removing the only recording leaves the plot as a new one starts (`Clear`). `IPlotPrompts` has a new `ChooseAsync` (the plot's list question, a `ChoiceWindow`), and the `NoPlotPrompts`, `WindowPlotPrompts` and the tests' `FakePrompts` implement it.
