#### The scan skips through a frame it is locked on, 4.1x faster again, with the same answers

The step before this one made each bit cheaper; this one stops looking at most bits. In lock, nothing the state machine
does between a frame's boundary and the bit before the next one depends on more than counting: an off-phase sync match is
ignored (the match test is not acted on), no lock decision falls there, and the frame's words are the register's contents
at known bit counts. So `scanBits` now takes those bits in one step, from the bits themselves:

- **What a skip does.** From a position in lock (`sync_count >= min_syncs`, at least 64 bits into the packet so the
  register can be read from the data) it takes up to the bit before the frame's boundary, or the run's end if that is
  nearer, and applies what the bits would have done: the lock and total bit counts, the frame position, the register
  (`bitsBefore`: the 64 bits ending there), each word that completes (the register at its last bit, stored as before), and
  the word count and `save_data` state. The boundary bit and what follows still go through the one-at-a-time loop, so a
  frame that ends in a sync, a lost one or a rollover is handled by the code that always handled it. A skip is not taken
  for fewer than 16 bits, nor for a sync mask wider than 57 bits (see below), nor in the odd state where the frame
  has all its words but is still collecting.
- **Syncs found are still counted exactly.** Every sync match is counted in `total_syncs_found`, which the run's report
  prints, so a skipped stretch cannot just be jumped: `countSyncMatches` tests the register at all eight bit positions of
  each byte at once. That needs the whole match window in the 64-bit register with the byte beside it, hence the 57-bit
  limit; a longer mask takes the bit-at-a-time path, as before.
- **Measured** (Release core, pinned to the performance cores, `eng\run_throughput_bench.ps1`; before -> after, and the
  two steps together against v3.1.0): the 1 Mbps channel 335 -> 87 ms, 5 Mbps 1712 -> 398 and 1711 -> 604, 20 Mbps
  6654 -> 1617 ms (4.1x; 7.2x against 11643); the four streams together 6549 -> 1650 ms (4.0x; 6.9x against 11460). The two
  5 Mbps channels no longer take the same time (398 and 604 ms: a PRN-11 and a PRN-15 stream); the cause was not
  investigated.
- **Same answers, checked three ways.** The 60 short pinned scenarios of the last step still reproduce. A second pinned set,
  `FrameProcessor: the scan's output on long synthetic streams is what it was`, runs 62 long ones (20 to 120 thousand bits,
  frames of up to 2300 bits, words of 3 to 32 bits, syncs of 2 to 60 bits, packets of up to 9000 bits, the same noise, decoys
  and gaps, every word of the frame mapped to a channel): the scenarios stay in lock across many frames, which the short
  ones barely do, a skip starts mid-word whenever a window ends mid-frame, and a quarter of the frames carry a sync-like
  stretch inside their words (a long sync never matches by chance, so without them the count of matches would be only the
  frames'). Its hashes were printed from the scan without the skip (v3.1.0 plus the last step), and the new scan
  reproduced all 62. The 34-run soak is byte for byte v2.14.2's exports. The managed and app suites pass.
- **Mutants** in `eng\mutants\scan-skip.json`: 15, all caught. The first run left two alive, and both were gaps in the
  scenarios rather than in the code: a 58-bit sync (the limit of the byte-wise count) never matched inside a frame, and
  only the first three words of a frame were read, so a word stored wrongly later in it showed nowhere. The long
  scenarios now plant syncs in frames, give a long sync its top bit, and read every word; the pins were taken again from
  the scan without the skip.
- **A kept list moved.** `scan-runs.json` S12 (the bit order in a byte) named text that two places now had; the read of a
  bit is one helper, `bitAt`, so it is still said once.
- **Not done.** Derandomizing a word at a time (RNRZ-L only) and the unlocked path (acquisition, a stream with no lock) are
  as they were: a stream that never locks is still scanned at the last step's speed.
  Baseline: native 526 -> 527.

#### The frame-sync scan is 1.75x faster, with the same answers

The scan is the limit on a big recording: one bit per pass, one core per stream, so a stream's time is its bit count
(a performance review measured about 4 ns a bit; the 20 Mbps channel of the 640 MB PRN recording took 11.6 s). Two
things made each pass dearer than the state machine needs. Every bit was timed and asked whether it closed a window,
and the machine's registers lived in `ScanState`, a memory location the compiler must assume the frame-word store can
change, so each bit loaded and stored them all.

- **Runs, not bits.** `process()` scans a packet in runs of bits that cannot close a window. A window closes when a bit's
  time passes its end, and time does not decrease along a packet, so `firstBitPastWindow` finds the first bit that does
  once per window, by doubling a step and halving back, asking the very time function the per-bit check used. It
  searches rather than computes: an estimate by division was tried first and was exact so often that the corrections
  around it could not be tested (four mutants survived, below), and a search needs none. A bit exactly at a window's end
  is still in it, as before. Abort is checked every 64 Ki bits as before.
- **Registers in locals.** `scanBit` (one bit through the state machine) is now `scanBits` (a run of them): the machine
  runs on copies of its registers and writes them back at the run's end. The rare events (a sync match, a frame) still
  write `ScanState` directly.
- **Measured** (Release core, pinned to the performance cores, `eng\run_throughput_bench.ps1`; before -> after):
  the 1 Mbps channel 592 -> 335 ms, 5 Mbps 2959 -> 1712 and 2904 -> 1711, 20 Mbps 11643 -> 6654 ms (1.75x); the
  four streams together 11460 -> 6549 ms. About 2.3 ns a bit now. Not a change of result: below.

  pins 60 random scenarios (frame geometry, noise, flipped bits, decoy syncs, odd packet lengths, gaps and time steps back,
  both clocks, windows that are a whole number of bit periods so that a bit lands on a window's end to the last digit),
  each folded to one hash of every series value to the last bit and the run's counts. The hashes were taken from the
  per-bit scan before it was changed, and the new scan reproduced all 60. The 34-run soak (`eng\run_soak.ps1`) exports
  every CSV byte for byte what v2.14.2 exported. The managed (415 total, 0 failed) and app (726 passed) suites pass.
- **Mutants** in `eng\mutants\scan-runs.json`: 10 caught, 2 equivalent. The two that survive (`>=` for `>` in the search)
  can only end a run a bit early, which splits a stretch and changes nothing: the next run starts on that bit, closes
  nothing, and carries on; a run that ends late is what changes a result, and the mutants that make it end late (a skipped
  bit, a probe past the packet) are caught. The first version of the list had four survivors in the estimate's correction
  loops, which is why the estimate was replaced. One kept list, `off-phase-sync-word.json`, was re-anchored: its
  text moved right by one level and `s.` became a local; the other lists on this file still match.
- **Not done.** The abort check inside a long packet has no test (it needs a thread to request it mid-scan, and a sleep
  cannot place it); it is kept as it was. The next step, skipping ahead while locked (a word at a time between syncs),
  is larger and needs the soak; it is not started.
  Baseline: native 525 -> 526.

#### The package refuses a Debug core

The release script builds the core in Release and stages `out\Release\tmdq_core.dll`, so a Debug core cannot reach the
package as the script stands. But nothing *checked* that. `build_core_dll.ps1`'s import allow-list admits the debug runtime
(`VCRUNTIME140D`, `MSVCP140D`, `ucrtbased`), so a Debug DLL passes it; and the step that copies the C++ runtime beside the
DLL would stop on one, but with a message about a file missing from the redist folder, not about the build. A Debug core
is unoptimised (the full PRN recording's first stream took about 14 s against 4.35 s, PR #264), and nothing about it looks
wrong until someone times it.

- **`eng\check_release_core.ps1`.** Reads the DLL's import list (`dumpbin /dependents`, loading the MSVC environment itself
  as the build scripts do) and refuses the debug runtime in any case: `VCRUNTIME140D`, `VCRUNTIME140_1D`, `MSVCP140D`,
  `CONCRT140D`, `VCOMP140D`, `ucrtbased`. It names what it found and says to build in Release. A DLL that lists no imports,
  or no DLL at all, is a failure, not a pass. `-Imports` takes the list in place of a DLL, for the tests.
- **Where it runs.** `deploy\build_package.ps1` checks the core straight after building it, so a mistake costs seconds and
  not the packaging run, and again on the copy it stages to ship; either refusal stops the script.
- **Tried by hand first, and it found a bug in itself:** every list reported "1 imports checked" and the empty list and the
  Debug core both passed. PowerShell variables ignore case, so the local `$imports` was the typed `[string]$Imports`
  parameter, and an array assigned to it collapses to one string. Renamed, with a comment saying why.
- **Checked.** New `ReleaseCoreGuardTests` (16 cases, each running the real script): a real Release core's import list passes;
  the numbered release runtimes (`VCRUNTIME140_1`, `MSVCP140_2`) are not mistaken for debug ones; each debug name is refused in
  any case and named; a debug import is found first, last and alone; no imports and no file are failures; a bad invocation is
  exit 2; the real `out\Release` core passes and the real `out\Debug` core is refused (a skip where that configuration
  was not built - CI builds both); and `build_package.ps1` makes both calls, in those places, each stopping the script.
  Mutants in `eng\mutants\release-core-guard.json`: 9 of 9 caught. One survived at first, and was the mutant's fault: it
  dropped an inline `(?i)` from the pattern, but `-match` already ignores case, so nothing changed. The pattern lost the
  flag (with a comment saying why) and the mutant now swaps `-match` for `-cmatch`.
  Baseline: managed 398 -> 414 passed (399 -> 415 total). Native and app suites are untouched by this change.

#### A sync match ignored in lock no longer costs the frame's words a bit

Found by reading `FrameProcessor::scanBit` for a performance review. While locked, a sync-pattern match that is not on
the frame boundary is data that happens to look like the sync, and is ignored ("leave all state intact"). But the data-word
`else` branch was the match's alternative, so the ignored match's bit was never counted towards the word being read:
`data_word_bit_count` did not advance, and every later word of that frame was read one bit late.

- **Who it hurt.** Receiver SNR: its channel values come from those words, so they were wrong for the frames hit. Frame
  Sync Lock results do not read the words and were not affected. How often depends on the pattern: about one bit in 2^32
  with a full 32-bit pattern, about one in 65,536 with a sparse mask such as 0x00FF00FF.
- **The fix.** The match is a match only for the sync rules (`sync_match`); it is a bit of data for the word count whenever
  it is not acted on. `total_syncs_found` still counts every match, which the failure report prints.
- **Checked.** New `FrameProcessor: an off-phase sync while locked leaves the frame's words where they are`: a locked stream
  whose middle frame's word 0 is 1001 (the sync itself), in both modes. Before the fix word 0 read as 2 and the average
  was 2.33 instead of 4.67; it also checks the match is still counted and costs no frame, and that the lock holds
  (36 of 40 bits). Mutants in `eng\mutants\off-phase-sync-word.json`. One kept mutant of `frame-processor-sums.json`
  (W2) was re-anchored: the fix removed a level of braces, so its text moved left by four.
  Baseline: native 524 -> 525.

- **A4, build hardening.** `SDLCheck` is on in both native projects and control flow guard (`/guard:cf`) in Release, for the

  Release DLL (180 targets) and in the hardened test executable (2,855), and none in the unhardened executable. The DLL reads recordings whose bytes nobody here controls, and control flow

#### The lock percentage is computed once (follow-up audit S4, third part)

`FrameProcessor` computed a window's lock percentage in two places, with the same expression: when a window closes in the
stream (`closeElapsedWindows`) and when the last, partly filled one is flushed at the end of the run. It is
`ScanState::lockPercent()` now, beside the two counters it is made from. No change of behaviour.

- **`ScanState::lockPercent()`**: the share of the window's bits seen in lock, 0 when it saw none. The valid bits are only
  counted together with the total and only while in lock, so it never exceeds 100 and needs no clamp (the note that said so
  at the flush moved with it). The two sites call it.
- **Checked.** `lock-percent.json` (new, 4 mutants: scaled by 99, the share out of lock, the flushed window reporting no
  lock, every closed window reporting full lock): 4 of 4 CAUGHT. Native 524 test cases, 0 warnings; managed 399 total (398 passed, 1 skipped) and app
  725 total (691 passed, 34 not run); the soak (eng\run_soak.ps1, Release core, all 34 runs): every CSV export byte for byte what v2.14.2 exported. Baselines: unchanged.
- This finishes S4 (its first two parts: the step-config file, and the plateau and saturated-top units).

#### The worker's running sums are the worker's (follow-up audit S2, first part)

could leave its sum in the word map for the next run to start from (`FrameProcessor` zeroed every sum at the start of a
run to guard against it, and a test set one to 1000 to check).

  starts and again when each window closes (`recordTimeSample` takes it). `ParameterInfo` has no `sample_sum`;
  `applyLinearCalibration` and the calibration extractor no longer reset one.
- **`process` takes a `const FrameSetup*`**, and the helpers a `std::vector<const ParameterInfo*>`: the word map a run
  reads is not changed by it, in the type. The hot loop sums into `s.channel_sums[i]` where it summed into the
  parameter.

  being the same parameter) lose that line, and the mutable-overload case uses a slope; one new case holds that two runs
  over one word map agree and that the map is as it was (`runPackets` takes a `const FrameSetup*`).

#### The two readers start a recording the same way (follow-up audit B9, S3)

`Chapter10Reader` (the channel list) and `Ch10PacketReader` (the run) each wrote out how a recording is started - open,
establish time, read the first packet, require TMATS, decode it - and the two copies had come to differ. They are one
now, in `ch10setup`, and the three hand-written walks of the TMATS tree's R records are one, in `tmatswalk.h`.

- **What differed, and what both do now.** (1) `prepare()` accepted irig106's "open warning" (a first packet it cannot
  read, or that is not a computer-generated packet) and `loadChannels()` refused it, so the metadata reader said
  `Error opening file` for a file the run would have told the real reason for: both accept it, and the steps after say
  what is wrong. (2) Only `prepare()` capped the read buffer, at 100 MB: `loadChannels()` allocated whatever a header
  claimed; both are capped. (3) A TMATS that failed to read or decode failed `prepare()` and let `loadChannels()` carry
  on to the end of the file and return true; both fail now, with the same words. (irig106's decoder returns OK for any
  text, so no test can make a decode fail; the step is shared all the same.)
- **What the user can see.** A file irig106 warns about still does not list, but says why in the words the run gives
  (`Failed to find TMATS message.` for a recording without its TMATS first, `Error establishing time sync.` for one cut
  inside its first header), not `Error opening file: <path>`, which stays for a file that does not open. The metadata
  reader reads only the first packet, as it always did in effect (it stopped at the first TMATS that decoded), so
  `inferChannelTypeFromHeader`, which could only see that packet's own type, is gone.
- **One rule for a data source's channel.** `tmatswalk::trackNumber` is the channel a data source names, or none: no
  track number, or a negative one, names none. The metadata reader used to list a negative one as a channel the packet
  reader then refused; both skip it now. Text still reads as 0, as `atoi` reads it (a malformed number is not told from
  channel 0), which is left as it was.
- **Where the code went.** `src/core/include/ch10setup.h`, `src/core/src/ch10setup.cpp`,
  `src/core/include/tmatswalk.h` (in `tmdq_core.vcxproj`; the `.cpp` in the native tests' project as well). The setup
  steps take the setup lock by reference (`Irig106SetupLock`, an alias in `irig106lock.h`), so a caller shows it holds
  it. `Ch10PacketReader::ensureBufferCapacity` and `Chapter10Reader::processTmatsPacket` are gone; the packet reader's
  `readPacket()` gives the run's two error texts once.
- **Tests.** `test_ch10setup.cpp` (7 cases: every step given a file that fails it, the cap, a packet read twice) and
  `test_tmatswalk.cpp` (4 cases: the walk and the track rule on trees built by hand); one case holding both readers to
  the same answer for seven files; two rows of the channel-listing case (a negative and a missing track number); two
  rows of the failed-load case changed to the shared messages. Their comment, which said no file reaches the
  metadata reader's TMATS check, is rewritten.
- **Checked.** Through `eng\mutate.ps1`: `reader-setup.json` (new, 16 mutants), and `reader-lifetime.json` and
  `packet-reader-optional-fields.json` re-anchored to the moved text. Native baseline 503 -> 515 test cases.

#### C++ tooling: .clang-format, .clang-tidy, the naming rule, include order, test-case names (follow-up audit C3, C5, C7)

The core had no formatter or analyser configuration (the `.clang-tidy` of #1 was deleted in #43, and `.vscode` ran clangd with `--fallback-style=none` because there was no `.clang-format`), its C++ naming
  rule decided on 2026-11-15 was written nowhere, and the native test cases were named three ways. Everything here is
  tuned to the code as it is: nothing is reformatted in bulk and no build or CI step runs the tools.

- **`.clang-format`** (root, with `tests/core/` overriding two options and `third_party/` unformatted) holds the code's
  structure: Allman braces with a namespace's brace left on its line, 4 spaces, 120 columns, the pointer with the type,
  an operator that breaks a line at the head of the next, no sorting of includes (the irig106 ones are in dependency
  order) and no comment reflow. Hand-aligned declarations and trailing comments are what it cannot hold exactly:
  formatting a whole file changes 27% of the product's lines and 35% of the tests' (measured over 91 files, option by
  option, which is how the options were chosen), so the guide says to format what you touch (`git clang-format`, Format
  Selection).
- **`.clang-tidy`** is the check list the core passes today: the old file's families, with 56 checks off, each listed in
  the file with its reason (style the code does not follow, its own idioms, the C ABI and C library boundary, noise on
  code that runs once per file), and the naming check on for everything the code follows. A first draft of the list
  found 119 things in the product sources: 10 are held on purpose and carry a `NOLINT` with the reason (the ABI's
  catch-all that must not unwind a host's thread, a destructor and a class whose constructors cannot throw, two
  roundings that are v2.14.2's own arithmetic, a tick loop over doubles, a static list of strings, three `atoi` calls on

  bit-exact comparison), and one unused variable in `test_abi.cpp` was removed. Both are clean. **Seen and not
  changed:** two of the three `atoi` sites in `chapter10reader.cpp` do not check what they read, where

- **`eng/gen_compile_flags.py`** defines `TMDQ_ABI_BUILD`: without it the header declares every ABI function `dllimport`
  and clang reported each definition in `src/core/abi` as a redeclaration (75 findings, in the editor too).
- **C3.** The naming rule is in the guide: PascalCase types and namespaces, camelCase functions, `m_snake_case` members,

#### The tests that read the process's memory no longer run beside other tests (follow-up audit)

`ParsedCsvsGiveTheirNativeMemoryBack` (#321) was the first of a family: five tests, in `ArenaTests`, `FormatsTests`,
  `HandleTests` (two) and `RunTests`, take the process's private memory before and after a loop and fail when it grew by
  more than a leak would. That number is the whole process's, and xunit runs test classes in parallel, so whatever else
  allocates while one of them runs is counted as its leak. Two tests added for an unrelated change were enough to move
  the schedule: `RunTests.DisposedResultsGiveTheirNativeMemoryBack` then failed on every full run (55, 62, 71 and 71 MiB
  grown against its 40 MiB, four runs of four), while passing alone, with its own class and on the code without the two
  tests. It is a leak of nothing: the same suite against the same DLL passed in the other tree.

- **`ProcessMemoryCollection`** (`DisableParallelization`) holds the four classes. xunit runs a collection like that
  alone, after the parallel ones, so nothing allocates beside these tests. Their other tests move with them (a class is
  one collection); the cost is about 8 seconds of the suite's 30.
- **Checked.** The managed suite 396 passed / 1 skipped three times in a row with the change; with the two tests that
  exposed it added (a tree with 398), it failed four of four before and passes three of three with the change. No
  product source changed, so there is no mutation check, and the native and app suites are not affected. No baseline
  moved.

#### A run disposed from its own callback is released once the callback has returned (follow-up audit)

An observer that disposes its run from `OnFinished` (or any callback) asked the binding to release it on the very thread
  the native library was calling back on. #315 made the library refuse that free, because the free joins the run's
  threads and the caller is one of them; the binding did not know it was refused. `RunHandle` and `CalibrationRunHandle`
  went on to free the callbacks' `GCHandle` anyway, so the run, never released, called back into a freed handle: an
  `InvalidOperationException` thrown out of an `UnmanagedCallersOnly` method, which ends the process.

- **`ObserverBridge.IsDelivering`** says whether the calling thread is inside one of that bridge's callbacks (a
  thread-static marker, saved and restored around each of the five callbacks, also when the observer throws): the
  library's own `CallbackEvents::delivering()`, one level up.
- **`CallbackRunHandle`**, the base of both run handles, releases as before from any other thread (the native free,
  which cancels and waits, and only then the context). From a callback it queues the same two steps to the thread pool,
  where the free waits for the callback to return and is not refused. `Dispose` from a callback therefore returns before
  the release has happened; its documentation says so, and says `Wait` from a callback returns at once.
- **Tests.** `HandleTests` and `CalibrationTests` each run a real run whose observer disposes it from its first progress
  report (and from the end, if there was none): it must still report its end, and its context must become collectible.
  `ObserverBridgeTests` (new) call the five callbacks through the pointers the library is given and check the marker:
  inside, not after, restored after a throw, and the outer run's restored when one callback is called inside another's.
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1`, managed, `eng/mutants/safe-handles.json`: 17 mutants, **17 CAUGHT or
  recorded**: H7 SURVIVED as recorded (a time base's few bytes), the other 16 CAUGHT. H3 and H4 were re-anchored to the
  new `Free` methods; new H13 (a release from a callback is not deferred: the old behaviour, a crash), H14 (the context
  freed before the native free), H15 (no thread is ever marked), H16 (not cleared after the end report) and H17 (cleared
  to nothing instead of the outer run's) are all CAUGHT. Managed suite **395** passed / 1 skipped, zero warnings; the
  app suite is unchanged. Baseline moved: managed 390 to 395.

#### The CSV memory test measures what it says it does (a flake on the CI runner)

`FormatsTests.ParsedCsvsGiveTheirNativeMemoryBack` failed on the CI runner of #320 ("private memory grew by 116 MiB over
  thirty parses"; its limit was 100) and once locally after a mutation run, and passed on a rerun each time. Nothing had
  changed in what it holds: parsing a CSV does not leak.

- **Why it flaked.** The test took the process's private memory as the measure of the native arrays, but each parse also
  makes managed copies of its arrays (about as many bytes again, on the large object heap), and how much of that garbage
  the collector keeps committed after a full collection varies: 15 MiB on a development machine, more on a loaded
  runner. So the managed heap's commitment was counted as a leak. **This is the explanation the numbers fit, not one
  seen on the runner:** the runner's managed figure was not logged, so it is unconfirmed there.
- **The fix.** The managed heap's growth in committed bytes
  (`GC.GetGCMemoryInfo(GCKind.FullBlocking).TotalCommittedBytes`, before and after the same collections) is taken off
  the private memory's growth, and the remainder is held to the same 100 MB. A leak of the 190 MB the arrays make is
  still far over it; the failure message now says how the growth divides.
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1`, managed (`eng/mutants/csv-parse-memory.json`): the free of a parsed
  CSV's native arrays dropped is **CAUGHT** by this test. The test passes five times in a row alone, and the managed
  suite: **390** passed / 1 skipped, no baseline moved. Native and app not affected.

#### Apply Template is busy while it checks the files, and the follow-up audit's small leftovers

- **The defect.** `ApplyTemplateAsync` checks the chosen recordings off the UI thread with no dialog up, and did not
  mark the window busy meanwhile, so Open, a drop and Recent Files were still there. A load started in that window made

#### The core: a reader's TMATS freed, the close inside the lock, and a free from a callback refused (follow-up audit)

Three defects the follow-up audit found by reading, each now held by a test. The first is a leak every session had; the
other two are a race and a crash no committed test or product path was known to reach.

- **The decoded TMATS was never freed.** irig106 allocates the tree a decode builds and gives it back only through
  `enI106_Free_TmatsInfo`, which nothing in the core called; both readers also zeroed the struct before each decode,
  which defeats the free the decoder itself does of an earlier tree. So every file opened, every run and every
  extraction kept one tree. Both readers now free it in their destructor (`Ch10PacketReader` after its channel table,
  whose entries point into the tree) and no longer zero it; `prepare()` on a reader prepared before closes the earlier
  handle and frees the earlier table first.
- **`Ch10PacketReader` closed its handle outside `lockIrig106Setup()`** (in its destructor and at the end of `run()`).
  The library's close marks the slot free before its last two writes to it, so an open on another thread could claim the
  slot and then have it marked closed. Both closes go through one `closeFile()`, which takes the lock; `irig106lock.h`
  and the domain invariant in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` now say the lock covers the close as well as the setup.
- **`tmdq_run_free` and `tmdq_calibration_free` from one of the handle's own callbacks** joined their own thread out of
  a destructor, which ends the process (from `finished`), or waited for a thread that was waiting for the callback (from
  a stream's). The header forbade the call and nothing refused it. The ABI's callback sink now knows which thread is
  inside one of its callbacks (`CallbackEvents::delivering()`), and free and wait both refuse there with a last error,
  releasing nothing; `tmdq_abi.h` says so. **A change of wording:** a wait from a callback used to fail inside the join
  and report "exception in tmdq_run_wait"; it now reports "tmdq_run_wait was called from one of the run's own callbacks
  and did not wait". Another run's callback, and a thread whose callback has returned, are refused nothing.
- **Not done.** The C# binding still frees a run's `ObserverBridge` after a free the library refused, so a managed
  observer that disposes its own run from a callback is still wrong (it was a crash before, and no product code does
  it); that is the binding's to refuse, in its own change.
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1`, native, `eng/mutants/reader-lifetime.json` (15 mutants): 15 **CAUGHT**.
  The leak: neither destructor freeing, either reader zeroing the tree before a second decode, a reader prepared again
  keeping its earlier handle (`a reader gives its decoded TMATS back`: private memory over 400 rounds, four ways). The
  lock: the close taking no lock, the destructor's or `run()`'s close going round `closeFile()` (`closing waits for the
  lock another thread holds`). The callbacks: a free from `finished` not refused (the test process dies), refused
  silently, or refused and freed anyway; a wait not refused; a thread left "inside a callback" after it returned; any
  run's callback counted as this run's (`onlyARunsOwnCallbackIsRefusedAndOnlyWhileItIsRunning` and the four
  `...FromItsOwnFinishedCallback...` cases). `-Rebuild` was not needed (no header deleted or renamed). Native **503**
  test cases passed / 1 skipped, managed **385** passed / 1 skipped, app **676** passed / 34 not run, zero warnings,
  imports on the allow-list. Baseline moved: native 498 to 503.

#### TmDq.Core: the native plumbing in Interop/, a type to a file, and a SafeHandle for each kind of handle (layout plan PR 5; audit S8)

The fifth of the source-layout PRs: the binding's files arranged the way the application's now are, and the one change
of behaviour the audit asked of it, handles that cannot be used while they are freed.

- **Moves.** What touches the DLL is in `Interop/`: `Native` (the P/Invoke declarations) and `NativeStructs` (its
  structs and
  the struct ids), `Arena`, `Text` (which lived in `Arena.cs`) and `ObserverBridge`. `Formats.cs` held thirteen types
  for five
  unrelated formats and is `Formats/` now, a file to a type; `MetricType` (used by the series and the plot, not only by
  the formats) and the public `Status` (six lines under a comment saying everything in `Native.cs` is internal) are
  files of the root, and `CalibrationPoint` and `CalibrationProfile` moved from `RunTypes.cs` to `Calibration.cs`. The
  namespace is still `TmDq.Core`, so no caller changed.
- **S8: a SafeHandle for each kind of native handle** (`Interop/Handles.cs`: run, calibration run, stream result, series
  set, series index, time base). The wrappers kept a raw `IntPtr`, three ways of behaving once disposed, a finalizer
  that
  one of them (`StreamResult`) forgot to suppress, and a `Cancel` that read the handle and then called native, so a
  `Cancel` racing a `Dispose` could pass a freed handle although the documentation said "safe from any thread". Now the
  P/Invoke declarations take the typed handle (the source-generated marshaller holds it open for the length of the call,
  so a handle cannot be freed under a call, nor one kind passed for another), only the free functions, which run in
  `ReleaseHandle`, take the raw value, and there is no finalizer on the wrappers (the handle's is the one). A call on a
  released handle throws `ObjectDisposedException`, which `Cancel`, `Wait` and `IsRunning` turn into "nothing is
  running", as
  they did. A run's or an extraction's handle owns its `ObserverBridge` and frees it after the native free, which
  cancels
  and waits, so the callbacks' context outlives every native thread that could use it.
- **One behaviour moves.** `Dispose` on a run or an extraction now cancels first. A `Wait` on another thread holds the
  handle open, and without the cancel the release would wait for the run to end by itself; with it, the wait returns at
  once and the release follows. With no other thread waiting nothing differs: `Dispose` still cancels, waits and frees
  before it returns, so an observer can be torn down straight after.
- **Not done.** The list-to-arena copy (three times), the pointer-array allocation (three times) and "negative means
  BadArgument" (four times) that S8 also lists are small repeats and are left; a handle's transient kinds (a parsed CSV,
  a geometry, a step list) are still freed in `try`/`finally`, being used within one call.
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1`, managed: `eng/mutants/safe-handles.json`, 12 mutants over the handles'
  lifetime, and the plot-index list (`eng/mutants/plot-index-binding.json`, repathed to the new handle's name) as a
  regression check. Safe handles: 11 **CAUGHT** and 1 **SURVIVED**, which was expected: a time base never freed leaks a
  few bytes that nothing can see. Caught: an index, a run, an extraction, a result and a series set never freed (the
  first by `HandleTests`, memory measured with disposed and with abandoned indexes; the run and extraction by their
  Dispose tests; the result and series set by the 30-result memory test), no handle owned, Dispose that does not cancel
  first while another thread waits on the run (`HandleTests`), Cancel and Wait after Dispose throwing, a released run
  reading as running, and a disposed result still read. Three mutants of mine were wrong and rewritten (a catch of
  `InvalidOperationException` is `ObjectDisposedException`'s base, so it changed nothing; and one the analyzer refused
  to compile). The four plot-index mutants are **CAUGHT**. The moves were checked by a build with zero warnings and the
  suite unchanged. Managed **380** passed / 1 skipped, zero warnings; app and native not affected (`clocktime.h` changed
  in a comment only). Baseline moved: managed 376 to 380 (`HandleTests`).

#### Each random draw in a native test on its own statement, so Debug generates what Release does

In a Debug build, `csvseries: the clock stamp is what v2.14 wrote, for every generated time` failed (three
assertions: the stamps' hash and two counts), on `main` as on any branch. CI runs the native suite in Release only, so
it never showed. The test drew two random numbers in one expression (`a + b`, each a `rng.below`), and C++ leaves
the order of the two operands to the compiler: the Debug build drew them the other way round from the Release build
the hash was recorded with, so it generated different times.

- **Found by a scan of every native test** for a statement with two draws whose order nothing fixes (a `?:`, `&&`, `||`
  and separate declarations all fix it). Two sites: that test (`test_csvseries.cpp`), and
  `seriesbuild: the plot's sequences ...` (`test_seriesbuild.cpp`, `bases[rng.below(8)] + (rng.chance(50) ? ...)`),
  which passed either way because it compares each sequence with the replaced code's answer in the same run, but
  generated different sequences in Debug and Release.
- **Each draw is now a statement of its own**, left to right: the order Release took, so no recorded value changes.
- **Checked.** Native, full suite in Debug: **498** passed / 1 skipped (was 497 and one failure); the two cases in
  Release pass. Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1` (`eng/mutants/random-draw-order.json`), 2 mutants: the clock-stamp
  test's two draws taken the other way round **CAUGHT** (the hash holds the order); the series test's the other way
  round **SURVIVED**, equivalent (that test holds no recorded order). Test code only: managed, app and soak not
  affected. No baseline moved.

#### The Receiver SNR yellow legible on the light theme

The yellow of the Receiver SNR primaries, `(230, 200, 30)`, is 1.7 to 1 against the light theme's white (WCAG's contrast ratio),
and the paler shades beyond the primaries are fainter still, so a yellow receiver's line and its legend swatch were hard to
see there. `ChartPalette.SeriesColor` now gives the colour a series is drawn in: its own, or, where its contrast against the
chart's background is below `MinSeriesContrast` (2.0 for the light theme, none for the dark), the same colour with its channels
scaled down by the least that reaches it. The line, the band and the legend's swatch use it, and the swatch follows a change of
theme. Of the primaries only the yellow is below 2.0 (the orange, the next lowest, is 2.3), so the other five are as they were.
The stored colour, the template, the Customize View swatch and the CSV are untouched, and the dark theme is unchanged;
a pale colour a user picks is drawn darker on the light theme too. `PlotColors`, and the 84 shades `PlotTests` holds to v2.14.2's,
are as they were.

Mutation check: eight mutants, the list kept outside the repository. Seven CAUGHT (the light theme's least set
to none, the contrast ratio flattened to 1, the scale starting too low, the threshold raised so the orange and green are
darkened, the line in the stored colour, and the legend's swatch in the stored colour at build and at a theme change). One
SURVIVED, as expected: the band's fill in the stored colour, which only the line's pixels, read back, test. The first run of the
legend mutant survived: the swatch was set right by the theme change when the view attached, so a recolour after the view was
shown, which rebuilds the rows, was added to the test. The app suite's baseline moves by four tests (664 to 668 with #301 and #302).

#### One fact in one place in the core: the receiver number, the sample period, the ABI getters, the units (audit X4, S6, S7, C4 in part)

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit; each site was re-read against the tree as of #299. Some of S6 and S7 had already
been done by earlier changes (the default settings path is `defaultReceiverParamsFile`; `toMetricType`,
`kCallbacksMinimum` and the enum asserts are in `abi_internal.h`; the chart wrapper reports under its own name): they
are not repeated here. The managed and app halves of C4 and X5 are left for the next change.

- **S6: the number after `_RCVR`, read in one place.** The series builder, the CSV column schema and
  `FrameSetup::receiverIndexFromName` each parsed it, and the first two kept a negative number where the third made
  it 0. That difference is recorded (the schema's 40000-header digest is the v2.14.2 parity oracle, and it keeps
  `_RCVR-7` as receiver -7), so it stays: `FrameSetup::receiverNumberInName` is the one reading, `receiverIndexFromName`
  is it with a number that is not positive made 0, and the other two call the first. Pinned before the move: a
  `_RCVR-3` row in the schema's parse table, a builder case for `-3`, `0`, `3x`, ` 2` and `+4`, and one for the two
  functions beside each other in `FrameSetup`'s tests. `asciiLower` (two copies), `upperAscii` and an inline
  lower-casing loop in `parseDouble` are `textparse::asciiLower` and `asciiUpper`, with a test that only A to Z and a to
  z move (UTF-8 bytes and the characters either side of the letters do not). Not done: the BOM sniffing in

  of the same four bytes), and the step file's default path (a different folder from the receiver parameters').
- **X4: the sample period, said and enforced.** `tmdq_abi.h` now says `0 = 1 s, 1 = 100 ms, 2 = 10 ms`, and
  `buildStreamJob` refuses any other index (`<label>: Sample period index is invalid.`, as it refuses a slope index)
  where it ran the stream at 100 ms in silence. The application cannot send one (a template's index is clamped to
  0 to 2 when it is read), so the change is for a host of the ABI. The recorded `sample-period-out-of-range` case, which
  expected the silent 100 ms, is three rejected cases (-1, 3, 7) and one for a lock stream; the builder's oracle is
  marked CHANGED as the others are, and the generated configurations draw an unknown index only one time in twelve so
  that the volume of accepted ones the test asserts stays. A managed test refuses -1, 3 and 99 through the binding.
- **S7: one ending for every getter.** Thirteen getters ended with the same four lines (`writeStruct`, else the
  last error "null output or a struct_size that is too small" and `TMDQ_ERR_BADARG`); they are `tmdq::writeOut`. A test
  pins the shared message for a short struct and a NULL one.

#### The analyzers and the editor settings, in the files that build (audit A2, A3)

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit; each count was re-measured on the tree as of #298 (the audit's 414 findings
were 140 once the rules it called noise were off, and the test projects, which it did not measure, added more).
The rest of the audit's standards work (the `.clang-format` of A4 and T8, the shared `eng/common.ps1` and
PSScriptAnalyzer of A5, the namespace style of C6) is left for the next change.

- **A2: the .NET analyzers are on, and every finding breaks the build.** `Directory.Build.props` sets `AnalysisLevel`
  `latest-recommended` and `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild`; the new root `.editorconfig` adds four rules the recommended
  set leaves off (CA2000 undisposed, CA1031 catch of `Exception`, CA1307 implicit culture, CA5392 P/Invoke search path)
  and switches off, each with its reason beside it, the ones that measured as noise (CA1515, CA2007, CA1062 and the
  API-shape opinions CA1003, CA1032, CA1308, CA1711, CA1716, CA1819, CA2227). A whole category cannot be switched on
  from the file (a rule the recommended set leaves off stays off under `category-X.severity`), so each rule is named.
  The tests have a short extra list (`[tests/**.cs]`: CA1305, CA1307, CA1310, CA1861, CA2000, CA1031, CA5392, about
  450 findings in ASCII fixtures, none a defect).
- **What the analyzers found, and was fixed.** `ProcessingViewModel` owned a `CancellationTokenSource` and was not
  disposable: it is now, and the run and the calibration extraction dispose it (a Cancel after that does nothing);
  `PlotChart` held its cached bitmap and its native indexes until the garbage collector reached them: both are
  released when the chart leaves the visual tree, and made again if it returns (the one suppression, of CA1001, says so);
  `StreamResult.Dispose` now suppresses the finalizer it made pointless; five `throw new ObjectDisposedException` are
  `ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf`; the 75 P/Invokes carry one assembly-level `DefaultDllImportSearchPaths`
  (assembly folder only; the resolver loads by full path before it is used); `string.IndexOf(char)` and `Replace`
  take `StringComparison.Ordinal`; six `FirstOrDefault()` on indexable lists are indexers; the "not an exported CSV"
  message is a cached `CompositeFormat`; two dash arrays are static fields; three return and parameter types are the
  concrete ones (`ConfigToJson`, `Sentence`, the legend's `Row`). Left as suppressions with their reasons: the observer
  bridge's five `catch (Exception)` (an exception must never unwind a native thread), its ownership hand-over of a

  doc comments, so the projects now generate the documentation file (`TmDq.Core.csproj` said `false`, and no longer
  does); it is not published (`PublishDocumentationFile`, `PublishReferencesDocumentationFiles`: a `dotnet publish`

  CS1573). The eight unused usings it found are gone (the audit's 26 had mostly gone with earlier changes).
- **Malformed doc comments, which the same switch found.** `StreamRules.TimeChannelText` had a raw `<id> - <name>`
  in its summary; two `paramref` named a parameter that is not there; `TempFiles` had three ambiguous `cref`s. And
  `CalibrationDigest.cs`, `FormatsDigest.cs` and `SeriesDigest.cs` were stored with CR CR LF line ends, which broke
  their doc comments: they are ordinary now (a whole-file diff, nothing else in them changed).
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1`: app (`ProcessingTests`, `PlotDraftTests`, `CalibrationDialogTests`,

#### The compiler's gate and the package versions, in the files that build (audit A1, T7, A5 in part)

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit; each claim was re-measured on the tree as of #297. The rest of the audit's
standards work (A2 and A3, the `.editorconfig` and the .NET analyzers; the `.clang-format` of A4 and T8; the shared
`eng/common.ps1` and PSScriptAnalyzer of A5) is left for the next change, which has to fix what those rules find.

- **A1, T7: level 4, and every warning an error, in the project files.** `tmdq_core.vcxproj` and `tmdq_core_tests.vcxproj`
  compiled at level 3 with five warnings raised to level 3 by switch, and with `TreatWarningAsError` false: the
  zero-warning rule lived in the scripts' scan of their own log, so a build from an IDE or VS Code was not gated, and an
  incremental scripted build did not recompile unchanged files, whose warnings were therefore not in the log. Both now
  have `WarningLevel` `Level4` and `TreatWarningAsError` true, and the five `/w3` switches go (C4100, C4189 and
  C4456 to C4458 are level 4 warnings). The audit's measurement held: the core's first-party code was already clean at
  level 4 (Debug and Release, `-Rebuild`, zero warnings), and the only cost was marking the vendored irig106 headers
  external (`ExternalIncludePath`, `ExternalWarningLevel` `TurnOffAllWarnings`), whose C4201 would otherwise fail every
  first-party file that includes them. The irig106 `.c` files still compile with warnings off. The scripts' scan stays,
  as a second line.
- **The tests' own code was not clean.** `test_framesync.cpp` had eight string literals in which an octal escape is
  followed by a digit (`"\0117\012"`, read as `\011` then `7`: C4125, a level 4 warning); each is now split at the
  escape (`"\011" "7\012"`), the same bytes. No other test file warned.
- **A5: `Directory.Packages.props` and `global.json`.** The Avalonia version `12.1.4` was typed six times in two project
  files and xunit's twice, and a bump that missed the test project would have been a run-time mismatch, not a build
  error. Every version is now in `Directory.Packages.props` (central package management; Avalonia's packages share one
  `AvaloniaVersion`), the projects name their packages without one, and a version typed in a project is refused
  (NU1008). The licence check still runs over whatever resolves, transitive packages included. `global.json` asks for
  the 10.0.100 SDK or a newer one (`latestFeature`, no prerelease): it stops an older SDK building the repository, but it
  does not pin the feature band, which CI's `10.0.x` would then have to follow.
- **Checked.** Negative checks with `eng\mutate.ps1`: a level 4 warning in a first-party source (an assignment in a
  condition, C4706, in `clocktime.cpp`) fails the native build (C2220), and a version typed in `TmDq.Core.Tests.csproj`
  fails the managed one (NU1008): both COMPILE, as expected. The core in Debug and Release with `-Rebuild`: zero
  warnings, imports on the allow-list. All three suites: native **495** (1 skipped, Release; the tests project also
  compiled in Debug), managed **366** passed / 1 skipped, app **647** passed / 34 not run, Release, zero warnings. No
  baseline moved. No product code changed, so no soak or throughput run.

#### The manual's figures the same in every render

Re-rendering the figures (`eng\build_manual.ps1`) changed four of them nearly every time. It looked like the run log's
clock, but that is already fixed (`FigureClock`). What varied, found by rendering the figures repeatedly and comparing them
pixel by pixel:

- the run log's lines. The core logs a `NN% read...` line at the first progress check past each tenth of the file, and that
  check is time-gated (`ch10packetreader.cpp`), so it read `42%` in one render and `41%` in the next; a stream's
  `elapsed N.Ns` is wall-clock time; and the reader's thread and the streams' threads log together, so `Reading Chapter 10
  file...`, the streams' start lines and their results came in a different order from one run to the next;
- the progress dialog's bar, which the capture takes at the first report past 70 %, so at 70, 71 or 73;
- the receiver tree's chevrons, which a new expander makes turned over and brings to rest at the first render ticks, so a
  capture before or between them caught a chevron half turned.

The harness now sets each right before a capture, and the application is as it was: `ManualFiguresTests.Steady` puts the
percentages and seconds in one wording and the racing lines in one order (the reader's `Reading...`, the start lines, the
percentages, then each stream's results, the streams by channel), the progress figure pins the bar at 70, and the
Customize View scene runs the ticks that bring its chevrons to rest (`AtRest`). The two pure rules have tests (eight
cases; the app suite is 682 run, 648 passed with 34 not run, from 640 and 34). Rendered seven times, 26 of the 27 figures
came out the same in every render. The 27th, the receiver tree's, still varies in about one render in four by one level
of colour in three pixels at a checkbox's edge, a fade that a longer wait did not end; its committed figure is left as it was.
The three figures that did change (`walk-err-01-log-error`, `walk-fs-04-processing`, `walk-theme-01-light-plot`) show the
log in its set order and wording, and are re-embedded in both manuals.

Mutation check: seven mutants of the harness. Six CAUGHT (the percentage set to the wrong tenth, the seconds to another
value, the start lines ranked after the results, the streams not taken by channel, the reader's first line left among the
percentages, and a capture that does not set the log steady, which the log-error scene asserts). One SURVIVED, as expected: the
progress bar not pinned at 70, which only the figure's pixels show and no test reads.

#### Tests that could not fail, and tests that could fail for the wrong reason (audit Q1, Q2, Q3)

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit; each site was re-read against the tree as of #293. Q4 (test support written several
times), Q5 (large test files) and Q6 (the smoke branch) are left for their own changes.

- **Q1: bare deletes, and swallowed ones.** Three tests deleted a `.ch10` the core had just opened in a `finally`
  (`ProcessingTests`, and two in `WalkingSkeletonTests`): now `TempFiles.Delete`, which waits out a virus scanner's hold
  and still throws on a leaked handle. Four build-tool test classes (`LicenceBuildTests`, `PackageLicenceTests`,
  `ThirdPartyNoticesTests`, `VersionBuildTests`) swallowed every delete failure in `Dispose` with no stated reason: now
  `TempFiles.TryDeleteDirectory`, named for what it is (a scratch folder a child process may still hold; a leftover folder
  in `%TEMP%` is no failure), with its own test. The `write-test` skill says which of the two to use.
- **Q2: expectations taken from the constant under test.** `StreamRules.PatternRequired`'s text was in no test (three
  files compared with the constant), so a reworded message passed: two cases now hold the literal. The plot's layout tests
  built their expected pixels from `PlotChart.OuterMargin`, `TopInset` and `AxisLabelGap`, so a moved margin moved test and
  chart together: `TheChartsMarginsAreTheValuesTheLayoutTestsAreWrittenIn` pins all five as numbers. `appVersionValues`
  (three numbers checked as not negative) could not fail; it now also refuses the 0.0.0 of an unset version, with no
  version typed in it (the managed suite's `VersionTests` hold the number to the packaging's).
- **Q3: timing and machine dependence.** `OnlyTheLastStepsDelaySettlesTheGesture` failed a plot that was right on a stalled
  machine ("too slow to tell") and held the settle to 390 ms of a 400 ms `Task.Delay`, which Windows' coarse timer can end a
  tick early (the same flake as #283 and #287): its delay is 1000 ms, the check has 500 ms of margin, a longer stall is a
  skip (`Assert.Skip`, shown to report as skipped under `AvaloniaFact`), and the end is held to 3/4 of the delay.
  `WhileBusyNeitherImportNorExportStartsAndBothAreToldWhenItEnds` polled for a log line with no limit and relied on the run
  being parked: it now waits for Configure Streams to be asked for (`FakeConfigurator.Waiting` takes a callback), with a
  60 s limit. The three native cases that slept 100 to 300 ms "so the worker reaches its empty queue" wait for each worker's
  own "processing..." line first (a stalled worker is no longer cancelled before it has started, which left the wake path
  unrun) and keep a 50 ms settle for its next call; the cancel-from-another-thread case cancels once the reader has begun
  and not 100 ms in. `Abi: aCsvIsParsedLikeTheCore` read two CSV exports from `tests/data` only where they existed, so
  CI covered less than a developer's machine: two real v2.x exports, trimmed to a header and a few rows, are committed in
  `tests/fixtures` and required.
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1`: app suite (four classes), 7 mutants, **7 CAUGHT** (Q2a a reworded message,
  Q2b to Q2d three margins moved, Q3a an earlier step's delay settling the gesture, Q3b half the delay, Q3c a load that is
  not busy while Configure Streams is up); native (`Constants*` and the CSV case), 2 mutants, **2 CAUGHT** (V1 an unset
  0.0.0 version, V2 a negative one). All three suites in Release, zero warnings: native **495** (1 skipped), managed **365**
  passed / 1 skipped, app **644** passed / 34 not run. Baselines moved: managed 364 to 365 (the `TryDeleteDirectory` test),
  app 643 to 644 (the margins test).

#### Behaviour bugs: one word-map resolution for both passes, a lost drag, a busy drop, a calibration result the core cannot give (audit B10, B5, B11, B4)

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit. B10's direction is the owner's of 2026-11-15 (both passes fall back, with a
warning); B4's seam was decided the same day.

- **B10: the main run and the calibration extractor resolved the word map differently.** With no file named and the
  shipped `settings\receiver_params\default.toml` present but unusable (a word past the frame, not TOML), the main run
  passed it over in silence for the sequential map while the extraction failed, though the extractor's profiles are
  matched to the main run's channels by word. Both now call one `resolveReceiverWordMap` (`framesetup.h`, with
  `defaultReceiverParamsFile`): the named file, else the default, else the sequential map for the counts; an unusable
  default is passed over in both, and both say so ("the default Receiver Parameters file 'default.toml' could not be
  used; the sequential word map for N x M receiver channels is used instead.", in the run's log once its job is accepted,
  and in the calibration's). `CalibrationExtractor::Request` gains `receiverParamsIsDefault`, which
  `buildCalibrationRequest` sets when the file it found is the default, so a file the user named is still an error. The
  extractor's load failure now says what the main run's does ("Failed to load Receiver Parameters from '<file>'. Check
  the word map."). Tests: `an unusable default word map is passed over for the sequential map, as the main run passes it
  over` (both passes, the same names on the same words), `a word map the user named is not passed over, even when it is
  the default file`; the stream-job oracle and three recorded digests gain the warning.
- **B5: a drag whose capture was lost went on.** `PlotChart` had no `OnPointerCaptureLost`: the plot would pan with no
  button down, or keep its band drawn, until the next release. Now a lost capture drops a band without zooming, settles a
  pan where it got to, and gives the cursor back; `PlotLegend`'s override gives its cursor back too. Tests:
  `ADragWhoseCaptureIsLostEndsWhereItIs`, `ADragWhoseCaptureIsLostIsTheFullPictureAtOnce`.
- **B11: the drag cursor offered a drop the app would ignore while busy.** The drop is Recent Files' open, so it now
  follows the command's rule: offered and taken only when `OpenRecentCommand` would take it. The drop test checks that
  a run in progress is offered nothing.
- **B4: a calibration result the core could not give.** `GetResult()` sat outside the extraction's `try`; a failure
  there (out of memory, an internal error) left the status at "Processing calibration file..." with the progress dialog
  gone. The run now starts through `ICalibrationRunner` (`Services`; the core's `CalibrationRun` by default), so a test
  can stand in, and the failure is a cross with the core's message. Test:
  `AResultTheCoreCannotHandBackIsACrossNotAProcessingThatNeverEnds`.
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1`: native (stream job, calibration extractor and request, frame setup), 5
  mutants, **5 CAUGHT** (N1 the warning dropped, N2 an unusable default refused, N3 the extractor ignoring that its file is
  the default, N4 the request never saying so, N5 the main run silent again); app (four classes), 8 mutants, **6 CAUGHT**
  (A1 the lost capture ignored, A2 the band left drawn, A3 the pan carrying on, A4 the pan's draft left up, A6 a drop
  offered while busy, A8 the result's failure unhandled) and **2 SURVIVED**, both reasoned: A5 the legend's cursor
  (Avalonia's `Cursor` exposes no type to assert) and A7 the drop handler's own busy check (the view model refuses a busy
  open too, so it is defence, not the rule). The soak ran on this change (`eng\run_soak.ps1`): all 34 runs exported byte for byte what v2.14.2 exported. All three suites in Release, zero
  warnings: native **495** (1 skipped), managed **364** passed / 1 skipped, app **643** passed / 34 not run. Baselines
  moved: native 493 to 495, app 640 to 643.

`PackageLicenceTests.EveryProjectInTheSolutionGetsTheCheckAndTheVersion` failed once on CI with
`'M' is invalid after a single JSON value` and never again: it could not be reproduced, and the message could not say
why, because `BuildTool.Evaluate` threw away the output it had failed to parse. It now reports it: a parse failure (or a
reply without the `Properties` object) raises a test failure naming the project and carrying everything `dotnet msbuild
-getProperty` printed. The assertions are unchanged, and no test was added or removed (app baseline as it was: 640
passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 34 not run). Checked by making the parse fail on purpose (a stray character put before the
output): the test then failed with the project, the parser's message and the whole of msbuild's reply.

#### The processing window that nothing could set, and two dead fields on the decode path (audit D2, D1, D3)

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit. D2 is the owner's decision of 2026-11-15: remove the window and say so in the user
story. D1 and the `is_enabled` half of D3 were held back from the dead-code PR because they are on the decode path too.

- **D2: the `[start, stop]` window is gone.** `ProcessingParams::startSeconds`/`stopSeconds` were only ever 0 and the
  maximum (the ABI has no field for them, and the calibration extractor set the same), so `in_window` was always true, the
  "processing (Ns to Ms)..." log line never printed, and the state existed for one test. Removed: the two fields and the
  three places that set them, the per-bit `in_window` test and the four branches it gated in `scanBit` and the bit loop
  (missed frames, the lock counters, word extraction, closing windows), and `ScanState`'s copies. The IRIG clock's first
  window is still seeded from the first packet's time (a time before the epoch, which a recording cannot carry, still seeds
  at zero, exactly as the window's zero start did). Tests: "a bounded window keeps exactly the bits from its start to its
  stop" and the reporting rows "bounded-window" and "stop-bounded" are removed, and "unsynced bits miss one frame per frame
  length, counted only inside the window" loses its from-100 s half and the last four words of its name. US3.1's scope now
  says missed frames are counted over the whole recording, as do `docs/framesync_logic.md` and the `tm-code-review`
  skill.
- **D1: `FrameProcessor::PacketTimeRef`.** `prev_time_ref`, `has_time_ref`, `start_bit` and `num_bits` were written and
  never read; the one field read, the packet's base time, is `item.baseAbsSeconds`, which the loop now reads directly.
- **D3 (b): `ParameterInfo::is_enabled`.** It was true for every parameter outside tests, so every word of the map is a
  channel; the filter in `buildEnabledParams` and the three places that set the flag are gone. The test "only enabled words
  become channels" is now "every word of the map becomes a channel" without its disabled word, and the stream-job digest
  test's recorded expectations drop the `window=11-99` and `en=1` fields they carried in every case (31 and 135 of them).
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1` on the native suite (frame processor, frame sync, stream job and
  calibration extractor cases), 7 mutants on the code that lost its guards, **7 CAUGHT**: W1 missed frames not counted,
  W2 the lock denominator not counted, W3 windows never closed, W4 the IRIG clock seeded at zero, T1 a bit's time without
  its packet's base, E1 a word of the map dropped, X1 no word extracted. The soak (`eng\run_soak.ps1`, all 34 runs) and
  the throughput gate (`eng\run_throughput_bench.ps1`) ran on this change: all 34 runs exported byte for byte what v2.14.2 exported. The gate passed, pinned to the performance cores: four streams in parallel 12.8 s against 13.2 s for the slowest alone (0.97x) and 20.4 s for all four in sequence (0.63x). All three suites
  in Release, zero warnings: native **493** (1 skipped), managed **364** passed / 1 skipped, app **640** passed / 34 not
  run. Baseline moved: native 494 to 493 (the bounded-window case).

product uses, after a re-count with the status bar back (it binds `Status`, `StatusLevel` and `HasStatusMark` only).

- **Dropped, seven.** `MainWindowViewModel.Progress` (the dialog's own progress is what the user sees),
  `Processing` and `Preferences`; `PlotViewModel.SetSeriesVisible`, `PushXZoom` and `ZoomDepth`, with
  `PlotTimeWindow.Depth`; `ExtractCalibrationViewModel.Steps`. Their tests now go through the product's paths: a visibility

#### Dead code: what nothing in the product reaches

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit (PR 9 of this series, the audit's own "dead code" PR: D3, D4, D5, D10, D11); each
finding was re-counted against the tree as of #283, and the decisions on D3 are the owner's of 2026-11-15. D1 and the
`is_enabled` half of D3 are on the decode path (`FrameProcessor`), so they wait for the processing PR with D2, which runs
the soak and the throughput gate; D8 gets its own PR.

- **D3: core parameters and branches no product caller reaches.** `TomlDocument::load` and `save` lose the `error`
  out-parameter no product caller passed (its three messages were unreachable; the callers say what failed in their own
  words). The test "the messages name the file and say what failed" went with them; "a missing file and an unwritable path
  report errors" became "a missing file is not ok and an unwritable path does not save". `SeriesTimeBase::recomputeClock`
  loses its `gmtime_r` branch for a platform this project does not build on. Kept, as decided: the test-only accessors
  (`FrameProcessor::result()`, `TomlDocument::arrayTables()`, `Chapter10Reader::clearSettings()`).
- **D4: three aliases in `constants.h`.** `kDefaultBitsPerFrame` (an alias of `kDefaultFrameSyncLockBits`) is gone and its
  one user names the original; `kNumKnownPrefixes` is now the prefix array's size and `kMaxSlopeIndex` the voltage table's
  size less one, with a `static_assert` that the two voltage tables agree.
- **D5: five unused includes** (`<algorithm>`, `<cmath>`, `<vector>`, `<unordered_map>`, `<utility>`), settled by a
  `-Rebuild` of the core and the native tests in Release with zero warnings.
- **D10: unused `using` lines.** A compiler pass with IDE0005 on (`AnalysisLevelStyle=latest-all`, built to a scratch
  folder) named 29 today (the audit's 26 plus three from files added since): 6 in the app and the binding, 23 in the tests.
- **D11: wider than needed, or never null.** Nine members used only in their own file are private (`StreamsRun.LabelOf`,
  `PeriodMilliseconds`, `Completed`; `MainWindowViewModel.NotAnExportedCsv`; `TemplateFile.MaxSamplePeriodIndex`;
  `MenuChoice.SeparatorHeader`; `PreferencesStore.FolderName`; `HelpManual.BaseManualResource`;
  `Startup.SmokeReportVariable`). `OkCommand?.` and `ApplyCalCommand?.` lose the `?`, since both constructors assign
  them before anything can call those methods. `partial` comes off the seven view models with no source generator behind
  them (the audit counted eight; one has gained a generator since). Nine `x:Name`s nothing references are gone
  (`RowsScroller`, the four Select All/None buttons, `LogBox`, `PlotFileMenu`, `ReadoutMenu`, `WordMap`).
- **Checked.** Mutation check, `eng\mutate.ps1` on the native suite (constants, TOML, stream job and frame setup cases),
  5 mutants: **4 CAUGHT** (D4a/D4b each derived count off by one, D3a1 a missing file read as ok, D3a2 an unwritable path
  reported as saved), **1 SURVIVED**: D3a3, a failure at close reported as saved, which needs a disk that fills mid-write
  and was untested before this change too. All three suites in Release, zero warnings: native **494** (1 skipped),
  managed **364** passed / 1 skipped, app **640** passed / 34 not run. Baseline moved: native 495 to 494 (the messages
  test).
- **Beside it: the wheel-settle flake again.** CI failed this PR on `TheWheelSettlesOnItsOwnAfterTheRefineDelay` with
  "settled 24.1 ms after the wheel, before its 30 ms delay": #283's 25 ms bound was too close. The refine wait is a
  `Task.Delay`, whose timer runs on Windows' coarse tick (15.6 ms) and can end up to a tick early, so no bound within a tick
  of the delay holds. The test now waits 100 ms and asks for at least 75. Mutants F1 (no delay) and F2 (half of it) are
  CAUGHT again.

  (channel 13), 116 samples, mean lock 93.5 %`, a path in the batch's, a reason per stream). Now:

  | Action | Was | Is |
  |---|---|---|

  | Export | nothing | `Exported data, plot image and log file.`; `Exported log file. Could not export data and plot image. See the log.`; `Could not export plot image. See the log.` |

#### Repository configuration: a lint config that was never read, ignore rules that would drop files, a solution platform that cannot build

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit (PR 5 of its list); each finding was re-run against the tree as of #276 before it was
touched. No product code changed. The one behaviour change, B7, has a test that fails against the old script (restored as
mutants B1-B4 below).

- **T1: `.pymarkdown.json` was never read.** pymarkdown 0.9.39 auto-discovers `.pymarkdown`, not `.pymarkdown.json`:
  `python -m pymarkdown scan docs/claude.md` reported 446 lines before and none after the rename (`git mv`). Every document
  outside the changelog and the records is clean with the config applied. `docs/claude.md` says which name it is.
- **T2 and the dead rules of D11: ignore rules that would hide a new file.** `git check-ignore -v` named `tests/.gitignore:2`
  (`*.txt`), `.gitignore:83` (`*.csv`) and `.gitignore:20` (`*.app`, which matches a folder `Foo.App/`, case-blind on
  Windows, and needed a `!TmDq.App/` re-include) for `tests/fixtures/x.txt`, `tests/fixtures/x.csv` and `Foo.App/x.cs`; after
  the change nothing names the first and third, and `*.csv` is `/*.csv` (the root only). Gone too: `*.o *.slo *.lo *.so
  *.dylib *.a *.lai *.la`, `*.sdf`, `*.opensdf`, `compile_commands.json`, `.clangd` (which would have hidden a real clangd
  config), `tests/.gitignore`'s `output/`, the `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json` re-include, and four `.gitattributes` rules
  (`*.sh`, `*.bat`, `*.cmd`, `*.rc`) that match no tracked file. `git status` lists no file that was not listed before.
  Kept: `*.VC.opendb`, `*.out`, and the binary rules for `*.exe`/`*.dll` (ignored anyway, but they say what a stray one is).
- **T3: the solution's `x86` platform built nothing.** It mapped both native projects to `Win32`, which neither vcxproj
  defines: `msbuild tmdq.sln -p:Platform=x86` failed with MSB8013 on both. The `x86` solution platform and its 26 mappings are
  gone, so it now fails at once with MSB4126 (an invalid solution configuration), and `x64` and `Any CPU` validate.
  `Any CPU` stays, because `dotnet build` of the solution defaults to it and it maps the native projects to `x64`.
- **T5: `eng\test_dotnet.ps1` computed a fallback DLL and never used it.** With `-Configuration Debug` and only a Release
  core built it went on, and `Env.DllPath` (Release first, then Debug) ran the suite against the other configuration's core.
  It now throws as `test_app.ps1` does, and hands the test exe the DLL of its own configuration through `TMDQ_CORE_DLL`
  (removed again afterwards, so a later run in the same session is not pinned to it). Checked by running it for Debug with only
  Release built: it stops, naming `eng\build_core_dll.ps1 -Configuration Debug`.
- **T8: editor configuration.** `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json` was inert (`C_Cpp.intelliSenseEngine` is `disabled`, clangd
  reads `compile_flags.txt`) and is deleted. The extension recommendation `eclipse-cdt.cdt-gdb-vscode` (a GDB adapter, which
  cannot read MSVC PDBs) is replaced by the two debuggers `launch.json` uses: `ms-vscode.cpptools` (`cppvsdbg`) and

  `settings.json` loses what served other projects (CMake, WSL, CUDA, doxygen, CodeSnap, Error Lens, IntelliCode,

- **T9: the Sandbox script failed as its header said to run it.** `run_sandbox_test.ps1` with no arguments installed into
  a Sandbox whose verifier needed four payload items it had not been given. With `-Payload` omitted it now supplies them:
  the portable ZIP beside the setup, `deploy\avalonia\staging\unsigned`, the PRN sample, and v2.x's setup (from `deploy\`

- **B7: a copyright pattern Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot match.** `eng\gen_third_party_notices.ps1` held a raw `©`
  (UTF-8 bytes C2 A9) in a file with no byte order mark, and the packaging always runs it under 5.1, which reads those two

  `Copyright (c) © X`. The pattern now says `\u00A9`, and the em dash in `eng\env.ps1`'s first comment is a hyphen.
  New tests: `ACopyrightThatStartsWithTheSignIsNotPrefixedAgain` (fails against the old script) and
  `TheScriptsWindowsPowerShellRunsHoldOnlyAscii` (every `eng` and `deploy` script that has no byte order mark).
  The app suite's `ThirdPartyNoticesTests` runs the real script in `powershell` (5.1).
- **`eng\mutate.ps1` can mutate a script a test runs.** A file under `eng\` is read by the test as a child process and
  built into nothing, so the "product newer than the mutated file" check reported every such mutant STALE; it now skips the
  check for those files.

#### The dialogs in Fluent's anatomy: one footer, 24 px of padding, switches for settings, Fluent's status colours

The second of the two steps asked for after #272 (the first, below, named the colours, the font, the type scale and the
corners): every dialog laid out as Fluent's ContentDialog is, a setting that is on or off drawn as Fluent's toggle switch,
and every status painted in one set of theme-aware colours. The dialogs stay windows with their own title bars.

- **One footer, `DialogFooter`.** Every dialog had laid its own buttons out (a `Grid` here, a `StackPanel` there, a
  `MinWidth` of 80, the margins 10, 12 or 16, and the accent only where someone had remembered it). Now each has the
  same band across the foot of its window: the base colour under a divider (`DividerStrokeColorDefault`), the buttons at
  the right in equal widths, none narrower than 96 px, 8 px apart (`ContentDialogButtonSpacing`), with 24 px round it. The
  default button (Enter) takes the accent on its own (a `DialogFooter` adds the class to whichever of its buttons
  `IsDefault`), so it cannot be forgotten; Escape cancels everywhere except the progress dialog, where it must not stop a
  run. What belongs to the choice rather than the answer ("Apply to all Frame Sync Lock streams", "All") is `Leading`, at
  the left. The content has 24 px of padding (`ContentDialogPadding`; was 12 to 16). `DialogFooter.Compose` builds the
  same for the dialogs made in code (`ChoiceWindow`, the four prompts, `ReportWindow`), which had a copy of the layout
  each. The `Separator`s that stood in for the divider are gone.
- **Fluent's toggle switch** for the three settings that are on or off: Derandomize and Invert Data (side by side now, in
  one row, since a switch carries its label above it) and Legacy Chapter 10. A check box remains where one chooses among
  several (a stream to process, "Apply to all", "All", what to export, the batch's options), as Fluent has it. The switches
  bind to the same properties, so nothing in the view models moved.
- **One status palette.** The application had three sets of values for success, warning and error: the log's (pure
  `#FF0000`, goldenrod, a dark `#008000` that was hard to read on the dark chrome), the converters' (`Brushes.Green`,
  `#CC0000`, goldenrod, `Gray`) and literals in two dialogs (`#2E9E44`, `#D13438`, `Gray`), none of them theme-aware. They
  are Fluent's four status tokens, with Fluent's values (success `#0F7B0F` light / `#6CCB5F` dark, caution `#9D5D00` /
  `#FCE100`, critical `#C42B1C` / `#FF99A4`, neutral `#72000000` / `#9CFFFFFF`): `SystemFillColorSuccess`, `Caution`,
  `Critical` and `Neutral`, a Color and a Brush each. `StatusPaint` is the one place a state becomes a colour: the view
  model's state maps to a `StatusLevel` (`StatusPaint.Match`, `StatusPaint.Calibration` for the converters), and the
  attached `StatusPaint.Level` binds a text's foreground to the level's token, so it follows the theme live. `StatusBrushes`
  keeps only `FromColor` (a series' colour is the user's, not a theme's). The log picks its lines' brushes when it adds
  them and draws them again when the theme changes (`LogView.ActualThemeVariantChanged`). The log's `ErrorBrush`,
  `WarningBrush` and `SuccessBrush` and the converters' `Of` and `OfMatch` are gone. **This is a visible change:** the dark
  theme's error is a light pink and its warning a yellow, which are Fluent's, where they were a saturated red and a gold.
  Configure Streams' ready marks, the setup dialog's problem text and calibration label, the batch confirmation's glyphs and
  Extract Calibration's two status lines take them too. The Export and Import icons' greens are the icons', and stay.
- **Secondary text.** The word map (Stream Setup) and the line saying why a stream cannot be processed (Configure Streams)
  were `Opacity="0.75"` of whatever they sat on; they take `TextFillColorSecondary`, as the hints and headers did.

**Tests:**
- New `DialogAnatomyTests.EveryDialogHasTheOneFooterBandWithItsButtonsAtTheRightInEqualWidths`, in both themes, for **every
  window kind the application has** (`IconTests.EveryWindowKind`, so a dialog added later is held without being listed): the
  one footer, spanning the window's width and ending at its foot; the band drawn in the base colour and its top row in the
  divider's, pixel by pixel; the content's 24 px margin; the buttons in one width of at least 96, 8 apart, the last 24 px from the
  right edge; the leading item at 24 px and clear of the buttons; the default accented and the only accent; a cancel button,
  except in the progress dialog, which has no default and no cancel.
- New `DialogAnatomyTests.ATextShowsItsStatusInTheThemesColourAndFollowsAChangeOfTheme` (a status text, light, dark,
  another level, then none) and `ProcessingTests.TheLogDrawsItsLevelsAgainInTheNewThemesColoursWhenTheThemeChanges`.
- New `StreamWindowsTests.TheOnOffSettingsAreSwitchesAndTheChoicesAreBoxes`: the three switches are switches and bind both ways;
  "Apply to all", "All" and each row's Process are check boxes.
- `EachThemesTokensAreFluentsNamesInVsCodesValues` has the four status tokens (as a Color and a Brush, both themes). The tests
  that pinned the old colours (the log's, the batch glyphs', the calibration labels', Extract Calibration's status lines)
  read the tokens' values, and `StatusBrushes.Of`/`OfMatch` became `StatusPaint.Of`/`OfMatch`, which return a level.

**Mutation check** (`eng\mutate.ps1`, app suite, 21 mutants): **21 of 21 caught**. The first pass caught 18; the footer's band colour, divider,
padding, button spacing, minimum width, accent and the leading item, the code-built dialogs' padding, Escape in a code-built dialog,
the status tokens, a warning mapped to critical, a status colour that does not follow the theme, the log not redrawn on a theme
change, a warning line drawn critical, the batch glyphs unpainted and a switch turned back into a box were all caught at once. Two
survived, which were gaps: the ready marks' colours (Configure Streams) and the setup dialog's problem text were held by no test;
`EachRowsReadyMarkIsInTheStatusColourOfItsState` (a ready, a blocking and an idle row) and a colour assertion in
`TypingAnInvalidPatternShowsTheProblemAndHoldsOk` hold them now. One mutant (Legacy Chapter 10 back to a box) did not compile, because
a tag has two ends; it became "no longer bound", which is caught.

**Baselines:** app **622 passed / 0 failed / 34 not run** (was 616: the anatomy theory (two cases), the status-follows-the-theme
test, the log's theme test, the switches test and the ready marks' test are new). Native and managed unchanged.
