#### Three app error paths that threw or said nothing

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit, by reading. Each has a test that fails against the old behaviour (restored as mutants
E1, O1 and C1 below, since the fixes were written beside their tests).

- **Apply Template with the core missing threw out of its command.** `NativeCore.EnsureLoaded()` and the check of the files
  (the first thing to need the core, after a template and recordings are chosen) sat outside the handler that Open, Import CSV
  and the batch have, so as a first action with a missing or mismatched `tmdq_core.dll` the `AsyncRelayCommand` faulted and
  nothing said why. It now says "The processing core could not be loaded: ..." in the status line and the log and asks nothing
  more. The message is `MainWindowViewModel.CoreNotLoaded`, one constant where it was typed three times.
- **An exception the run's observer threw was kept and never read.** The core's bridge catches what an observer method throws,
  so a run goes on, and the first one waits on `ProcessingRun.ObserverException`; the app never looked, so a completed stream
  whose report failed to be handled (the log, the status) left no trace. `StreamsRun.Run` now reads it once the run has ended
  and reports it as an error of the run, "A report from the core could not be handled: ...", in the outcome's errors (so in
  the status line) and the log.
- **The status line's numbers used the machine's culture.** `Describe` formatted the mean lock with `{mean:F1}` and the counts
  through the current culture, so on a comma-decimal machine "33,3 %" ended the smoke report that other tools read (the
  packaging scripts read only its invariant prefix, so no shipped file was wrong; the tests would have failed there). It is
  invariant now, as every other number the app writes.

**Not done, and why:** the audit's fourth item, `run.GetResult()` in `ExtractCalibrationViewModel` sitting outside its `try`, is
left. The calibration run is a static call on the binding and `GetResult()` throws only for a native out-of-memory or an
internal error, so there is no seam to make it fail, and a catch with no test is the kind of line the mutation check exists to
refuse. It wants either such a seam or a decision that the guard is worth carrying untested.

**Checked:** three new app cases (`TemplateBatchTests.ApplyTemplateWithoutTheNativeCoreSaysSoAndStops`,
`ProcessingTests.AReportTheObserverCouldNotHandleIsSaidNotDropped`,
`ConfigureStreamsTests.TheStatusIsWrittenTheSameInEveryCulture`). `eng\mutate.ps1` with `eng/mutants/app-error-paths.json`
(app, 8): **7 CAUGHT and 1 COMPILE** (the batch going on after a missing core, which the compiler refuses because the checks
are unassigned). Native, managed and the shipped smoke report are unchanged.

App baseline **619 passed, 34 not run** (was 616; 653 in all).

#### Nothing leaves the ABI as an exception; the ABI's duplicated pieces are one

The header promises "Nothing throws across the boundary", and four exports could break it (found by the whole-tree cleanup
audit, read from the code, not seen to fail from a host). A C++ exception unwinding into managed code is undefined, so each
now answers with a status or a last error.

- **`tmdq_run_wait` and `tmdq_calibration_wait`** join the run's driver thread, and `progress`, `log` (from the reader) and
  `finished` are all delivered on it, so a host that waited from one joined its own thread and `std::thread::join` threw.
  The header already forbade the call; now it returns at once with `exception in tmdq_run_wait: ...` as the last error. A
  wait from a stream's callback would still wait for itself, and the header says so.
- **`tmdq_chart_ticks` and `tmdq_chart_time_ticks`** built `max(2, count)` doubles with no guard, so a large count threw
  `std::bad_alloc`. A count above **65,536** (more ticks than a chart has pixels; the app asks for under ten) is now refused
  with -1 and "a tick count above 65536 is not an axis", before anything is built, and the call is guarded as well. This is
  the one narrowing of a documented contract here (the header's line for the two says so); the ABI revision is unchanged.
- **`tmdq_stream_key_equal`** copies two labels into strings and is guarded now (out-of-memory only).
- **`tmdq_chart_geometry_indexed`** reported its exceptions under its sibling's name, `tmdq_chart_geometry`.
- **Written once:** `toMetricType` (it was in `abi_formats.cpp` and `abi_series.cpp`, verbatim, with its `static_assert`s
  beside only one copy) and `kCallbacksMinimum` (`abi_run.cpp`, `abi_calibration.cpp`) are in `abi_internal.h`; the
  calibration outcome, a bare `static_cast` before, is held to the ABI's numbering by `static_assert`s as the metric is.

**Checked:** three native cases, each red against the old code: a run and a calibration waited on from their own `finished`
callback (the test sees the exception that used to leave, and the last error that replaces it), and a tick count at and
over the bound. `eng\mutate.ps1` with `eng/mutants/abi-boundary-guards.json` (native, 10): **8 CAUGHT, 1 COMPILE** (the ABI's
outcome renumbered, which the new asserts refuse) **and 1 equivalent survivor**: the ticks' result mapped to 0 instead of -1
when guarded code throws, which nothing can reach with the bound in front. The key compare's guard has no test of its own
(only an out-of-memory throws there). Not changed: the other ABI boilerplate the audit listed (the repeated "null output or
a struct_size that is too small" text, the index-wrap cast).

Native baseline **495 test cases** (was 492; 1 skipped). Managed and app unchanged.

#### The packet reader no longer crashes on a TMATS source that lacks a field

Found by the whole-tree cleanup audit and confirmed by a test that crashed before the fix. `Ch10PacketReader::prepare()`
sets up each data source of the recording's TMATS, and read two of its fields unchecked: `szEnabled[0]` (CHE-n, "channel
enabled") and `szChannelDataType` (CDT-n, handed to `strcasecmp`). The vendored decoder leaves a field the TMATS does not
carry NULL, and `Chapter10Reader` deliberately copes with that (a missing CHE-n counts as enabled, a missing CDT-n gives a
channel no type), so Configure Streams could offer a stream from such a recording and the run then died with a
segmentation fault in `prepare()`, for any data source in the file, not only the one asked for. The five committed
recordings carry both fields on every source, so nothing exercised it.

- **The data type is compared only when present.** A source with no CDT-n gets no attributes, so it is not taken for PCM:
  a stream asked of it is refused with the existing "Unable to load PCM attributes for channel N." A time source with no
  CDT-n, or any source with no CHE-n, no longer matters to a PCM stream.
- **`SuChanInfo::bEnabled` and `uChID` are deleted.** The first was the field read unchecked, and nothing read either:
  the reader never refused a disabled channel, and the metadata reader decides what is listed.
- **`freeChanInfoTable` is unchanged.** Its own comparison is reached only for a source that was given attributes, which
  now means one whose data type is present and PCMIN.
- **`test_support.h` takes `firstPacketLength` and `writePatchedStepCal`** from `test_chapter10reader.cpp`, so the packet
  reader's test edits step_cal's TMATS the same way (same-length key renames) instead of a second copy of the helper.

**Checked:** `Ch10PacketReader: a data source TMATS does not fully describe is not a crash` runs four edited copies of
`step_cal` (the PCM source without CHE-n, the time source without CHE-n, the time source without CDT-n, the PCM source
without CDT-n) and requires the first three to set up and read exactly the unedited recording's packets and the last to be
refused with its message. Written and run against the unchanged reader first: a segmentation fault on the first row.
`eng\mutate.ps1` with `eng/mutants/packet-reader-optional-fields.json` (native, 4): **all CAUGHT**: the data type compared
unchecked (a crash), a missing type taken for PCM, the refusal's message losing its channel, the data source not kept.

Native baseline **492 test cases** (was 491; 1 skipped). Managed and app unchanged.

#### The theme in Fluent's vocabulary: semantic tokens, Segoe UI Variable, Fluent's type scale and corners

Asked for after #272: keep the VS Code look, but base it on Fluent UX, especially for the dialogs. This is the first of two
steps (the second is the dialogs' own layout: spacing, footer and button bar, default and cancel keys, switches). The
colours are unchanged to the pixel; what changes is how they are named and used, and the font, the type scale and the
corners the application draws with.

- **Colours as Fluent's semantic tokens.** WinUI's token names do not exist in Avalonia's Fluent theme (it has the older
  `SystemControl*` and `System*Color` names), so the application defines them: a `Color` each in the Light and Dark theme
  dictionaries, and the `Brush` over it (`SolidBackgroundFillColorBaseBrush`, ...). They replace #272's ad-hoc keys:

  | Token | Dark | Light | Was | Used for |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `SolidBackgroundFillColorBase` | `#181818` | `#F8F8F8` | `ChromeBackground` | the window, title bar, log |
  | `LayerFillColorDefault` | `#1F1F1F` | `#FFFFFF` | `ContentBackground` | the chart, every dialog |
  | `CardBackgroundFillColorDefault` | `#202020` | `#F8F8F8` | the tooltip's own | widgets |
  | `ControlFillColorDefault` | `#313131` | `#FFFFFF` | its brushes' own | inputs, dropdowns, empty checkbox |
  | `ButtonFillColorDefault` / `Hover` | clear / `#2B2B2B` | `#E5E5E5` / `#CCCCCC` | the button's own | the secondary button |
  | `ControlStrokeColorDefault` | `#3C3C3C` | `#CECECE` | its brushes' own | an input's, a popup's and a chip's border |
  | `DividerStrokeColorDefault` | `#2B2B2B` | `#E5E5E5` | `Hairline` | the lines between the panes |
  | `SurfaceStrokeColorDefault`, `ButtonStrokeColorDefault` | `#313131`, 10 % white | `#E5E5E5`, 10 % black | their own | the loading label's, the button's border |
  | `SubtleFillColorSecondary` | 22 % grey | 22 % grey | `TitleBarHover` | the title bar's buttons under the pointer |
  | `TextFillColorPrimary` / `Secondary` | `#CCCCCC` / `#9D9D9D` | `#3B3B3B` / `#616161` | the chips' own; `Opacity="0.7"` | text; hints and headers |
  | `AccentFillColorDefault`, `AccentTextFillColorPrimary` | `#0078D4`, `#4DAAFC` | `#005FB8`, `#005FB8` | `SashHover`, `ChipAccent` | the divider under the pointer; links and the chips' accent |

  The brushes Fluent looks its controls up under (`TextControl*`, `ComboBox*`, `Button*`, `CheckBox*`, `MenuFlyoutPresenter*`,
  `ToolTip*`: 27 of them) and the chips' and loading label's five are now aliases of these, never colours of their own, so a
  token changed changes every control on it. `ButtonFillColorDefault` and `Hover`, and the translucent chip and loading
  fills, are the only colours with no WinUI name.
- **Segoe UI Variable Text**, Windows 11's Fluent font, is `ContentControlThemeFontFamily`: Fluent's own controls, every
  window, the log and the plot's text (and so an exported image's) take it. Avalonia's theme asks for Inter, which this
  application does not bundle, so until now it fell back to the system's Segoe UI: the change is the optical-sized
  variable face (a few pixels of width, a little lighter), and the font is no longer left to a fallback. Where Segoe UI

#### The pan and zoom keys draft a heavy plot too

The draft below came with the wheel and a drag only; the keyboard's pans and zooms (the arrows, `+` and `-`) stepped a
heavy plot in full each time, and a held key repeats. Now a key bound to one of those four commands is a step of a
gesture too: while it is held a heavy plot is drafted, and its release paints the full picture at once, as a released
drag does. Which keys count is read from `PlotView`'s key bindings, the one place that maps keys to commands, so a key
rebound there follows; only a command that can run counts. `Home`, `Backspace` and `R` jump once and are not drafted.
`PlotView` watches the keys on their way down, handled or not (the bound ones arrive handled), and calls the chart's
`Moving`, now internal.

Checked: `PlotDraftTests` holds each of the five bindings (the arrows, `+` with and without Shift, `-`) drafted while
repeating and settled by its own release and not another key's, the three jumps never drafted, and a pan key pressed with
nothing plotted leaving no draft behind when data arrives. `eng\mutate.ps1` with `eng/mutants/plot-draft-keys.json`
(app, 7): all CAUGHT, among them the left arrow or `+` not a step, every bound key a step (K3, caught by `Home` and `R`;
`Backspace` cannot catch it, since its binding has already run and Zoom Back has nothing left to undo by the time the
view sees the key, which is why only a pan or zoom key's command, which can always run with data, is asked), any key
going up settling the gesture, and the handler missing the keys that arrive handled. The kept `plot-draft.json` still
matches the code. App suite 604 passed with 34 not run (the baseline moves from 595); nothing native or managed changed.

#### A large plot stays responsive while it is panned or zoomed

The user found the plot sluggish on large datasets. Measured first, on the largest recording on the development machine
(`prn_agc_testfile, full.ch10`, 4.9 GB: five streams at 10 ms, 52 series shown, 406,000 samples each, 21 million in
all), Release core, pinned to the performance cores, 1600 x 900: a full-view frame took 359 ms, of which 280 ms was the
core walking every sample in view to build each pixel column's envelope, 69 ms Skia, and under 2 ms marshalling, the
legend and the axes together. A pan ran at 3 frames a second zoomed out and 16 at 1 % of the span; the wheel at 6.
The chart already drew dense series from a per-column min/max band and mean, culled to the view and cached between
frames (none of that had been lost in the port); what it lacked was a way to build the envelope without visiting every
sample, and a cheaper picture while a gesture is in flight.

- **A series' index** (`chart::SeriesIndex`, ABI revision 3: `tmdq_series_index_*`, `tmdq_chart_geometry_indexed`;
  `SeriesIndex` in the binding). A pyramid of each 32-sample block's minimum, maximum and sum, built once per long
  series (about 1.5 bytes a sample; 35 ms for all 52 series above). A column's envelope is the samples at its two ends
  plus a handful of blocks, so a frame costs time in proportion to the plot's width, not to the samples in view. It
  draws exactly the walked envelope's columns and band (the transform to pixels is monotonic, so a column's extreme
  pixels are the pixels of its extreme values) and its mean line to rounding (the largest difference over the
  generated series was 3e-11 px). A one-sample dropout is still its column's minimum. `PlotChart` builds an index for
  each ordered series of 4096 samples or more the first time it draws it, and frees it when the series goes.
- **A draft while a gesture moves a heavy plot.** While the wheel or a drag moves a plot whose last full paint took
  longer than 30 ms, the data layer is painted without the bands' fill and with every line one device pixel wide, which
  Skia draws as a hairline, without its stroker (the 1.5 px mean lines alone were 32 ms of the 69). The draft is still
  each column's minimum to maximum outline, so dropouts and spikes stay visible. The full picture is painted when a drag
  is released or 150 ms after the last wheel notch. A light plot (the full PRN recording's four series paint in 8 ms) is
  never drafted, and an export is never a draft.

Only what is drawn changed: the series, the readout and the CSV are untouched. Before and after, on the recording
above, in a real window, the two builds run alternately (a game was running on the machine throughout, so both sides
share its load; two runs each):

| Gesture | Before | Index only | Index and draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pan at 85 % of the span | 3.1 fps | 10.0-10.3 fps | 23-25 fps |
| Pan at 50 % | 4.5 | 11.3-11.4 | 28 |
| Pan at 10 % | 10.7 | 14.1-14.3 | 31-32 |
| Pan at 1 % | 15 | 15 | 32-33 |
| Wheel zoom in and out from the whole span | 5.9 | 12.3 | 27-28 |
| A full-view frame painted in full | ~320 ms | 90-94 ms | (the full picture after a gesture) |
| The core's envelopes for all 52 series, full view | 288-293 ms | 16-17 ms | |

The cursor's readout is unchanged (33-40 fps before, 36 after, with the game running; 158 fps before it started).
Below 0.1 % of the span a series is no longer drawn from its envelope and nothing changed there.

Checked: the native suite compares the looked-up envelope with the walked one over 1,500 generated series (up to 200,000
samples, with dropouts, repeated times, jumps in time and upside-down plot areas) and the index's summaries with a walk
over every run of short series; the ABI and the binding are held to the core; `PlotDraftTests` renders the draft and the
full picture (a dropout reaching the bottom of the plot in both, the fill gone and the lines thinner in the draft), the
release and the delay settling a gesture, only the last step's delay counting, an export during a draft being the full
picture, and each long series' index (built, used, kept through a shift of the times, freed).

Checked with `eng\mutate.ps1`, the lists kept in `eng/mutants/`. `plot-envelope-index.json` (native, 23): 21 CAUGHT,
among them the index used for out-of-order times or of the wrong size, each end of a run's blocks rounded the wrong way,
either odd node or a pair's sum dropped, a run not cut at a dropout, the column end guessed without the forward
transform's check (N13), and the band's edges taken in the values' order on an upside-down plot area (N15, caught once
the generator made such areas). Two SURVIVED, both equivalent and marked so: N11 (a node holding a non-finite value is
never read whole) and N14 (always searching rather than trusting a checked guess finds the same column end; only speed
differs). `plot-index-binding.json` (managed, 4): all CAUGHT. `plot-draft.json` (app, 17): 15 CAUGHT, among them never
drafting, a draft keeping its fill or its 1.5 px line (caught by `ADraftsLinesAreAPixelWide`, written for it), a
released drag left drafted, an earlier step's delay settling a later one (`OnlyTheLastStepsDelaySettlesTheGesture`,
written for it), and the index built but not drawn from (`ALongSeriesIsDrawnFromItsIndex`, written for it). Two
SURVIVED, equivalent at the 100 % scaling the headless suite renders at, where a device pixel is a logical one: a
draft's band edge (A5) and its line width (A6) at 1 logical pixel instead of one device pixel. The side-by-side soak (`eng\run_soak.ps1`): all 34 runs exported what v2.14.2 exported, byte for byte.

Baselines: native 491 test cases (1 skipped), managed 364 passed / 1 skipped, app 595 passed with 34 not run.

#### The run-log tests assert only the order the core promises

`ProcessingTests.TheRunLogsTheJobLinesThenTheSummaryThenWhatTheRunSays` failed once in a full app-suite run (2026-11-13):
it expected the reader's "Reading Chapter 10 file..." straight after the summary, and got the stream's
"[CH 26 RCVR] processing..." there. The test was wrong, not the core. The core keeps each source's lines in order (the
reader's, each stream's) but not one source's against another's: `tmdq_abi.h` and `pipelinerunner.h` say so, and
`FrameProcessor::streamTag` exists because the streams' lines interleave differently from run to run. `PipelineRunner::drive`
starts the stream threads before the reader, so that each is already waiting on its queue, and each logs its first line
straight away. v2.14.2's `ProcessingCoordinator` did the same ("Start workers first so they are waiting before the reader
produces"). The reader's first line came first only because the reader usually wins. Making that order a guarantee
would mean holding every stream until the reader has spoken, for a line nobody depends on, so the core is unchanged.

- `TheRunLogsTheJobLinesThenTheSummaryThenWhatTheRunSays` now asserts that after the job line and the summary, the
  reader's first line and the stream's first line each appear exactly once, in either order, and that the stream's
  completed line follows its first line. `pipelinerunner.h` documents that order: a stream's result is reported after
  its last line.
- `TheLogTellsTheStoryOfARunAsV214Did` had the same assumption (`lines[12]`) and now asserts the reader's line once
  after the summary.

Checked with `eng\mutate.ps1` on the app suite's `ProcessingTests` (the list is kept as `eng/mutants/run-log-order.json`).
R1 holds the reader's first line back 300 ms, so the stream always speaks first: on `main` it is CAUGHT by both old
tests, which reproduces the failure every time; with the new assertions it SURVIVES, as it should. R2 holds the stream's
line back instead and also SURVIVES. CAUGHT: the reader's line misworded (M1) or logged twice (M2), what the threads
said while the run was starting logged before the summary (M3), no line for a completed stream (M4), and the stream's
first line misworded (M5). App suite 586 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, 34 not run: no baseline moved.

#### The window as it opens: v2.14.2's size and empty grid, a divider that shows, no status bar

The window as it opens, compared side by side with v2.14.2 built from its tag, and the log sidebar's resizing.

- **The empty chart draws its grid again.** Before a recording was processed, v3 drew the chart's frame and labels
  but no grid, ticks or tick labels: ticks come from the core, which is loaded only once a recording opens (plan step
  4.3b recorded the choice). v2.14.2 drew them from its default range. The empty chart now draws its own: the dotted
  grid, 10 by 6, evenly across the plot area, the tick marks on both axes, and the left axis's values (0.0 to 100.0)
  beside its ticks (`PlotChart.DrawEmptyTicks`). The time axis has its marks but no labels: v2.14.2's read
  "000:00:00:00" nine times and "000:00:00:01" once, an accident of its 0 to 1 second default range.
- **The log wraps to the width it is dragged to.** The log panel had a 400 px minimum of its own, and its column none,
  so the divider dragged the column narrower than the panel: the panel stayed 400 wide, centred in the column and cut
  off at both edges, its text wrapped as before (measured: at a 250 px column the panel was 400 wide at x = -74). The
  minimum is now the column's, 200 px (`MainWindow.LogMinWidth`), lifted while the sidebar is hidden so the column can
  close; the panel takes its column's width and the text re-wraps to it.
- **The divider shows where to drag.** It was a 4 px transparent strip, found only by the cursor changing over it. It
  is now 6 px with a short grip (2 x 36) in its middle, a shade off the window's background; under the pointer, or
  dragged, the strip takes a shade and the grip brightens. New theme brushes `SplitterGrip`, `SplitterGripHover` and

#### The sidebar toggle's glyph is centred in its button

The title bar's sidebar toggle drew its glyph in the button's top-left corner, not centred as the menu button's is. The
title bar's `Button` styles centre their content, and in Avalonia a `ToggleButton` is not matched by a `Button`
selector. So the toggle kept the theme's stretched content: its glyph's text box was the whole 30 x 26 button, and the
glyph drew from its corner.

- **`MainWindow.axaml`:** the toggle centres its content itself. Its glyph box is now 15 x 15 at (8, 6), where the menu
  button's is (measured after layout; it was 30 x 26 at (0, 0)).
- **Tests:** `TheTitleBarIsTheApplicationsOwnAndTellsWindowsWhatEachPartIs` now holds every title-bar button's glyph
  smaller than its button and centred in it. Mutation check (`eng\mutate.ps1`, app suite): the fix undone, centred
  across only, and aligned left were all CAUGHT (3 of 3). App baseline unchanged (the case was extended, not added).
- **The manual:** the four figures that show the title bar were re-rendered (`eng\build_manual.ps1`) and the manuals
  re-embedded: `walk-app-01-hamburger`, `walk-err-01-log-error`, `walk-fs-04-processing` and
  `walk-theme-01-light-plot`. Below their title bars only the run log's progress percentages and elapsed times
  differ, which vary between captures (#259). `walk-cust-02-snr-tree` was restored: its only change was the known
  two-pixel variation.

#### VS Code runs the application on the Release core

Processing in the application run from VS Code took about three times as long as v2.14.2. The application itself was
not the cause. VS Code's only launch entry, "App (Debug)", builds the native core in Debug, and the app copies that
`tmdq_core.dll` (`out\Debug`) beside itself. The Debug core is unoptimised.

Timed on the full PRN recording's first stream (`TMDQ_SMOKE_REPORT`, the real exe, unpinned, five rounds each,
alternating), on an i7-14700KF:

| Build | Time |
|---|---|
| Release core, CET on (what ships) | 4.35 s |
| Release core, `CETCompat=false` (as v2.14.2 ran) | 4.14 s |
| Debug core | about 14 s |

The 5% between the first two is the CET shadow stack, as the soak measured (`docs/records/soak.md`).

- **`.vscode/launch.json`:** a new first entry, "App (Release)", runs `bin\Release` after a new task, "Build app
  (Release)" (`.vscode/tasks.json`), which builds the core and the app in Release. "App (Debug)" stays, for stepping
  through the C#, and the file's header says which entry to use.
- **Checked:** the new task's command, run from a shell with no developer prompt, builds the Release core and the app,
  and puts the 666 KB Release `tmdq_core.dll` beside the exe, not the 2.8 MB Debug one. That exe processes the
  recording to the same result. No code changed, so no suite or mutation check applies.

### v3.1.0 — Clean-up, and v2.x's preferences no longer imported

The first release after the move off Qt: the application gains its icon (v3.0.0 shipped without one), the plot's keys act
only when pressed alone, the manual's figures show this version, and the one-time import of v2.x's preferences
goes, as planned for after 3.0.x. Underneath, the repository is in its final layout (`src/`, `tests/`, `eng/`,
`third_party/`), the application in MVVM's usual shape, and the Qt-era leftovers cleared.

#### A build outside a developer prompt finds mt.exe

Building in VS Code (its C# tools run a plain `dotnet build`) failed with MSB3073, exit code 9009: the targets that
merge the UTF-8 code-page manifest into the app's hosts and the managed test exe ran a bare `mt`, which is on PATH only
in a Visual Studio developer prompt (the repository's scripts make one with `eng\env.ps1`, which is why they worked).

- **`eng\WindowsSdkTools.targets`** (new, imported by `Directory.Build.targets` into every `.csproj`): `TmDqFindMt`
  looks for `mt.exe` where the Windows SDK installs it (`bin\<version>\x64` under the registry's `KitsRoot10`), the
  newest version, and falls back to `mt` on PATH. The four manifest targets in `TmDq.App.csproj` and
  `TmDq.Core.Tests.csproj` depend on it and run `$(TmDqMt)`.
- **Checked:** with `mt` not on PATH, `dotnet build` of the app, both test projects and a single-file `dotnet publish`
  all succeed (they failed with 9009 before), and the published exe carries the UTF-8 code page; the managed and app
  suites pass, `ManifestTests` included, which assert the code page in the built exes.

#### v2.x's preferences are no longer imported

v3.0.0 read the Qt application's INI file on its first run, so an upgrade from v2.x kept the theme, the sidebar and
legend choices, the recent files and the last folders. `docs/claude.md` planned to keep that import through the 3.0.x
releases and then drop it; 3.1.0 drops it.

- `QtSettingsImport` and `QtIni` (about 250 lines) and `PreferencesStore.QtFileName` are gone; `PreferencesStore.Load`
  reads this application's `preferences.json` or starts from the defaults. An INI file v2.x left in the folder is not
  read and not touched.
- **Upgrading from v2.x now starts from the default preferences** (dark theme, sidebar and legend shown, no recent
  files). The settings files under `settings\` are kept as before; only the window preferences are not carried over.
- The installer's clean-machine check (`deploy\sandbox\verify_avalonia_install.ps1`) still installs v2.14.2 with its INI
  file and upgrades it; it now checks that the first run wrote the defaults and left the INI file as it was.
- **Tests:** the importer's tests and their three QSettings fixtures went with it; a new case holds that a v2.x INI file
  is left alone and the first run starts from the defaults. App baseline 613 -> **577 passed** / 0 failed, 34 not run
  (the importer's 37 cases out, one in).

Checked: mutation check, 3 mutants, all **caught** (an INI file read again on the first run; the first run's defaults
not written; the INI file deleted rather than left alone).

#### Pre-release tidy: stale guidance, dead code and Qt-era leftovers

A whole-repository audit before 3.1.0 (the native core, the .NET projects, the scripts, docs and ignore files, and
GitHub). Nothing behaves differently.

- **Guidance that steered wrong:** `tm-code-review` said frame-sync Load/Save keeps `Randomized` out (it round-trips,
  with `Inverted`, as `.claude/CLAUDE.md` says), named files that are gone, and called a packet's payload a copy-on-write
  `QByteArray` (it is a shared, read-only `std::vector<uint8_t>` a worker copies before changing). `cut-release` still
  named `build_release.ps1` and the Qt build's derived version files. `code-cleanup` cited guidance that does not exist.
- **Comments in the core** that named classes v3 does not have (`ProcessingCoordinator`, the C++ `MainViewModel`,
  `PlotViewModel::addStreamData`, `TestStepDetector`) now name what does the job (`PipelineRunner`, `buildStreamJob`,
  `buildStreamSeries`, `CsvSeriesWriter`, the native tests). `stepdetector.h` no longer says `TomlDocument` has no
  arrays (the step file is read through its `tables("step")`), and `ChannelData::channelCount` says what it counts now.
  Checked: every changed native source is identical to before with its comments removed.
- **Docs:** `SNR_logic.md` names `buildStreamJob`; the template and multi-file design notes say they were written for
  v2.x and where the code is now; the future-plans table says its paths are of their day; `eng\ch10_triage.py` and
  `.pymarkdown.json` are documented in `docs/claude.md`'s tooling list.
- **Dead code:** `PlotViewModel.XMin` and two unused constants in `PlotCommands`; `LegendLabel` uses `ChannelLabel`
  instead of repeating it; `SetSeries`' and `LegendVisible`'s comments say what is true now. The three Qt-era INI
  fixtures (`tests/fixtures/test_framesetup*.ini`), which nothing read, are deleted.
- **Ignore files:** `deploy/.gitignore` re-included two deleted files and not the release notes or the portable
  README, which were tracked only because they predate its rule; the root, `tests/` and `.claude/.claudeignore` rules
  for the Qt build (`build/`, `debug/`, `release/`, Makefiles, `version_autogen.h`, the generated solution) are gone,
  and `.claudeignore` lists the v3 build output instead.
- **Outside the repository:** the retired self-hosted runner's 357 `test-results-self-hosted` artifacts were deleted
  from GitHub, and the Qt build output and old packages (about 1.4 GB) from the development machine.

#### The manual's figures the same in every capture, and re-captured for 3.0.0

`ManualFiguresTests` made some figures differently from one capture to the next, so a re-capture changed figures whose
subject had not changed. Rendering every figure several times found five causes:

- **The log's clock** (the main window's figures): it now reads one fixed time (`FigureClock`), not the run's.
- **Paths** that differ by checkout and by run, and that put the user's name in the manual: the Export dialog showed the
  repository's folder, the batch confirmation a scratch folder named for the run. Both now show `D:\Flight Tests`.
- **Animations** caught part way (the Customize View tree's chevrons, a check box's colour): a capture now draws the
  window again, time and frames apart, until two drawings in a row match, and fails if it never settles.
- **The text caret**, which blinks on the clock (Set Time Window): figure windows hide it.
- **What stays the run's own:** the log of a real run, where the streams are processed in parallel, so the order they
  start in, the percentages read and the seconds elapsed vary. That touches the four figures with that log in view.
  One check box's corner in the Customize View tree also differs by a few pixels' shade between processes (never
  within one); its cause was not found.

**The re-capture also brought the manual up to 3.0.0:** the main window's figures still showed "v2.14.2" in the log
and "Version 2.14.2" in the status bar, having been rendered before the version changed. Eight figures changed (the
Export dialog, the batch confirmation, Set Time Window, the Customize View tree, and the four with a run's log); the
other nineteen render byte for byte as before. Checked by rendering every figure five times, in Release as the manual
build does, and comparing each with the others; the Debug suite passes too.

#### The menus, the chips and the keys declared in AXAML and bound

The last of the three steps that bring the application to MVVM's usual shape. The menus look exactly as they did: the
manual's menu figures render byte for byte as committed.

- **The plot's right-click menu, its chips and its keys** are declared in `PlotView.axaml` (a `ContextMenu` on the
  chart, the chip bar, `KeyBindings` on the view's root) and bound to `PlotCommands`, which became their view model: a
  command for each item, chip and key, each unable to run without data (the item disabled, the key passed on); what
  the chips and the menu show; and Plot File's and Readout's entries. The view makes it for its plot with its prompts
  and lets the old one go when the plot changes. `PlotView` no longer builds the menu each time it opens
  (`BuildContextMenu`) or reads keys itself (`OnKeyDown`); its code-behind keeps the legend, and the menu's Opening,
  where a readout pin gone stale is dropped as before.
- **The hamburger menu** is declared in `MainWindow.axaml` and bound to `MainWindowViewModel`, its icons as dynamic
  resources; Help and Exit, which act on the window, are click handlers. `BuildMenu` is gone, and
  `MainWindow.NoRecentFiles` is now `MainWindowViewModel.NoRecentFiles`.
- **Menus filled from the data** (Recent Files, Plot File, Readout) are lists of `MenuChoice` (new, in `ViewModels`),
  shown through the `MenuChoice` and `RadioChoice` item themes in `App.axaml`; a choice headed `-` is drawn as the
  separator, as Avalonia draws such an item. Plot File's and Readout's lists are made again only when their entries
  change, so an open menu's items are never replaced under the pointer.
- **One change a user can notice: a plot key now acts only bare.** It used to ignore the modifiers, so Ctrl+R reset
  the view and Ctrl+L toggled the legend; now those go on to the window, like any key the plot does not use. `+` still
  works with Shift, which is how most keyboards type it, and the keypad's `+` and `-` still zoom. Backspace with no
  zoom to step back from now goes on to the window too (it did nothing there either way).
- **Tests:** a helper (`Menus`) reads the menus open, as the user sees them: the plot's menu opened by a context
  request, as a right-click opens it (`ContextMenu.Open` alone does not raise its Opening), and a submenu opened before
  its items are read (closed, an item does not follow its command, and a list's items do not exist). The cases that
  read the built menus read the declared ones; new ones hold that a key with Ctrl does nothing and Shift with `+`
  zooms, that a view's commands let go of a plot replaced and take prompts set later, that a view with no plot has no
  menu, no chip bar and no "Loading...", and that Plot File's separator is drawn as one. `CommandExtensions` (test
  code, used only by the old Plot File case) is gone.

#### No brushes in the view models, and a test that holds the layers apart

The second of the three steps that bring the application to MVVM's usual shape. Nothing looks or behaves differently.

- **The view models make no brushes.** Customize View's rows, receivers and channels report their `Color`; the batch
  confirmation's rows already reported whether a file matches; Extract Calibration already reported each status's
  kind. The windows paint them through three converters in `Views/StatusBrushes.cs`, with the same colours as before
  (v2.x's green, goldenrod, red and gray). `GlyphBrush`, `StepBrush`, `CalBrush`, `BrushOf` and the three `Brush`
  properties are gone.
- **Avalonia's `Color` stays** in the series, the plot's prompts and the template file: a plain four-byte value, and
  templates read colour text through its parser. Replacing it was weighed and declined.
- **`TemplateBatch`, a model, no longer takes the plot.** Its `Build` and `ApplyAppearance`, which read and change the
  `PlotViewModel`, moved unchanged to `ViewModels/Plot/PlotTemplates.cs`.
- **`LayerTests`** reads every model, view model and service type as compiled: its signatures and the types and
  members its methods' code names, the compiler's lambdas and state machines included. It fails on a model that reaches
  a view model, a service, a view or `Platform`; on a view model or service that reaches a view or `Platform`; and on
  any of them that reaches Avalonia beyond `Color` and `Colors`. A third case proves the reading sees what it must: a
  view's base type, and a type a picker names only inside its async code.
- **Tests:** the ones that read the old brushes read the colour, the match or the status instead, and check the
  converters' colours. Two now check the window as well: the batch confirmation's glyphs are green and red, and
  Customize View's receiver names are in their colours. A recoloured SNR channel now has to say so (`Color` changed).

Checked: mutation check (`eng\mutate.ps1`, a `C:\tmp` worktree), 12 mutants, all **caught**: a brush made inside a view
model's method, a brush back in a view model's signature, a model calling into a view model, a view model naming a
view, a model reaching Avalonia through a brush (`LayerTests`); the glyph colours swapped, the glyph's binding replaced
by a fixed colour, every swatch gray, the step line painted by the calibration file's status, a recolour not announced,
a receiver in its last channel's colour (the window and view-model tests); a template's colours not put back by the
moved `ApplyAppearance` (`TemplateTests`). App suite **612 passed / 0 failed**, 34 not run (was 608: `LayerTests`' three
cases and the batch window's glyph test).

#### The application in folders by MVVM layer

The first of three steps that bring the application to MVVM's usual shape. Files move and their namespaces follow
them; nothing behaves differently.

- **`Models/`** holds what has no UI: `Streams`, `Processing`, `Settings`, `Templates` and `Logging`, from the top of
  `src/TmDq.App`, now `TmDq.App.Models.*`.
- **`ViewModels/Plot/`** holds the plot's view models and their helpers, from `Plot/` (`TmDq.App.ViewModels.Plot`).
- **`Services/` holds the interfaces a view model asks the user through**, and `IPlotPrompts` (from `Plot/`) and
  `DialogConfigurator` (from `Processing/`) join them. Each interface shared a file with its Avalonia implementation,
  so the files view models use imported Avalonia and the views; none does now.
- **`Platform/`** (`TmDq.App.Platform`) holds those implementations, one a file: the `Storage*` file pickers, the
  `Window*` dialogs, `WindowPlotPrompts` and `PlotViewImageExporter`.
- `docs/claude.md` describes the layout, and the `add-stream-setting` skill names the new paths.

Left for the next steps: view models still make brushes, and `PlotSeries`, `IPlotPrompts` and the template's
`SeriesAppearance` carry Avalonia's `Color` (step 2); `TemplateBatch`, a model, takes the `PlotViewModel`.

Checked: each class moved out of a `Services` file compared with main's text, identical; every other changed line is a
using, a namespace or a name partly qualified by an old namespace (`Settings.RecentFiles`, `Logging.LogLevel`, a
cref). A build with unused-using (IDE0005) and doc-comment checks turned on reports nothing the move added. App suite
**608 passed / 0 failed**, 34 not run. No mutation check: no behaviour changed, and no test reads these paths.

The last of the three PRs that tidy the repository's layout. Files move; no code changes, beyond the paths that name

#### The application's icon

v3.0.0 shipped an exe with no icon: the Qt application's came from its `.rc` file, which the port left behind, so
Explorer, the taskbar, Alt+Tab, the shortcuts and every title bar showed a generic one.

- **`resources/icon.ico`** is square in every size Windows asks for (16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 256 px), made from the
  original artwork (`docs/design/icon_image.png`, centred on a square canvas) by the new `scripts/gen_app_icon.py`. It
  was one 64 by 61 image. The installer (`SetupIconFile`) takes the same file.
- **`TmDq.App.csproj`** sets `ApplicationIcon`; the SDK copies the assembly's resources into every host, single-file
  included, and the manifest merge (`mt.exe`) leaves them alone. Every window takes the same file as an Avalonia
  resource, through an `:is(Window)` style in `App.axaml`, for its title bar and Alt+Tab.
- **`IconTests`**: the file's sizes, its images byte for byte in the built exe's icon group, the windows' resource the
  same file, and every window kind showing it. **`build_avalonia_package.ps1`** reads the icon back out of the
  single-file published exe, as it does the manifest, and fails without it.

**Checked:** five mutants (`scripts\mutate.ps1`, a `C:\tmp` worktree), four caught; the fifth, a plain `Window`
selector, is equivalent, because `Window` gives every subclass its own style key (`StyleKeyOverride`). Rebased onto
the layout tidy, the artwork's new place in `docs/design/`, and the app suite run again. App baseline 608 passed / 0
failed, 34 not run (was 604).

#### The shared build files at the root, the finished docs in their own folders

The first of three PRs that tidy the repository's layout now the move off Qt is finished; this one moves no code.

- **`Directory.Build.props` and `Directory.Build.targets`** at the root import `dotnet/build/AppVersion.props` and
  `dotnet/build/PackageLicences.targets` into every .NET project, which imported them one by one. The rule "every
  project imports them" is now held by MSBuild rather than by each project, and it closes a gap it hid:
  `TmDq.Core.Tests` never imported the version (it built as 1.0.0). Both files apply only to `.csproj`; the native
  projects import them too and are left alone.
- **`PackageLicenceTests.EveryProjectInTheSolutionGetsTheCheckAndTheVersion`** replaces the test that read each
  `.csproj` for the import line: it asks MSBuild what each project evaluates to (`dotnet msbuild -getProperty`), the
  licence script and the version, so a project the root files miss fails whatever its text says.
- **`docs/design/`** holds the design notes of features that shipped (`processing-template-design.md`,
  `multi-file-input-design.md`, the Configure Streams wireframes, the icon's source image), and **`docs/records/`** gains
  the finished improvement plan (`IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md`, with a note saying so) and `ci_runner.md`. Every reference is
  repointed: `docs/claude.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/future_plans/README.md`, and comments in
  `seriescolumnschema` and `templatematcher.h`.

**Checked:** the core built in Debug and Release; every suite at its baseline (native 485 test cases, 1 skipped; managed
360 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped; app 604 passed / 0 failed, 34 not run); the release consistency check. Four mutants,
all caught by the new test: the targets' import removed, either root file's condition never true for a `.csproj`
(no check; every project at 1.0.0), and `TmDq.Core.Tests` opting out of the targets, which only the evaluation sees.
They were run by hand in a worktree, because `scripts\mutate.ps1` requires a rebuilt binary newer than the mutated
file, and a build file mutant changes none (the test reads what MSBuild evaluates, at run time).

#### TempFilesTests start the clock before the hold

Two timing checks (`AFileHeldForAMomentIsReadOnceItIsReleased`, `AFileHeldForAMomentIsDeletedOnceItIsReleased`) started
the thread that holds the file and then the stopwatch. The hold's 400 ms runs from the thread's start, so a stall between
the two made a correct wait measure short: 194 ms against the 300 ms floor on a busy CI runner (PR #252). The clock now
starts first, so the measured time is never less than the hold. Test only; `TempFiles` is unchanged.

**Checked:** the managed suite at its baseline (360 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped); three mutants against
`TempFilesTests`, all caught: `TempFiles` never retrying (six tests), and each test with a 0 ms hold (its own test), so
the 300 ms floor still catches a wait that did not happen.

#### The self-hosted runner removed

The runner CI used until plan step 6.4 (`tmdqa-selfhosted-1`) is off the development machine: its registration and
service, `C:\actions-runner`, and the `RUNNER_ADMIN_TOKEN` secret. `docs/ci_runner.md`, which said how to remove it, now
records that it was removed, how that was checked (GitHub lists no runner, no service, registry key or process is left,
the repository has no secrets), and that a self-hosted runner must not be registered again while the repository is
public. `docs/claude.md`'s CI paragraph says the same. Docs only: nothing builds or runs differently.

#### The guides rewritten, the plan and the spikes gone (plan step 6.5)

The last step of the move off Qt. Its three choices were the user's: the history moves to a file of its own, the parity
and soak records are kept, and the "plan step" references in the code stay, resolved through this changelog.

- **`docs/changelog.md`** is this history, moved verbatim out of `docs/claude.md`, whose Version History section it
  was (6,629 of its 7,442 lines). `scripts\check_release_consistency.ps1` reads the release's section and the
  Unreleased rule from it; `cut-release` turns Unreleased into the release's section there.
- **`docs/claude.md`** describes the code as it stays, in about 900 lines:
  - **the user stories' notes** name the app's types where they named the Qt application's (`TemplateBatch`,
    `BatchRunner`, `StreamRules.ApplyToAll`, `PlotView.OnKeyDown`, the tests that hold them);
  - **the reference sections** are rewritten: the architecture's three layers, each component as it is, the working
    method (the plan's rules, still how a change is made), and a test catalog that says what each suite covers, where
    it was the record of how each was ported.
- **`.claude/CLAUDE.md`:** the migration section is now "Docs and history" (a changelog entry with every change, what a
  "plan step" reference means); no Qt left but the version history's one line.
- **`docs/dotnet-migration/` is gone.** `parity.md` and `soak.md` are kept as records in `docs/records/`, each with a
  note saying so; the plan, its README, `presentation-layer.md` and the 18 renders are deleted (git keeps them).
- **The three spikes are deleted** (`dotnet/chart-spike`, `hybrid-spike`, `interop-spike`, 57 files). Nothing built
  them; the comments that cited them now say what they found.
- **`docs/future_plans/`:** the move off Qt was its one open item and graduates as its rule asks: the assessment
  (`dotnet-port-assessment.md`) is deleted and the index's Shipped table gains the row.
- **Also repointed:** the package script's, `mutate.ps1`'s, the app project's and `tmdq_abi.h`'s comments,
  `dotnet/.gitignore`'s note, `README.md`'s tree, `.pymarkdown.json`, and the `write-test` skill's rule references.

**What the plan said, for the references that remain.** Code comments cite its steps ("plan step 4.7"), decisions
("plan decision D3") and rules ("plan rule 5"). Each step has its section in this changelog; the decisions and rules
were the plan's own, so they are here.

- **Decisions:**
  - **D1.** The chart draws with Skia in Avalonia, from geometry the native core builds (culling, the per-pixel-column
    envelope); PNG, SVG and PDF come from the one drawing routine (decided in step 0.2, measured against Direct2D).
  - **D2.** The native tests use doctest, one vendored header.
  - **D3.** Anything that defines a file format or computes data is the native core's (the CSV, its columns, stream
    settings to a job, template matching, series construction and time re-basing); presentation state is C# (palette,
    visibility, axis ranges, zoom history, recent files, preferences). The template JSON is C#'s, tested against
    templates the Qt application wrote.
  - **D4.** The first Avalonia release is v3.0.0, with the last Qt release downloadable for one release cycle.
  - **D5.** No licensed Avalonia tooling and no Accelerate component: the framework is MIT, so the project stays
    GPL-3.0; `scripts/check_package_licences.ps1` enforces it.
- **Rules:** (1) the Qt application kept building and shipping until step 6.1, every step a PR on `main`; (2) tests
  first, on the old code, the old implementation kept as an oracle; (3) mutation-check every step; (4) a clean build
  before believing a result, zero warnings, the throughput gate on the decode path; (5) one implementation of every file
  format. Rules 2 to 5 are `docs/claude.md`'s Working Method now.
- **Steps:**
  - **0, groundwork:** 0.1 merge the exploration; 0.2 measure a Skia chart (D1); 0.3 the docs in line with it.
  - **1, Qt out of everything below the view:** 1.1 `SeriesColumnSchema`; 1.2 `CsvSeriesParser`; 1.3
    `TemplateMatcher`; 1.4 the frame-sync and receiver-parameter TOML helpers; 1.5 stream settings to a job; 1.6
    series construction and time re-basing; 1.7 the DTOs.
  - **2, the core as a product:** 2.1 `tmdq_core.dll` built from `main`; 2.2 the full C ABI (2.2a to 2.2d); 2.3 the C#
    library (2.3a to 2.3d); 2.4 the core's suites off Qt Test.
  - **3, the app's skeleton:** 3.1 projects and conventions; 3.2 CI for the app; 3.3 the packaging prototype; 3.4 a
    walking skeleton.
  - **4, parity, in the order a user meets the features:** 4.1 Configure Streams (4.1a its rules, 4.1b its dialogs);
    4.2 processing; 4.3 the chart (4.3a its geometry in the core, 4.3b the plot); 4.4 around the chart; 4.5 export and
    import; 4.6 calibration; 4.7 templates and batch; 4.8 the shell; 4.9 Help.
  - **5, switch over:** 5.1 the parity review; 5.2 the side-by-side soak; 5.3 release v3.0.0.
  - **6, retire Qt:** 6.1 delete the Qt application; 6.2 Qt out of the tooling; 6.3 Qt out of the names that stay; 6.4
    consolidate the new code; 6.5 this.

**Checked:** the core built Debug and Release; native 485 cases (1 skipped), managed 360 / 0 / 1, app 604 / 0 / 0 (34 not run), zero warnings: every baseline unchanged. The release check passes, and fails in release mode on this Unreleased section, so it reads the new file. Two hand mutants of the changelog, run in a worktree: the v3.0.0 heading renamed (`docs/claude.md` no longer has one to fall back on) and the file missing. **Both caught.**

#### CI is one job, on a hosted runner that has never had Qt (plan step 6.4)

The last item of 6.4. Every PR ran the build and the three suites twice: on the self-hosted runner, or the hosted
fallback when it was offline, and in `core-without-qt` beside either. The second run was there because the self-hosted
machine still has the Qt kit, so only a hosted image could show that nothing needs Qt. With the Qt application gone,
the hosted job is the only one, at the user's choice.

- **`ci.yml` is one job, `ci`, on `windows-2022`,** with the steps the jobs shared, in this order: the release
  consistency check, MSVC and .NET 10 set up, the toolchain's versions, the check that the machine has no Qt, the core
  in Debug and Release, then the native, managed and app suites. The job keeps the name of the old aggregate check, so
  a PR's status still reads `ci`.
- **On `windows-2022`, with Visual Studio 2022, which the job checks.** `windows-latest` now carries Visual Studio
  2026 (MSVC 14.51): this PR's first run built there, and so had every `core-without-qt` run. Only the self-hosted
  job built with the compiler `env.ps1` pins and releases use (VS 2022, MSVC 14.44). So the job runs on
  `windows-2022`, asks `msvc-dev-cmd` for 2022, and fails unless `VisualStudioVersion` is 17.0.
- **Gone:** `pick-runner`, its probe of the runner's status through `RUNNER_ADMIN_TOKEN`, `build-self-hosted`,
  `build-hosted`, and the aggregate job.
- **Faster, not slower:** the self-hosted runner ran one job at a time, so a PR's job waited behind main's. On #245
  the result came 15 minutes after the push; the hosted job alone takes about 11.
- **The self-hosted runner is retired.** `docs/ci_runner.md` now says how to remove the runner, its service and the
  secret, and keeps the lessons that still apply to the hosted job.
  - **It should be removed:** the repository is public, and a pull request from a fork runs the workflow from its own
    branch, so it could target a registered runner's labels. The old note allowed self-hosting only while the
    repository was private.
- **Stale comments corrected:** the throughput benchmark's case, its script and `tests/.gitignore` described CI
  overlaying the full PRN recording on the runner, which ended in 6.1.

**Checked by running it:** this PR's own CI is the one job. On `windows-latest` (the first run): no Qt found; native
485 cases (1 skipped), managed 360 / 0 / 1, app 604 / 0 / 0 (34 not run), zero warnings, 11 minutes. Then on
`windows-2022` with Visual Studio 2022.

#### `MainWindowViewModel`'s jobs in their own types, its services in one object (plan step 6.4)

The fifth item of 6.4. The main window's view model opened and imported, exported, saved and applied templates, ran
batches with their per-file export, and kept the preferences and Recent Files. Its constructor took eleven optional
services. The plan's three pieces are now types of their own in `dotnet/TmDq.App/ViewModels`. The file goes from 713
lines to 566, and nothing the window does changes.
- **`ShellPreferences`:** what the shell remembers between sessions: Recent Files, the theme, the sidebar, the last
  folder and the legend's choice, each change written at once. The view model forwards these properties and passes on
  their notices, so the window's bindings are unchanged.
- **`SessionExport`:** Export's writes, in v2.x's order, with their log lines. These are the data, the image and the log
  (CR LF, UTF-8 without a byte-order mark). A batch's per-file CSV and images go through it too.
- **`BatchRunner`:** Apply Template's loop over the files, and each file's CSV and images. It reaches the window through
  a small internal interface (`IRunHost`) for the status line, the file being run (named in the warning that a
  recording shares no time with the others), and a run with the progress dialog up. The view model keeps the busy
  guard, clearing the plot, the recordings kept, the summary and the core-not-loaded error.
- **`MainWindowServices`** replaces the eleven optional parameters. Each service is a property that says what leaving it
  out does (Open unavailable without a picker, and so on). Every construction now names what it hands in. That is 70
  in the tests, rewritten by a script that matched each named or positional argument to its property, and one in
  `App`.

**The members stay**, as forwards, so the tests that pin the window's behaviour run as they were, apart from how they
construct it.

**Mutation check** (`scripts\mutate.ps1`, the seven app test classes that drive the main window). There were 29
mutants, one or more for each new type:
- **`ShellPreferences`** (8): Recent Files changed without a notice; the theme's menu text not updated; the sidebar's,
  the legend's and the last folder's choices not remembered; a recent file kept as given rather than by its full path;
  Clear Recent Files clearing nothing; the shell's notices not passed on.
- **`SessionExport`** (7): the image written before the data; an export with no data; the log written with LF, or
  without a final line end; a batch file's CSV line reworded; the image format's name not in capitals; a batch with no
  image writer trying images.
- **`BatchRunner`** (7): a missing file not counted as skipped; the warning about a recording that shares no time with
  the others not naming it; the plot titled with the last file; the template's names and colours put back the wrong way
  round; the view not put back after the per-file images; the files left overlaid; the summary not saying where the
  output went.
- **The view model** (3): a batch's recordings not kept for Save as Template; a batch drawn onto the last run's plot;
  the status line not following the files.
- **`MainWindowServices`** (4): the configurator, the image exporter, the picker or the preferences handed in and
  ignored.

**27 were caught. Two survived, and both were gaps, now closed** by one test
(`WithNoImageWriterABatchExportsEachCsvAloneAndItsStatusNamesTheFileRunning`):
- **images tried with no image writer:** every image would be logged as failed, and no test ran a batch with an output
  folder and no writer;
- **the status line not following the files:** the summary replaces it when the batch ends, before any test read it.
  The test's progress dialog now notes the status each time it is shown: "Processing flight 1.ch10 ...", then
  flight 2's.

**Checked:** the soak, all 34 runs exporting byte for byte what v2.14.2 exported, the two template batches among them. App **604 / 0 / 0** (was 603), and 34 not run.

#### `PlotViewModel`'s four jobs in their own types (plan step 6.4)

The fourth item of 6.4. The plot's view model was ported from Qt whole, and it did four jobs beside holding the
series. Each is now a type of its own in `dotnet/TmDq.App/Plot`. `PlotViewModel` goes from 923 lines to 724, and nothing
the plot does changes.

  keys that move the window: the wheel and drag, a band, an entered window with its warnings, the arrow keys, + and -,
  Zoom Back and Reset Span.
- **`PlotReadout`:** what the crosshair's readout says, pinned or nearest within 10 px.
- **`PlotCsv`:** the series to the core's CSV writer, and a parsed file back into series as a run's would be.
- **`PlotColors.Assign`:** the colours, beside the shades they are made from.

**The public surface is unchanged.** `PlotViewModel` keeps every member as a one-line forward, so `PlotTests`,
`AroundTheChartTests` and the views run untouched. They were written against the old code, so they are the proof that
behaviour is unchanged. Moving the callers onto the new types would have rewritten those tests (about 260 lines).
**Also tidied:** two copies of the rule for which left-axis metric a new series shows (`ShownInView`), and two of the
span's computation (`SpanOf`).

**What stays on `PlotViewModel`, on purpose:**
- **The readout's pin and the loading flag:** they are properties the views bind to.
- **The clock** (`FormatTime`, `ParseTime`, `TimeOrigin`): it reads the time base, which belongs to the series.
- **The legend's rows.**

**Checked:**
- **Every suite:** app 603 / 0 / 0 with 34 not run, unchanged.
- **The soak** (`run_soak.ps1`, since the change touches the plot's series and the CSV path): all 34 runs exported
  byte for byte what v2.14.2 exported.
- **Mutation check** (`scripts\mutate.ps1`, against the plot's, the chart's, the export's and the templates' classes):
  26 mutants in the four new types and the view model's wiring to them. **All caught**, once three gaps were closed:
  - **The time window:** the history one short; a click taken as a band; an arrow key acting on the whole span; a stop
    before the start kept; a window moved off the start not counted as zoomed; Reset Span keeping the history; + past
    the narrowest band. Also: `SetSeries` and an imported CSV keeping the history, a window's warnings not passed on,
    and Plot File not showing the recording's span.
  - **The readout:** a pinned readout reading any series, and the missed frames' unit.
  - **The CSV:** source 0 exported with every source; an imported series not given the core's stream order; a CSV
    that cannot be written reported written.
  - **The colours:** the second stream already a shade, and receiver 1 taking the second primary.
- **Three gaps, closed in `PlotTests`.** None was opened by the split: the tests are as before, and so was the code they
  missed.
  - **A gesture past either end by less than a second:** the test went 20 s past at least, so a clamp that let up to
    1 s through survived, at either end.
  - **The two notices a move gives:** the chart and `PlotView` redraw on `RangesChanged` and on any property change
    alike, so dropping either notice changed nothing they did. The test now counts both, so a listener that relies on
    one notice is protected.
  - **The readout's reach:** the test probed 50 px from a sample only. It now reads a sample at 10 px and not one at
    15, which also holds the boundary.

The third item of 6.4. The port wrote the same test helpers in several classes, one step at a time. They are now in

**One thing it showed:** with the waiting configurator answering at once, `ARecentFileOpensByItsSuffixAndNotWhileBusy`
still passes. The open reads the recording's channels off the UI thread, so the window is busy before Configure Streams

#### A file the core has just written is read back through `TempFiles`

`FormatsTests.AWrittenCsvIsAnExactFileAndIsReadBackWithTheSameIdentities` failed CI four times in six runs on the
self-hosted runner, all on PRs #244 and #245, once with the machine idle. Each time it was the same `IOException`: the file
was in use when the test read back the CSV the core had just written. The core's writer had closed it already, so another
process held the new file for a moment, most likely the virus scanner in the runner account's temp folder.
`TempFiles` already waited out the same hold for deletes (PRs #218 and #221).

- **`TempFiles.ReadAllBytes` and `ReadAllText`** read as `File`'s do, retrying while the file is in use, with the
  same window as a delete (3 s). A missing file is an error at once, and a hold that lasts past the window is still
  an error, so a test that reads a file to prove the core let go of it still fails when it did not.
- **`FormatsTests`' four reads of a file the core wrote** go through them.
- **`TempFilesTests`, three more:** a read waits out a brief hold, gives up on a lasting one, and fails at once
  on a missing file.

**Mutation check** (`scripts\mutate.ps1`, `TempFilesTests`): either read not retrying, the public read given no
window, a lasting hold waited for forever (caught as a hang), a missing file waited for, and what was read thrown away.
**All six caught.**

Managed baseline **360 / 0 / 1** (was 358 / 0 / 1).

#### Qt out of the names that stay (plan step 6.3)

The code that outlives the Qt application no longer names it, except where the reference is the point: the oracles
recorded from v2.14.2, and the import of v2.x's settings file. Nothing a user sees changes, and no test's expectation
changes.

- **One range helper, named for its rule.** The core's `qtMin` / `qtMax`, defined twice (`csvseriesparser.cpp`,
  `seriesbuilder.cpp`), are one pair in `include/model/seriesrange.h`, `runningMin` and `runningMax`, with the NaN rule
  written out. **The rule is not symmetric**, which the old names hid:
  - the minimum takes the new value unless the range so far is strictly lower, so a NaN sample makes the minimum NaN
    and the next sample replaces it;
  - the maximum keeps the range so far unless the new value is strictly higher, so a NaN sample leaves it as it was.

  `tmdq_abi.h`'s `y_min` / `y_max` and `TmDq.Core`'s `SeriesSpec.YMin` / `YMax` state it for a host, in place of "as
  Qt's qMin sees a NaN".
- **The app's colour arithmetic, named for what it does:** `PlotColors.QRound`, `ToQtHsv` and `FromQtHsv` are
  `RoundHalfAway`, `ToHsv16` and `FromHsv16`. Where the arithmetic came from is said once, in the class's summary.
- **`constants.h`:** the QSettings keys, the theme identifiers and the recent-files limit go, with the four native cases
  that pinned them (native 494 cases, was 498). They were the Qt application's; the import of v2.x's settings carries the
  key names it reads, held by `PreferencesTests` against the INI files v2.14.2 wrote. The full manual's note says "compiled
  into the application".

  what v2.14.2 wrote or did (the oracles themselves are unchanged). `parity.md` names the new ones; the table below maps
  the old names the changelog entries above use.
- **The comments, about 600 lines in some 120 files,** stand on their own:
  - a behaviour once explained by a Qt function ("as `QString::toInt` reads it") is stated, checked against the code,

  - a note saying what a class was ported from ("the Qt `BatchApplyDialog`") says what it does, or its user story;
