### v3.0.0 — The Avalonia Application

The first release of the Avalonia application (`docs/dotnet-migration/avalonia-plan.md`, decision D4): every user story
of v2.14.2 on Avalonia 12 and .NET 10, over the Qt-free native core, its CSV exports byte for byte the Qt application's
(5.2's soak). The installer replaces a v2.x install in place; v2.14.2 stays downloadable as the fallback for one release
cycle. Everything below, from the plan's first steps to its stage 5, landed between v2.14.2 and this release; the
release itself is the first section.

Before the plan was written, the work started as items from `docs/future_plans/dotnet-port-assessment.md` that are worth doing whether or not
that port ever happens - the throughput guard, the TOML move off `QSettings`, and now the
de-Qt of the native core in small steps (QtGui out of the model's headers, then
`PacketQueue`, then the `QElapsedTimer`s, then the packet bytes, then the first `QVector`s, the processing result and the pipeline's pointer lists) - plus the clean-build regression the TOML change
caused, a generated Visual Studio solution, and C++20. The first `QString` steps move `TomlDocument`,
`FrameSetup` and the step-file parser to UTF-8 `std::string`, and the `QObject` steps take
Qt out of `FrameProcessor` and `Ch10PacketReader`; the DTOs follow, starting with
`ProcessingParams` and `ProcessedStreamData`, and `FrameSetup`, `Chapter10Reader` and `ChannelData` lose their `QObject`s and `QString`s, the calibration report becomes `std::string`, and `CalibrationExtractor` becomes a plain class (the last `QObject` in the core); the last Qt header the core reached, in `constants.h`, goes, and a test now guards it. One user-facing fix, found during the
`QString` survey: recordings under a folder with a non-ASCII name can be processed.

#### The release: v3.0.0 ships the Avalonia application, and replaces v2.x when installed (plan step 5.3)

The first release built from `deploy/avalonia/build_avalonia_package.ps1` rather than `deploy/build_release.ps1`. Two choices, both the user's: **the installer replaces a v2.x install** rather than installing beside it, and the mutation harness (#237) merged first so this section gathers the whole of the work.

- **`AppVersion` 3.0.0** (D4). The manuals that ship are re-stamped by `build_manual.ps1 -Preview -NoCapture`; their figures are unchanged.
- **The installer** (`deploy/avalonia/tmDataQualityAnalyzer.iss`, renamed from the preview's):
  - **the Qt installer's AppId, folder and Start menu name,** so v3.0.0 is v2.x's upgrade: one entry in Installed apps, in the folder the user already has;
  - **`[InstallDelete]`** takes away what v2.x left that this version does not ship: `bin\` (the Qt exe, runtime and plugins), `UserGuide.txt`, and `UserManual.html`. **The last is a trap the upgrade would otherwise have sprung:** Help opens a `UserManual.html` beside the exe when there is one, and v2.x's sat exactly there, so declining the full-manual task would have left Help opening the Qt application's manual;
  - **`settings\`** is the same folder in both layouts (v2.x's exe in `bin\` looked one level up for it), so `onlyifdoesntexist` keeps the user's files through the upgrade (US8.0);
  - **the `.ch10` association,** as v2.x wrote it, now pointing at the exe in the install folder; declined on an upgrade, v2.x's ProgID is deleted rather than left opening an exe the upgrade has removed;
  - **What's New** (`InfoBeforeFile`) is `deploy/RELEASENOTES.txt`, as v2.x's installer showed it;
  - **preferences** need nothing from the installer: the app imports the Qt INI file on its first run (4.8).
- **The package script** names the artifacts `tmDataQualityAnalyzer-v3.0.0_portable.zip` and `_setup.exe`, runs `check_release_consistency.ps1 -ReleaseMode` before anything is built (as `build_release.ps1` did), and puts `deploy/README_portable.txt` in the ZIP as `README.txt`, rewritten for this layout (the `portable` marker, no `UserGuide.txt`, the third-party notices).
- **The consistency check** reads the manuals that ship, `resources/usermanual-preview.html` and `UserManual-preview.html`. The Qt manuals are no longer shipped and still say 2.14.2, which is true of them; 6.1 gives the preview copies their names.
- **The Sandbox verifier** (`deploy/sandbox/verify_avalonia_install.ps1`, renamed from the preview's) now tests **the upgrade**: v2.14.2 installed with its default tasks, a settings file edited and the Qt INI written, then this setup over it. It checks the Qt `bin\` and text guide gone, the full manual this version's, the edited settings file kept, `.ch10` opening the new exe, one entry in Installed apps, the first run importing the Qt preferences, and on uninstall the association and the entry gone with `settings\` left.
- **`cut-release`** describes this build: every suite (native, managed, app, and Qt while it is in the tree), `build_avalonia_package.ps1`, the artifacts in `deploy/avalonia/`, the Sandbox upgrade test, and the two US8.0 criteria checked by hand.
- **`deploy/RELEASENOTES.txt`** says what moved and how the preferences and settings carried over.

**Verified on the release build:**
- **Every suite at 3.0.0:** native 498 cases (1 skipped, the opt-in benchmark), managed 358 / 0 / 1, app 602 / 0 / 0 (34 not run, the soak), Qt 458 / 0 / 0 with zero warnings.
- **The package:** the consistency check clean in release mode; the signing pre-flight; the exe and `tmdq_core.dll` signed by this project's certificate and the six other PE files by their publishers, all Valid, in the staging folder, inside the ZIP and in the installer; the staged app processing the PRN sample (channel 13, 116 samples, mean lock 93.532 %).
- **Inno Setup failed once** with "EndUpdateResource failed, try excluding the Output folder from your antivirus software": the virus scanner held the new setup.exe while Inno wrote its icon. The installer step alone was run again from the same staged files and succeeded, signed.
- **The Sandbox, under Smart App Control, on the signed packages: every check passed.** The unsigned control was blocked. v2.14.2 installed (its `bin\`, text guide and full manual), a settings file edited and the Qt INI written (light theme, legend hidden); then this setup over it: exit 0, the Qt `bin\` and `UserGuide.txt` gone, the full manual this version's, the edited file kept (and kept again by a reinstall), `.ch10` opening `C:\Program Files\tmDataQualityAnalyzer\tmDataQualityAnalyzer.exe`, one entry in Installed apps at 3.0.0, all nine PE files Valid. The installed app opened its window, took the Qt preferences on its first run (`"Theme": "light"`, `"LegendVisible": false`) and processed the PRN sample; `tmdq_core.dll` answered ABI revision 2; the portable copy opened and processed the sample; Code Integrity blocked nothing of ours; uninstalling removed the application, the association and the entry, and left `settings\`.
- **Checked by hand, both passed:** the two US8.0 criteria the Sandbox cannot reach, since it installs silently and elevated. In a Sandbox, the user ran this build's setup, chose "Install for me only" and a folder of their own, and watched the progress page.

Every baseline is unchanged.

#### A Visual Studio solution, generated rather than committed

`scripts/gen_vs_project.ps1` produces `tmDataQualityAnalyzer.sln` for developers who want
Visual Studio Community instead of VS Code + the `env.ps1` shell. It runs `qmake -tp vc`
on the app and test `.pro` files (so the `.pro` files stay the single source of truth for
sources, defines and libraries) and writes the solution around the two projects. The
output is **gitignored**: it carries absolute Qt and repo paths, exactly like
`compile_flags.txt`, and a committed copy would rot at the next Qt bump. Regenerate after
a `.pro` change, a Qt bump or a Visual Studio update. Regenerating keeps build products,
so the build that follows is incremental (0 files recompiled, 3 s, against about 170 s
for a clean one).

Raw `qmake -tp vc` output does **not** build usefully in Visual Studio. Six things are
corrected after the fact, each found by building and reading the failure:

1. **Executable location.** The app finds `settings/` relative to its own directory and
   the tests find `data/` one level above theirs, so the exes must land in
   `build/<cfg>/` and `tests/<cfg>/`, not under `vs/`. `OutDir` is rewritten.
2. **Vendored C warnings.** `lib/irig106` raises C4100/C4267 at the project warning
   level, and the zero-warning gate applies. The library may not be edited, so its
   `ClCompile` items get `WarningLevel=TurnOffAllWarnings`. The script throws if it finds
   none, so a layout change cannot silently turn this into a no-op.
3. **Qt's own deprecation warnings.** `thirdparty.pri` passes `/external:anglebrackets
   /external:W0`; MSBuild adds `/external:W3` itself, which then collides (D9025,
   "overriding /external:W3 with /external:W0"). The raw options are stripped and the
   equivalent properties `TreatAngleIncludeAsExternal` and `ExternalWarningLevel` are
   set instead.
4. **Parallel PDB writes.** A solution build compiles both projects at once and fails
   intermittently with `C1090: PDB API call failed, error code '3'` (about one build in
   four) because the two compilers race on the PDB service. `ForceSynchronousPDBWrites`
   (`/FS`) fixes it; three consecutive full `/t:Rebuild` runs were clean after the change.
5. **Qt runtime.** A post-build step runs `scripts/deploy_qt_local.ps1`, so F5 needs no Qt
   on `PATH` (the same reason that script exists for IDE launches in general).
6. **Solution file.** qmake writes only projects. The `.sln` is written directly (UTF-8
   with BOM, CRLF), app project first so it is the startup project, with the project GUIDs
   read back out of the generated `.vcxproj` files.

Verified: Debug|x64 and Release|x64 both build with 0 warnings and 0 errors, and the
Visual Studio-built test exe gives 426 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, identical to the
`jom` baseline. No Qt VS Tools extension is required.

**Toolchain drift, and the pin.** Since Visual Studio Community 2026 was installed,
`env.ps1` resolved `cl` to its MSVC 14.51 (toolset v145) rather than the Build Tools'
14.44 (v143): `vswhere -latest` takes whatever is newest, so the "MSVC 2022 only"
statement in these docs, the Qt `msvc2022_64` kit and CI no longer described what a local
build used, and a tree built across the install held objects from both compilers.
`env.ps1` now asks vswhere for `[17.0,18.0)` (override: `TMDQ_VS_RANGE`), and skips its
2022 path-probe fallback when a range was requested so a failed 2026 lookup cannot quietly
return 2022. `gen_vs_project.ps1` requests `[18.0,19.0)`, because the projects it writes
carry the compiler's `PlatformToolset` and VS 2026 builds v145; it warns if the shell
already holds an older environment. Verified: default resolves 14.44, the override
resolves 14.51, an unsatisfiable range throws, and a clean Debug rebuild of the app and
tests under 14.44 gave 0 warnings and 435 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped.

#### A deleted header broke the clean build, and an incremental one could not see it

CI went red on `main` for one reason: the TOML change below deleted
`include/model/tomlconfighelper.h` and left a dangling `#include` in
`src/view/streamconfigdialog.cpp`. The include was **dead** - nothing in that file used
it - so nothing functional was wrong, but a clean build cannot compile the file.

**Every verification build had been incremental, and that is why it passed.** jom does not
notice that a header has been *deleted*, so the stale `streamconfigdialog.obj` was relinked
and the build reported success. The full suite ran **414 / 0 / 0 with zero warnings** against
that stale object. CI builds clean and failed immediately.

This is the stale-object trap `CLAUDE.md` already documents, arriving from the opposite
direction: not a crash at a meaningless address, a **false pass**. And grepping for the class
name `TomlConfigHelper` could not have found it, because what survived the refactor was the
*filename*. `CLAUDE.md` now says plainly that a change deleting a header is only verified by a
clean build.

A second stale-artifact trap on the way to fixing it, also now recorded: wiping `tests/debug/`
removes the Qt runtime that `deploy_qt_local.ps1` had put beside the test exe, so the suite
dies before its first test with exit **127** and `Qt6Cored.dll: cannot open shared object
file`. Meanwhile `output/results.txt` still holds the *previous* run's numbers, so reading it
reports a result for a run that never happened.

#### Qt's own deprecation warnings are suppressed, in the one way v2.9.0 left open

With the compile error gone, a clean build surfaced **13 `warning C4996`** - all from Qt 6.12
itself, at `qguiapplication.h(169)`, where `QGuiApplication` overrides the deprecated
`QCoreApplication::compressEvent`. Every translation unit that includes `<QGuiApplication>`
emits it, this application never calls `compressEvent`, and there is no fix available in our
code. CI's gate matches `warning [A-Z]\d+`, so a clean build could not go green while they
were visible.

`thirdparty.pri` now sets **`/external:anglebrackets /external:W0`**.

**Deliberately not `/wd4996`.** That flag used to live in this very file, suppressed
deprecation warnings for *application* code as collateral, and was removed on purpose in
v2.9.0 - the file carries a note saying so. `/external:` suppresses warnings whose *location*
is a non-first-party header while leaving our own files fully warned, and a deprecated API
called from our code is reported at **our** call site, so those keep warning exactly as
v2.9.0 intended. Every first-party header here is quote-included, so `anglebrackets` covers
Qt, the CRT and the Windows SDK in one rule. Stable since VS2019 16.10; this toolchain is
19.51.

#### The mutation harness, committed (plan step 6.4)

Since 2.4, every step was mutation-checked by a runner kept in a session's scratch folder and rewritten for each step. It is now `scripts/mutate.ps1`, so the method outlives the sessions that wrote it. Neither application changes.

- **One list, one suite:** a JSON list of exact-text mutants (id, file, old text, new text) and the suite that should catch them: `native` (doctest), `managed` (`TmDq.Core.Tests`) or `app` (`TmDq.App.Tests`). The test exe's arguments and environment can be set for the whole list or for one mutant. For `managed` and `app` the DLL is rebuilt first, so a mutant in the native core reaches them.
- **The verdicts:**
  - CAUGHT: a failing test, a crash, or a hang past the limit (420 s unless the list sets another).
  - SURVIVED.
  - COMPILE: not a survivor. Rewrite the mutant, unless the compiler is what holds the rule.
  - Four that mean nothing ran: NO-MATCH, NO-TESTS, STALE and LOCKED.
- **The traps the scratch runners each learned, now in one place:**
  - **Only in a linked worktree;** the main checkout is refused. An IDE's design-time build shares obj and bin with the loop (found in 4.7 and 4.8).
  - **A green baseline first,** with zero warnings for the native suite.
  - **The pristine bytes kept:** every restore is compared, and the run stops if one fails.
  - **No stale binary:** the test exe is deleted before each build, and what the mutated file compiles into (the test exe, `tmdq_core.dll`, or its project's assembly) must be newer than the file.
  - **An old text found exactly once:** one that matches nothing would run unmutated and "survive".
  - **The file's own line endings.**
  - **A filter that matches no test** fails the baseline, and makes a mutant's run NO-TESTS rather than a survivor.
- **A list that records decisions:** a mutant's `expect` (caught, survived or compile) marks an equivalent mutant, or a rule the compiler holds. A rerun reports any verdict that no longer matches, and its exit code says so.
- **The options:**
  - `-Parts 2 -Part 0` and `-Part 1` split a long list over two worktrees;
  - `-Only` reruns what survived;
  - `-Out` writes each verdict as it comes.
- **`scripts/mutants/example.json`:** four mutants of `TomlDocument`, one for each verdict a mutant that runs can get: two caught, one equivalent, one refused by the compiler.

**Found on the way:** the app's assembly is `tmDataQualityAnalyzer`, not `TmDq.App`. The first app mutant was reported STALE until the freshness check read the project's `AssemblyName`.

**Checked by running it, under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7,** in a worktree:
- **every verdict reached by a real mutant:**
  - a catch in each suite, and a native-core mutant caught by the managed suite through the rebuilt DLL;
  - the equivalent mutant and the compile error;
  - a text that matches nothing;
  - a filter that matches no test, both at the baseline and for one mutant;
  - a one-second limit, which killed the run and left no process behind;
- **the main checkout refused;**
- **`-Only`, `-Parts`, `-NoBaseline` and `-Out`;**
- **the worktree clean** after each run.

**Not reached:** LOCKED and a failed restore, both of which need a lock held from outside.

No test baseline changes.

#### The side-by-side soak (plan step 5.2)

The same recordings processed in both applications, the CSV exports compared byte for byte and the plots by eye: the record is `docs/dotnet-migration/soak.md`. Everything on the machine was used, and the session's settings swept, both at the user's choice.

- **34 runs over all 17 recordings** (11.6 GB): the five committed ones, the full PRN, Safran and PRN-AGC recordings, and nine local ones under `tests/data`. Every sample rate and averaging period, both modes, Derandomize, Legacy Chapter 10, a narrower sync mask, a typed data rate, the default, RASA and TRC receiver parameters, six non-linear calibrations and two template batches with every file exported.
- **All 40 CSV files identical** in the two applications (58 MB). The Qt side ran from a Debug and a Release build and gave the same bytes both times.
- **The plots match** in everything the data decides. Three differences, all in the legend or the margins:
  - **the Qt batch export draws the legend before laying it out,** so the missed-frames image's rows overlap: a Qt defect since v2.7.0, left in Qt (5.3 retires it); the Avalonia batch lays the view out first, since 4.7;
  - **Avalonia draws the legend's scroll bar into the image** when the legend scrolls, as its chart shows it (US6.0);
  - **Avalonia's plot area is about 13 px taller** at 900 px.
- **Which channels lock was found first,** by running every frame-sync guess over every channel: STEP CALS channels 27 and 28 and PRN-AGC's channel 26 are encoded the opposite of what their TMATS names say, and no recording on the machine is inverted, so Invert Data is not exercised by a run that locks.
- **The Avalonia application processes 3 to 6.5 % slower on the large recordings, all of it the process's CET shadow stack:** pinned to the performance cores, three rounds each, the full PRN recording takes 12.4 s in Qt and 13.2 s in Avalonia, and 13.2 s straight through `TmDq.Core` with no application. The DLL's build is not it: the same `tmdq_core.dll` from a small C++ program takes 12.5 s. .NET 9 and later mark the app host CET-compatible (`CETCompat`), so Windows keeps a hardware shadow stack of every call and return, the core's included: the C++ program linked `/CETCOMPAT` takes 13.2 s, and the C# one built `CETCompat=false` 12.5 s. Keeping it (it guards against return-oriented attacks, in a process whose C library parses the recordings it is given; the Qt application never had it) was decided on 2026-11-02: it stays on. Peak memory is about 60 MB higher (the .NET runtime and the test host), 89 MB on the largest run.

**How:** one list of runs, `dotnet/TmDq.App.Tests/Soak/soak.json`, every stream stating every setting so neither application fills anything in from its own defaults.
- **The Qt half was throwaway** (a Qt test case in a worktree, never committed): `MainViewModel`, `PlotViewModel::addStreamData`, `PlotWidget::exportImage`, `BatchController` and the Extract Calibration dialog's extraction, wired as the Qt main window and dialog wire them. Its CSV hashes are the manifest's `qt` blocks.
- **The Avalonia half is committed** (`SoakTests`, explicit): a real `ConfigureStreamsViewModel`, `ExtractCalibrationViewModel` and `MainWindowViewModel`, each run's CSV held to the Qt bytes. `scripts\run_soak.ps1` runs them one process a run. Once Qt is gone (6.1) the recorded bytes are the oracle.

**A trap in the Qt harness, not in either application:** its first images were exported the instant a run finished and drew the legend's rows where they had been before its last rebuild (CH-04 over CH-01). The single runs' images were made again with the layout settled; the batch was left as the Qt application really exports it.

**Mutation check, in a worktree, each mutant against the run that should catch it:** 17 mutants of the configurator and the comparison (each setting it hands on, the calibration, the batch's reuse of looks, OK refused in Extract Calibration). **16 caught**, two after rewriting ones the compiler refused, and **1 equivalent** (the number of receivers, which a receiver parameters file overrides, and every Receiver SNR run names one). One survivor was a gap, now closed: the typed data rate was 1.0 Mbps on a 1 Mbps channel, so it changed nothing; it is 1.25 Mbps, and both applications were run on it again. The comparison was given a wrong manifest four ways (a wrong hash, an extra file, no Qt result, a missing recording) and failed each time.

App baseline **602 / 0 / 0**, and 34 not run (the soak's explicit cases). Native, managed and Qt baselines unchanged.

#### The parity review (plan step 5.1)

Every acceptance criterion above checked against the Avalonia application, and every Qt test case ported or recorded as dropped with a reason: the record is `docs/dotnet-migration/parity.md`, both tables. Four independent mappings made it (one for the criteria, three for the Qt suites); every gap and every "met but untested" was then checked by hand.

- **Criteria (157):** 153 held by a test; 2 checked by hand (the installer's per-user directory and its progress page are Inno Setup's own, and the Sandbox installs elevated and silently, so 5.3 checks them on the release build); **2 removed, at the user's choice,** because neither application ever did them:
  - **US4.0 "Frame Sync Lock curves are drawn with a visually highlighted style, while Receiver SNR curves are not":** every curve has had one 1.5 px pen since the QCustomPlot days (4.3b flagged it);
  - **US5.2 "a Reset button":** neither Receiver SNR dialog has one; Load with the shipped `settings/receiver_params/default.toml` does its job.

  Each story keeps a note saying what was removed and why.
- **Qt test cases (278):** 254 ported, 23 dropped with a reason, 1 not held.
  - **Dropped:** Qt mechanics (stylesheet hooks, the event queue, an editable read-only combo), an idle coordinator's state, the five `removeSource` cases (nothing in the Qt application calls it), a chart's series index, and `TestCoreQtFree`'s self-tests and include-layer checks, which end with Qt.
  - **Not held:** `AddStream` ignoring a stream with no samples. Reaching it takes a stream that extracts frames yet completes no sample window, which no committed recording does; a stream that finds no sync or no frames is an error and never reaches the plot.
- **Closed with tests:** 11 Qt cases and 3 untested criteria:
  - **the plot** (`PlotTests`, `AroundTheChartTests`): a left minimum moving the drawn line; the plot view holding only the chart and its overlay; the title's notice, once a change, and its redraw; the axis titles' own words, and the right one drawn only while its axis is; three recordings each a day earlier than the last moving the time base twice (`TemplateBatchTests`, its `ADayLater` now taking a number of days);
  - **Configure Streams** (`StreamWindowsTests`, `StreamSetupViewModelTests`): a long channel name trimmed within its column with the whole name as its tooltip; the column headers light on the dark theme and dark on the light; the Average Period, polarity and voltage-range lists; Apply to all off at first;
  - **the run:** a batch of no files doing nothing; every progress report reaching the dialog on the UI thread (`ProcessingTests`);
  - **Open's and Import CSV's filters** (`ShellTests`);
  - **the native projects** (`NativeProjectTests`, in `TmDq.Core.Tests`): every file a project compiles exists, the DLL compiles every core and ABI source on disk, and the native tests compile every test file and exactly the DLL's sources. `TestCoreQtFree` held the core's list to the `.pro` and goes in 6.1; these checks need no Qt, so a test file left out of the project can no longer silently never run. The two Qt model sources are named in the test, which fails once 6.1 deletes them until they are taken off its list.
- **One difference, fixed:** Open offered "All files" beside Chapter 10 recordings, so a CSV could be chosen there and fail as a recording. It offers recordings only, as the Qt Open does (US6.3). `StorageRecordingPicker.Options` and `StorageDataFilePicker.CsvOptions` give the dialogs' options, so the filters can be tested.
- **Noted, not changed:** Qt upper-cased "ß" to "SS" in a pattern file and C# keeps it, which no hexadecimal field accepts either way; a non-ASCII channel name is held natively and through the managed library, not by an app test.

**Mutation check, in a worktree, each mutant against the whole app suite (stopping at its first failure):** 16 mutants, one for each behaviour the new tests hold: "All files" put back on Open and on Import CSV; a batch of no files run; the title announced on every set, and the chart not redrawn for it; the left minimum not reaching the chart; the right axis's title drawn with the left axis's visibility, and reworded; the channel name not trimmed, and without its tooltip; the headers given a colour of their own; a button beside the chart; progress reported from a thread-pool thread; only the series at zero moved when the time base moves; a choice relabelled; Apply to all on at first. **All 16 caught.** Five more, run by hand against `NativeProjectTests` (a test file and a core source taken off their projects, a source that does not exist and one listed twice added, an ABI source taken off the native tests only): **all caught.**

App baseline **602 / 0 / 0** (was 591); managed **358 / 0 / 1** (was 355 / 0 / 1). Native and Qt baselines unchanged.

#### The user manual for the Avalonia app, its figures rendered from the app (plan step 4.9)

The new application's own manual: both of them, the base one compiled in and the full one with the walkthroughs, rewritten where the new application differs and illustrated with figures rendered from it. 4.8 brought Help > User Manual and About; this step is what they open. The Qt application still ships, with its manuals unchanged.

**Two choices, both the user's:**
- **A preview copy of each manual,** rather than the one manual rewritten now: a Qt release before v3.0.0 still ships a manual that describes it. At the switch-over the copies replace the originals.
- **Figures rendered by script on the headless platform,** rather than captured by hand: reproducible, re-run after any change to the interface, and checked.

- **The plan said `build_manual.ps1` "grabs Qt widgets". It never did:** the Qt manual's figures are screenshots taken by hand, which it crops, scales and embeds. The plan is corrected.
- **The manuals** (`resources/usermanual-preview.html`, compiled into the application in place of the Qt one; `docs/manual/walkthroughs-preview.html`, spliced into `UserManual-preview.html`), copies of the Qt manuals with what differs rewritten:
  - **the setup dialog's own words:** Configure (gear), Frame Sync Lock or Receiver SNR, the five fields a pattern file keeps;
  - **problems shown as they arise:** OK and Process waiting, and the line under the rows saying which stream is not ready; Apply Cal unavailable, its tooltip saying why;
  - **the run:** its Cancel stopping every stream, the results plotted when it completes;
  - **the legend** shown or hidden from the menu or L, with no button on the chart;
  - **the pan cursor** (a hand, a left-right arrow while dragging);
  - **an image's format by its extension** (.png, .svg, anything else a PDF), and Browse adding the format's own;
  - **a batch's single image** for a file with no frame sync streams;
  - **the title bar** with snap layouts, and **settings kept between sessions,** taken from 2.x's on the first run;
  - **Ctrl+O** opening a recording; **Export** in the main menu.
- **The figures** (`ManualFiguresTests`, in `TmDq.App.Tests`): seven tests set up the manual's scenes from the committed recordings and the shipped settings, render 27 figures in the dark theme the application opens in (the light theme where it is the subject), and check what each caption says:
  - **the scenes:** two PRN streams locked (13 and 15, as the Qt application's template has them); step_cal's 48 receiver channels, linear and with a calibration extracted from it; three copies of the PRN sample and step_cal for the batch.
  - **the claims held:** the streams and which axes show; three files matching and one rejected; Plot File's entries; 48 channels; "11 steps parsed" and "Calibrated 12 of 48 channel(s)" with the clips at 6 and 2; receivers 1, 3, 5 and 6 calibrated; the calibrated staircase topping out at 60 dB; a Ready mark of each kind; the partly checked receiver; a stream with the wrong pattern leaving an error and one curve fewer.
  - **The menus are popups,** which the headless platform does not draw into a window's frame, so each is drawn in a window of its own and laid over the chart or the window where it opens (the right-click menu, Y Axes, Plot File, the application menu). **The progress dialog is caught in a real run** at its first report past 70 %: the plot still empty, the log part-way.
  - **The dialogs are given their services,** so each control is as available as in the application (Load and Save, Apply Cal, Browse, the menu's commands).
  - With `TMDQ_MANUAL_FIGURES` set they are written to that folder; otherwise to a temporary one, deleted after, so every test run proves each figure can still be made and each caption still holds.
- **Four Qt figures are not carried over:** the Windows file dialogs behind Open, Load receiver parameters and Save as Template, which no headless render can draw and the prose already describes, and the Qt installer's page. **One is shared:** the step file open in a text editor, which shows nothing of either application.
- **`build_manual.ps1 -Preview`** renders the figures (the tests built in Release; `-NoCapture` reuses them), scales them and embeds them through `embed_manual_images.py --preview`: its own paths, the same anchors (the figures keep the Qt files' names), two captions of its own, no installer figure. All 28 figures are placed: 17 in the base manual, 34 in the full one. The Qt manuals' build is unchanged; rebuilt, both come out identical.
- **The preview package** carries the full manual as `UserManual.html`: always in the portable ZIP, an optional "Install the full illustrated user manual" task in the installer, as the Qt one offers it.

**Found on the way, in the Qt manual as well:** five statements were already wrong for the Qt application, and are right in the preview's:
- **"These three fields can be saved...; Randomized ... not saved":** a pattern file has kept Derandomize and Invert Data since 2.14.2;
- **a legend button on the chart,** removed in an earlier release;
- **Ctrl+O "Open a Chapter 10 or CSV file":** Open takes recordings only;
- **"Right-click the chart and choose Export":** Export is in the main menu;
- **"an optional start/stop time range":** Configure Streams has none.

Left as they are in the Qt manual, as decided; a fix for a Qt release would be a small prose change.

**Tests:** 7 more in `TmDq.App.Tests` (591 in all): `ManualFiguresTests`, one per group of figures. `ShellTests`' manual test compares the compiled-in manual with the preview's.

**Mutation check:** the step's application change is one line, the manual compiled in; pointing it back at the Qt manual fails `TheManualIsTheFullOneWhenInstalledElseTheBaseOneCompiledIn`. The rest is test code (the figure tests, whose assertions are the captions' claims) and build scripts, held by running them: the preview manuals built, the Qt manuals rebuilt identical, the unsigned preview package built with the manual in its ZIP and its installer.

#### The shell in the Avalonia app: title bar, menu, recent files, drag and drop, themes and preferences (plan step 4.8)

The main window as the Qt one frames it: a title bar of its own, the hamburger menu with the Qt sections, Recent Files, a file dropped on the window, the light and dark themes, the log sidebar's toggle, and preferences kept between sessions, imported from the Qt application's on the first run. Renders are beside the plan: `shell-dark.png` and `shell-light.png` (the running app), `shell-menu.png` (the menu) and `shell-dialog-dark.png` (Configure Streams in the dark theme, its frame dark). The Qt application still ships.

**One PR, at the user's choice; the preferences in a file of the new application's own, imported once,** also the user's choice (rather than reading and writing the Qt INI file, which would have needed a QSettings-compatible writer).

- **The title bar** (`MainWindow`), in place of the system's: the client area extended into the frame, with `WindowDecorations="BorderOnly"` (a resizable frame, no drawn title bar), 40 px as the Qt bar is:
  - **left:** the menu button and the sidebar toggle ("Toggle sidebar (Ctrl+B)");
  - **right:** minimize, maximize (restore while maximized, its glyph and tooltip following the window however it is maximized) and close, in the Windows icon font's caption glyphs at 30 by 26 px, close red on a hover;
  - **between them,** the caption, which drags, snaps and maximizes on a double-click.
  - **Each part says what it is** (Avalonia 12's `WindowDecorationProperties.ElementRole`): the caption the title bar, the window's buttons the minimize, maximize and close buttons, the menu and the toggle the application's own. **Snap layouts, which the plan asked to verify first:** on the running app, `WM_NCHITTEST` answers `HTMAXBUTTON` at the maximize button, which is what makes Windows 11 offer its layouts on a hover; `HTMINBUTTON`, `HTCLOSE` and `HTCAPTION` at the others, and `HTCLIENT` at the menu and the toggle. The Qt title bar answered `HTCAPTION` and `HTCLIENT` only, so it never offered them.
- **The menu** (`BuildMenu`, rebuilt each time it opens), the Qt one in its order:
  - **Process:** Open... (Ctrl+O), Recent Files, Save as Template..., Apply Template to Files...;
  - **Import/Export:** Import CSV..., Export...;
  - **Settings:** "Switch to Light Theme" or "Switch to Dark Theme";
  - **then** Help (User Manual..., About...) and Exit, each set off by a separator.
  - **Each section's heading** is a disabled item, small and bold. The folder, floppy disk and import and export arrows are the Qt menu's icons, drawn as Avalonia drawings from the same SVG paths (the arrows a shade for each theme). Each entry is available as its command is, and the tooltips are the Qt ones.
  - **The top-bar buttons** of 4.5 and 4.7 (Open, Import CSV, Export, Save as Template, Apply Template) are gone into it.
- **Recent Files** (the Qt `addRecentFile` and its menu): at most five, the newest first, a file opened again moved to the top. A recording joins once its channels are read (even when Configure Streams is then cancelled, as in Qt), a CSV once it is imported; a file that is not a recording, or a CSV that is not an export, does not. Each is listed by its name with its path as the tooltip, then Clear Recent Files; with none, a disabled "(No recent files)". A file chosen opens by its suffix (an exported CSV imported, anything else opened as a recording), and not while busy. Missing ones are dropped at start-up.
- **Drag and drop:** a recording or an exported CSV dropped anywhere on the window opens as a recent file does: the first of the files that is one, by suffix in any case. The drag is offered as a copy only when there is such a file.
- **The themes** (US9.0), dark at first as in Qt:
  - **the chart** (`ChartPalette`, the Qt `PlotWidget::applyTheme`): background, axes and text, grid and title in each theme's colours, its cached layer repainted when the theme changes;
  - **the legend** (the Qt `PlotLegendOverlay::applyTheme`): translucent in either theme, its rows recoloured;
  - **the chips, the "Loading..." label, the log's panel and the title bar's hover:** theme dictionaries in `App.axaml`;
  - **every window and dialog,** through the application's theme, **native frames included:** on the running app, Windows reports Configure Streams' frame (and the main window's) as dark in the dark theme and light in the light one.
- **The log sidebar's toggle,** in the title bar and Ctrl+B: hidden, its column and the splitter's give their width to the chart; shown again, it comes back at the width it was dragged to.
- **What is remembered between sessions** (`Preferences`, `PreferencesStore`): the theme, the sidebar, the legend's visibility (4.4 kept it for the session), Recent Files, the folder of the last recording, CSV or template (where the file dialogs start and Export proposes to write; 4.5 kept it for the session), and the folder of Extract Calibration's last calibration recording (4.6's).
  - **Where:** `preferences.json` in `%APPDATA%\tmDataQualityAnalyzer`, beside the Qt application's settings; for a portable copy (a file named `portable` beside the exe) in a `tmDataQualityAnalyzer` folder beside it, as the Qt application decides. The preview's portable ZIP now carries the marker, as the Qt one does.
  - **Each change is written at once**; a file that cannot be read is the defaults, and a folder that cannot be written keeps the change for the session.
  - **The installer's smoke run keeps nothing,** so its recording reaches nobody's Recent Files.
- **The Qt application's settings, imported on the first run** (`QtSettingsImport`, `QtIni`): when there is no preferences file yet, the Qt INI file beside it is read, as QSettings reads it, and written as the new application's. From then on the new file is the one read.
  - **The keys:** `Theme` (anything but "light" is dark, as Qt reads it), `SidebarVisible`, `LegendVisible` (QVariant's string-to-bool: false only for "", "0" and "false" in any case), `RecentFiles`, `LastCh10Directory` and `CalibrationSetupDialog/lastCalDir`. `LastTomlDirectory` is left out: the Qt application never wrote it.
  - **The format, as Qt 6 reads it:** UTF-8; `[General]` in any case the top level, `%General` a section called General, any other section prefixing its keys; a key's `%XX` and `%UXXXX`; a list where a comma stands outside quotes; quotes keeping spaces and commas; every backslash escape, hex and octal included; `@Invalid()` for nothing, `@@` for a literal "@"; Qt paths given Windows' form.
- **Help:**
  - **User Manual:** the full manual when installed beside the application, else the base manual, compiled in (`resources/usermanual.html` as an embedded resource) and written to the temporary folder for the browser. A manual that cannot be shown is said so.
  - **About:** the name, the version and what the application does.
  - The manuals' text and figures for the new application, and the preview installer's optional full manual, stay 4.9's.

**The oracle:** three INI files Qt 6.12's `QSettings` wrote (a throwaway program, kept byte for byte in `dotnet/TmDq.App.Tests/QtSettings`, `-text` in `.gitattributes`): every key the Qt application keeps, with the values a user can have (commas and spaces in recording names, a semicolon, an equals sign, a quote, a backslash, a leading space, non-ASCII); a list of one; an empty list. Each reads as Qt wrote it. They show the rules a reader has to follow: a list of one is written as a plain value, an empty one as `@Invalid()`, and an item with a comma, a semicolon, an equals sign or a leading space is quoted.

**Found on the way:**
- **The plan said the Qt settings were in the registry, or a portable INI. They are always an INI file:** `main.cpp` sets `QSettings::setDefaultFormat(IniFormat)`. The plan is corrected.
- **Avalonia drew its own title and caption buttons over the extended client area,** a fullscreen button among them, under and beside the application's; its maximize button answered the hit test at our minimize. Found by capturing the running window, not by a test. `WindowDecorations="BorderOnly"` removes them and keeps the resizable frame.
- **The window crashed at start-up:** `AvaloniaXamlLoader.Load` leaves the named controls null; the generated `InitializeComponent()` is what fills them. A menu flyout declared inside a button's `Flyout` in XAML is not in the window's name scope either; it is made in code.
- **The menu's section style did not reach the menu:** a flyout is a popup of its own, so the style is application-wide.
- **Headless drag and drop needs its DragEnter:** a DragOver or a Drop without one reaches no handler. User code cannot implement `IStorageFile`, so the tests take storage items from the window's storage provider.
- **A test method's opening brace sat on its declaration line** in `ExportImportTests` (left by an earlier edit); fixed.

**Not ported, or not yet:**
- **The window's size and place are not remembered,** as the Qt application does not (it opens at 1920 by 1080; this one at 1280 by 800).
- **A recent file that fails to open stays in the list,** and a file dropped that is neither is refused without a word, both as in Qt.
- **The Qt title bar's menu and sidebar glyphs were painted in code;** these are the Windows icon font's.

  - **The recent-files list records the imported CSV:** `TheMainWindowRemembersItsFolderItsRecentFilesAndItsChoices`.
- **US9.0:**

**Tests:** 67 more in `TmDq.App.Tests` (584 in all; the two top-bar tests of 4.5 and 4.7 are replaced by the menu's):

#### Templates, batch and Plot File in the Avalonia app (plan step 4.7)

A template saved from one processed recording, then run over several recordings that share its channels, each kept in the plot, with the Plot File selector to view one or all, and an optional CSV and images per file (US1.1). The render of the batch confirmation is beside the plan (`batch-apply.png`). The Qt application still ships.

**One PR, at the user's choice; Save as Template and Apply Template are top-bar buttons beside Open,** also the user's choice, with tooltips, until the shell's menu (4.8).

- **The template file** (`TemplateFile`, decision D3: template JSON is C#'s), the Qt `ProcessingTemplateSchema` and `StreamConfigSchema`, so a template either application wrote loads in the other:
  - **What it holds:** every row of Configure Streams (processed or not), the time channel's place in its list, the byte order, and each series' name and colour. No recording paths, and no calibration profiles: only what a calibration was extracted from, so a batch processes with the linear calibration, as Qt's does.
  - **Reading keeps the Qt rules:**
    - a key that is missing, or of the wrong type, keeps its default, as `QJsonValue`'s typed reads do (a fractional number is not an int);
    - an entry without a channel id and a label is skipped;
    - the sample period and slope indices are clamped, and the polarity is not;
    - an unknown mode reads as Receiver SNR, an unknown metric as SNR, a colour that is not one as black;
    - a template from before the byte order was kept reads as swapped;
    - no schema version, or a newer one, is refused; so is JSON that is not an object with an entries array.
  - **Writing gives the Qt application's bytes:** `QJsonDocument`'s indented form (keys sorted, four spaces, an empty array's bracket on its own line), whole numbers without a point, doubles as the shortest text that reads back, Qt's escapes, CR LF, UTF-8 without a byte-order mark.
- **Save as Template** (the Qt `saveTemplateButtonPressed`): available once a recording has been processed. With several (after a batch), a choice of which, "&lt;file&gt; (source N)" (`ChoiceWindow`, the Qt `QInputDialog::getItem`). Then the save dialog, then "Template saved: &lt;file&gt;". The series' names and colours are captured as they are now.
- **Apply Template** (the Qt `applyTemplateButtonPressed`):
  - **The template**, with its errors in the log in the Qt words (cannot be opened, not JSON with the parser's reason, an unsupported schema version, not a template, no stream entries).
  - **Then the recordings,** several at once, each checked against the template off the UI thread. A file matches when its PCM channel ids are exactly the template's (the core's `TemplateMatcher`), never by name.
  - **The confirmation** (`BatchApplyWindow` over `BatchApplyViewModel`, the Qt `BatchApplyDialog`): "N of M selected file(s) match the template and will be processed.", a row per file (✓ and its name, or ✗, its name and its missing and extra channels), a CSV and plot images per file into a folder (Browse), and the template's names and colours reused (on at first). Process needs a matching file, and a folder while exporting.
- **The batch** (`MainWindowViewModel.RunBatchAsync`, the Qt `BatchController`), one file after another under the progress dialog:
  - **A fresh plot,** then each file opened and **checked again at its turn** (it may have changed since it was chosen), and run with the template's processed rows, over the time channel at the template's place in the file's list (the file's default when its list is shorter), in the template's byte order.
  - **Each file is kept in the plot as a recording of its own,** named by its file for the Plot File selector, with the template's names and colours put back when asked (the first series of that recording with the look's channel, metric, receiver and channel, then one refresh).
  - **A file that is gone, no longer matches, or fails** is skipped and said so; a recording that does not overlap the others is warned of, naming it.
  - **When a folder is given, each file's own export** (the Qt `finish`): its CSV (every series of that recording), then with frame-sync data `<file>_framesync_lock.png` and `<file>_missed_frames.png`, else `<file>.png`. Each image shows that recording alone in the metric it names; the view is put back after.
  - **Then:** the plot on the first file, titled with its name, and "Batch complete: X processed, Y skipped." with where the output went.
- **Plot File** on the chart's menu (the Qt submenu): "All files (overlaid)", then one item per recording. Enabled with data and more than one recording. Choosing one shows its series only, over its own span with the SNR axis ranged to it (`PlotViewModel.SetVisibleSource`); it narrows what is drawn, never what a CSV holds (US6.1).
- **Configure Streams hands back what it settled** (`StreamsChoice`): the run, every row and the time channel's place, which a template captures. An Open clears the recordings with the plot.

**The oracle:** the Qt application's own templates, and its own batch export.
- **Three templates written by the Qt application,** kept byte for byte in `dotnet/TmDq.App.Tests/Templates`: the PRN sample's four channels with names and colours, a Receiver SNR row with calibration references, and a template with no entries. A throwaway case in the Qt suite wrote them and was removed. Each reads as Qt reads it, and writing what was read gives the same bytes.
- **The batch over two copies of the PRN sample** exports a first-file CSV identical to the Qt export of that file (9,479 bytes).

**Found on the way:**
- **A fixture cannot be called `prn.json` on Windows.** PRN is a reserved device name, like CON and NUL, so git could not create the file and the commit failed. It is `prn-sample.json`.
- **The repository's `* text=auto` stored the Qt-written templates with LF,** so a checkout without `core.autocrlf` would have had files no longer as Qt wrote them, and the byte-for-byte tests would have failed in CI only. `.gitattributes` now marks them `-text`.
- **An image exported just after the view changed was laid out for the previous view.** The batch switches the recording and the metric before each image, and the legend's size had not yet followed. The export now lays the view out first.

**Not ported, or not yet:**
- **The Qt batch's per-file progress lines** are the run's own lines here, one run at a time, under the same progress dialog as an Open.
- **The last folder between sessions, drag and drop, and recent files** are 4.8's.

**Each acceptance criterion of US1.1**, with the test that holds it:
- **Apply Template, then several files at once:** `ApplyTemplateReadsTheTemplateChecksTheFilesAndRunsTheOnesThatMatchOnceConfirmed`, `TheTopBarHasSaveAsTemplateAndApplyTemplate`.
- **Configured once, by Save as Template:** `SaveAsTemplateCapturesTheRecordingJustProcessed`, `WithSeveralRecordingsSaveAsTemplateAsksWhichAndAnOpenForgetsThem`, `ATemplateIsCapturedFromOneRecordingAndItsSeriesAsTheyLook`.
- **Matched by channel id, the missing and extra channels told:** `AFileMatchesOnItsChannelIdsAloneAndAMismatchIsSpelledOut`, `TheConfirmationSaysHowManyMatchAndNeedsAFolderOnlyToExport`.
- **Every file kept; a CSV and images per file to a folder, named from each file:** `ABatchRunsEachFileInTurnKeepsEachAndExportsEachAsTheQtApplicationDoes`.
- **Progress, and a summary of processed and skipped:** the same, and `ATemplatesNamesAndColoursGoOnEveryFileWhenAskedAndAFailedFileIsSaidSo`.
- **The settings round-tripped, and the names and colours:** `TheQtApplicationsTemplatesReadAsTheyWereWritten`, `ATemplateIsWrittenAsTheQtApplicationWritesIt`, `ATemplatesLooksGoBackOnOneRecordingsMatchingSeriesInOneRefresh`.
- **The Plot File selector:** `ThePlotListsItsRecordingsAndShowsOneOrAll`, `PlotFileListsTheRecordingsAndShowsTheOneChosen`.

**Tests:** 43 more in `TmDq.App.Tests` (519 in all):
- **`TemplateTests` (30):** the Qt templates read and written byte for byte; doubles; what is left out; every refusal; missing keys, wrong types, clamped indices; appearances; matching and its words; capture, the looks put back, a recording's run; the plot's recordings and Plot File;
- **`TemplateBatchTests` (12):** the batch over PRN copies with its export against the Qt one; names and colours and a failed file; a recording that shares no time with the others (step_cal and a copy a day later, its time packets edited) and a Receiver SNR batch's images; a template that cannot be used; Apply Template end to end with the confirmation's choices; Save as Template, with one recording and several; an Open keeping the byte order and time channel; the confirmation's state and window; the choice of recording; the top bar;
- **`ExportImportTests` (1):** an image exported just after the view changed, laid out for the new view.

`TestProcessingTemplateSchema`'s and `TestBatchController`'s cases, and `TestPlotViewModel`'s source-view cases, are ported among them.

**Mutation check, in two worktrees, with a seven-minute limit on each run:** 196 mutants:
- **the template file** (58): reading (each refusal, every key's default and type, the clamps, the modes, metrics and colours, the appearances) and writing (the indented form, the sorted keys, the empty array, the numbers, the escapes, CR LF, no byte-order mark, what is left out, the schema version);
- **the batch's rules** (25): the match and its words, capture (the name, the rows, the looks of that recording and channel), the looks put back (each part of the match, one refresh), a recording's run (the rows, the time channel's place and its bounds, the byte order, the source);
- **the confirmation** (17): the summary, the rows' marks and words, Process's rule, Browse, Process and Cancel;
- **Plot File** (21): the source gate, the span and range of the recording shown, the notices, the labels, the submenu's items, checks and enabling;
- **the main window** (66): Save as Template (the choice, the dialog, the words, the folder), Apply Template (each step and its words), the batch (each skip and its words, the run, the sources and labels, the looks, the warning, the summary), each file's export (the CSV, the images and their names and metrics, the view put back), and Open (the sources, the label, the choice kept);
- **Configure Streams' choice and the run with no dialog** (8); **the image laid out before export** (1).

**Thirty-five could not be built the first time:** the Windows SDK was being modified while they ran, and `mt.exe`, which merges the manifest, was missing for half an hour. They were run again. **Of the 196, the first conclusive run caught 147.** Five were refused by the compiler; four were rewritten and caught, and one (dropping the save dialog's null check) is held by the compiler's null analysis. **Forty-four survived:**
- **Thirty-six were gaps, now closed:**
  - **the template file:** a number of the wrong type (a boolean) read as its default; the mode a row's settings belong to; control characters up to 0x1F escaped, in Qt's lower case; a template read at an older schema version written at the current one;
  - **the batch's rules:** a single missing channel spelled out; the time channel at the template's place inside the list, and just outside it at either end; a look kept off another recording's, receiver's and channel's series;
  - **the confirmation:** Process run regardless with nothing matching;
  - **Plot File:** source 0 shown alone; a recording of one sample shown at its instant; the choice announced; "All files (overlaid)" chosen again;
  - **the main window:**
    - Apply Template waiting while a batch runs;
    - the confirmation's Reuse and Export choices carried out, and its folder trimmed;
    - the parser's reason after "not valid JSON";
    - **the warning that a recording shares no time with the others, naming it.** No committed pair of recordings could raise it, so the test makes one: a copy of step_cal with every time packet a day later;
    - the summary's counts told apart (2 processed, 1 skipped, where the tests had equal counts);
    - each recording kept with the template's time channel and byte order;
    - a CSV that cannot be written said so;
    - a Receiver SNR batch's one image per file;
    - a recording that cannot be read forgetting the batch's recordings;
    - an Open keeping the byte order and the time channel's place Configure Streams settled;
  - **the run with no dialog:** only the first row processed; the default time channel's place. **Configure Streams** handing back the place chosen;
  - **the image** laid out for a view just changed.
- **Two were lines that did nothing, and are gone:**
  - Open noting the file for the warning above: an Open clears the plot first, so the warning cannot arise there;
  - Save as Template told when the recordings change: they change only while busy, and the end of it tells Save as Template.
- **Four were in `StreamsChoice.Of`,** which only a test's fake configurator used. It is gone from the app, and the fake makes its own choice.
- **Two are equivalent, and the code stays,** since each says the Qt rule:
  - a look matched on its metric: a rename or recolour reaches the stream's other metric anyway;
  - Plot File needing data as well as two recordings: two recordings are data.

**187 of 196 caught by a test,** one by the compiler, two equivalent, two lines removed, and four with the code moved to the tests.

#### Extract Calibration and Apply Cal in the Avalonia app (plan step 4.6)

Non-linear step calibration (US5.3) from the Receiver SNR setup dialog. The extraction is the core's, already held to the core's own answers by the managed library's `CalibrationTests`; this step is the dialogs around it. Renders are beside the plan: `extract-calibration.png` (step_cal, clips set past its end) and `calibration-report.png` (its report). The Qt application still ships.

- **Apply Cal** (the Qt `ReceiverSNRDialog`'s group 3), in the Receiver SNR setup dialog under the word map:
  - **The label beside it:** "(none — using linear calibration)" in gray, or "N channel(s) calibrated (non-linear)".
  - **On OK of Extract Calibration:** the dialog keeps the profiles, the two files and the clips. The setup dialog's OK gives them to the row, Apply to all copies them (4.1a), and Process hands the profiles to the run.
  - **Then the report,** in a "Calibration Extracted" box (`ReportWindow`, selectable and scrolling). Its text is the core's summary of every receiver, or "Applied non-linear calibration to N channel(s)." when that is empty.
  - **Apply Cal is unavailable, with its tooltip saying why,** while the stream's settings have a problem or the recording has no time channel. The Qt dialog warned in a box instead, at Apply Cal ("No Time Channel") and at the recording's Browse ("Missing Frame Sync"). This follows 4.1b's rule: a problem is shown as it arises, not after the click. `ExtractCalibrationViewModel` still refuses a recording without a frame sync pattern, with the Qt words in its status.
- **Extract Calibration** (`ExtractCalibrationWindow` over `ExtractCalibrationViewModel`, the Qt `CalibrationSetupDialog`):
  - **The step file:** the one the stream last used if it is there, else the shipped `settings/rcvr_cals/default.toml`, loaded as the dialog opens. Its status says "N steps parsed (loaded automatically)."
  - **Browse starts** in the shipped step files, and for the recording where the last recording came from this session (Qt kept that folder between sessions; that is 4.8's).
  - **Clip Start and Clip End:** 0 to 100,000 s, one decimal.
  - **The extraction runs** once both files are in hand, and again after any change to either file or to a clip. The progress dialog ("Processing calibration file…") sits over the dialog, and its Cancel stops the extraction.
  - **Each status line** is marked and coloured as Qt's: ✓ green, ⚠ goldenrod, ✗ red, gray while pending. A setting that cannot be read (the pattern, the mask) is a ✗ before anything starts.
  - **Clips past the end:** "Clip Start + Clip End (X s) exceed the recording (Y s) - clips ignored." is a ⚠ before the summary, and heads the report.
  - **OK** is available once the step file parsed and at least one channel calibrated.
- **The time channel and the byte order:** the extraction now uses the time channel chosen in Configure Streams and the recording's byte order (Legacy Chapter 10). The Qt dialog took the recording's first time channel whatever was chosen (decided in 4.1).
- `ProcessingViewModel` takes the text it shows, so the calibration's progress says its own words.

**Found on the way:**
- **Which time channel is used cannot be seen in the result.** A time channel only sets the reader's clock, and steps are found in elapsed time. An extraction told to use a time channel step_cal does not have still calibrates the same 12 channels. So the choice is held where it travels: Configure Streams' selection (16, on a PRN copy with a second time channel) reaching the extraction's request. The Qt defect was real but, on these recordings, without effect on the profiles.
- **The clip boxes were too narrow for "1000.0"** (it read "1000."). Found by looking at a render, not by a test. They are now the setup dialog's 150 px.

**Each acceptance criterion of US5.3**, with the test that holds it:
- **Enabled from the setup dialog ("Apply Cal"):** `ApplyCalIsForAReceiverSnrStreamWithATimeChannelAndNoProblem`, `TheSetupWindowHasApplyCalWithItsCalibrationBesideIt`.
- **The step file, and the calibration recording:** `TheDialogOpensOnTheStreamsStepFileElseTheShippedOne`, `BrowseStartsInTheShippedStepFilesThenWhereItLastWent`.
- **Clip Start and Clip End:** `ClipsBeyondTheRecordingAreIgnoredAndSaySoAtTheStreamsDataRate`, `TheExtractCalibrationWindowShowsTheDialogsState`.
- **Steps extracted per channel; profiles for those that map, the rest linear:** `TheCalibrationRecordingIsExtractedWithTheProgressDialogUp` (12 of 48, the words), `OnlyTheRecordingsOwnByteOrderInversionAndRandomizationCalibrate`.
- **The summary box, its flags and the clip report:** `ApplyCalExtractsWithTheSettingsAsTheyStandAndOkKeepsItsCalibration`, `ApplyCalWithAReportlessExtractionSaysHowManyChannels`, `ExtractCalibrationAndItsReportSitOverTheSetupDialogAndClose`. The report's wording is the core's, pinned in the native suite.

#### Export and import in the Avalonia app (plan step 4.5)

The plot as an image, its data as CSV and the log as text, any of them from one Export dialog, and an exported CSV read back into the plot (US6.0 to US6.3). The render of the dialog is beside the plan (`export-dialog.png`). The Qt application still ships.

**One PR, at the user's choice; Import CSV and Export are top-bar buttons beside Open,** also the user's choice, with the Qt menu items' tooltips, until the shell's menu (4.8).

- **The Export dialog** (`ExportWindow` over `ExportViewModel`, the Qt `ExportDialog`):
  - **Three rows, in the Qt order:** the plot image (ticked at first), the data (CSV) and the log (text). Each has a box, a path and Browse.
  - **A row's path and Browse are enabled only while its box is ticked.** Export is enabled while some box is ticked and every ticked row has a path.
  - **The defaults** are the plot's title (or "plot") with `\/:*?"<>|` replaced by "_", as `<title>.png`, `<title>.csv` and `<title>_log.txt`. They go in the folder of the last recording opened or CSV imported this session, else the application's folder.
  - **Browse** opens the platform's save dialog with the Qt titles and filters, starting at the row's path. A name chosen without a suffix gets the row's own.
  - **On Export,** the data is written first, then the image, then the log, so the log carries the lines about the other two.
    - Each export logs where it went (green) or that it failed (red), worded as the Qt ones are.
    - A failure does not stop the rest.
    - Nothing is written without data.
- **The image** (`PlotImageExport`, the Qt `PlotWidget::exportImage`):
  - **What it shows:** the chart's data layer at its size on screen, without the crosshair, the zoom band, the chips or "Loading...". The legend is drawn where it is on the chart, dragged and scrolled as shown, unless it is hidden.
  - **The suffix decides the format** (`ImageFiles.Resolve`): .png and .svg in any case, anything else a PDF, with ".pdf" added unless the name ends with it.
  - **One routine draws all three,** onto a Skia canvas: a raster surface, an SVG canvas, or a PDF page sized in points. Avalonia draws onto any canvas through `DrawingContextHelper.RenderAsync`. So the screen and every format share one renderer, as the Qt application has since v2.9.0.
- **The data** (`PlotViewModel.ExportCsv`, the Qt `exportCsv`):
  - **Every series, shown or not,** goes through the core's writer with the recording's clock.
  - **A source id keeps that source's series only,** for 4.7's per-file batch export.
  - **Nothing to write writes no file.**
- **The log:** the sidebar's lines, CR LF (Qt's text mode), UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, ending with a line end.
- **Import CSV** (`MainWindowViewModel.ImportCsvAsync`, `PlotViewModel.LoadCsv` and `LoadCsvAsync`; the Qt `importCsv`, `loadCsvFile`, `loadCsvFileAsync` and `commitParseResult`):
  - **The dialog:** "Import CSV File", filtered to "Exported CSV", starting in the last folder.
  - **What happens, in order:**
    - "Importing CSV: <file>" is logged;
    - the plot is cleared;
    - the file is read off the UI thread with "Loading..." over the chart;
    - the file's series are shown as a run's would be: the clock from the file; each Frame Sync Lock stream given the core's stream order, so its two metrics share a colour; the metric of the view in use shown;
    - the plot is titled with the file's name, and "Imported CSV: <file>" logged in green.
  - **Skipped rows:** "Skipped N malformed row(s) while loading the CSV." is logged in goldenrod before the success line.
  - **A file that is not an exported CSV** (the legacy `Day,Time` layout, a wrong header, no data rows) is the Qt error, word for word. Nothing is shown.
  - **While a CSV is being read,** a second request is dropped, as Qt drops it.

**The oracle: the Qt application's own export of every committed recording, byte for byte.** A throwaway case in the Qt suite processed seven runs, recorded the size and SHA-256 of each CSV, and was removed:
- **the runs:** the PRN sample (two PRN streams), step_cal and TRC each in both modes, RASA's receivers with `RASA.toml`, and Safran's PRN-15 channel with the byte swap off;
- **how each was recorded:**
  - the core's job builder over the very settings the test states;
  - a `ProcessingCoordinator` run;
  - each stream handed to the Qt `PlotViewModel::addStreamData`;
  - `exportCsv`.

The app runs the same settings through `StreamsRun` into its plot and exports. **All seven matched on the first run.** A second test reads each export back and writes it again, byte for byte.

**Found on the way:**
- **The legend was missing from the first images.** The image tests read back the PNG pixel by pixel, and both of my first two attempts drew no legend.
  - **What the helper does:** `RenderAsync` replaces the canvas's transform. Unless told otherwise, it also clips to the visual's bounds, and the legend's bounds carry its place on the chart. So it drew the legend at its origin and clipped it away.
  - **The fix:** the legend is recorded into an `SKPicture` at its origin, clipped to its size. The recording (vector still) is played back at the legend's place.
- **US6.1 says the CSV covers "every visible" series; the Qt application writes every series, shown or not.** `exportCsv` has never looked at visibility. The user's decision: the CSV outputs everything, every time. The criterion is reworded to say so, with a scope note (hiding a series, the view's metric and zoom change what is drawn, never what is exported), and the port writes every series as the Qt application does.
- **US6.0 is reworded the other way, also the user's decision:** the image is exactly what the chart shows (the series shown, the metric in view, the time window and axis limits as set, the legend where it sits or none), for making charts by setting up the screen; the interactive overlays (crosshair, zoom band, chips, "Loading...") are not chart and are left out. The port already drew it so; `AnImageShowsOnlyWhatTheChartShows` now holds it: a hidden series is absent and appears once shown, and a zoomed image holds the window and nothing past it.
- **Two streams on one channel keep only the later.** My first oracle runs put step_cal's and TRC's lock and receiver streams on the same channel. Their exports held only the receivers: a stream processed again replaces its earlier series, keyed by source, label and channel. That is true of the Qt application and the port alike. Configure Streams has one row per channel, so it cannot arise there, and the runs are now one mode each.
- **A PDF is about 1.1 MB.** SkiaSharp is built without Skia's font subsetter, so it embeds the two Segoe UI faces whole. The Qt PDF embeds subsets. Text stays text, and the page is the chart's size in points.

**Not ported, or not yet:**
- **The log's lines are plain text.** In the Qt sidebar the export messages are links to the file. The exported text is the same.
- **The SVG has no title or description.** Skia's SVG canvas writes none, where Qt's `QSvgGenerator` set both. The PDF carries the title.
- **Drag and drop, recent files, and remembering the last folder between sessions** are 4.8's.
- **Per-file batch export** is 4.7's.

**Each acceptance criterion these stories have**, with the test that holds it:
- **US6.0:**
  - **One image of exactly what the chart shows:** `AnImageShowsOnlyWhatTheChartShows`, `APngIsTheChartAtItsSizeWithTheLegendWhereItIs`, `TheCursorsCrosshairIsNotExported`.
  - **SVG, PNG, PDF:** `AnSvgAndAPdfAreTheChartsSizeAndAnyOtherNameIsAPdf`, `AnImagesNameDecidesItsFormat`.
  - **The file chosen in the dialog:** `BrowseStartsAtTheRowsPathAndANameWithoutASuffixGetsTheRowsOwn`, `TheExportWindowIsLaidOutAsQtsAndEachRowFollowsItsBox`.
  - **The legend at its place:** `APngIsTheChartAtItsSizeWithTheLegendWhereItIs` (dragged, and hidden); `TheCursorsCrosshairIsNotExported`.
  - **One dialog for any combination:** `ExportWritesWhatWasChosenInTheQtOrderAndTheLogSaysWhere`, `AFailedExportSaysSoAndTheRestStillRun`, `TheExportDialogsAnswerIsCarriedOut`.
- **US6.1:**
  - **Every series in one CSV, every time, a time column and one per series, self-describing headers:** `EveryRecordingExportsTheQtApplicationsCsvByteForByte`, `AnExportHoldsEverySeriesShownOrNotAndNothingToWriteWritesNoFile`, `ALaterSourcesColumnsAreQualifiedAndASourceCanBeExportedAlone`.
  - **The file chosen in the dialog:** above.
- **US6.2:** `ExportWritesWhatWasChosenInTheQtOrderAndTheLogSaysWhere`, `AFailedExportSaysSoAndTheRestStillRun`.
- **US6.3:**
  - **Import CSV, a CSV-only dialog, disabled while busy:** `TheTopBarHasImportCsvAndExportBesideOpen`, `ImportCsvAsksInTheLastFolderAndAnImportOfSkippedRowsWarnsBeforeItSucceeds`.
  - **Straight into the plot, the application's own format, each series to its axis, metric and colour:** `ImportCsvShowsTheFileTitledByItsNameAndSaysSo`, `AnImportedPlotIsShownAsARunsWouldBe`, `EveryExportReadsBackAsItsSeriesAndExportsAgainByteForByte`.
  - **Exported again:** `EveryExportReadsBackAsItsSeriesAndExportsAgainByteForByte`.
  - **A file not in the format rejected with an error:** `AFileThatIsNotAnExportedCsvChangesNothing`, `ACsvThatIsNotAnExportIsAnErrorAndLeavesThePlotEmpty`.
  - **Malformed rows skipped and counted:** `MalformedRowsAreSkippedWithAWarningThatCountsThem`.
  - **Loading shown:** `ACsvIsReadOffTheUiThreadWithLoadingShownAndASecondRequestDropped`, `LoadingIsShownOverTheChartWhileACsvIsRead`.
  - **Not yet:** drag and drop, and recent files (4.8).

**Tests:** 53 more in `TmDq.App.Tests` (448 in all), in `ExportImportTests`:
- **the oracle:** seven runs, byte for byte, and read back and written again;
- **the image:** read back pixel by pixel, the SVG's and the PDF's sizes, the format rule, a write that fails;

`TestExportDialog`'s cases, `TestPlotWidget`'s export cases, and `TestPlotViewModel`'s and `TestMainView`'s CSV cases are ported among them.

  - a hidden legend not drawn: the renderer skips an invisible visual anyway;
  - the PNG cleared to transparent: a new raster surface is;
  - a dropped read treated as loaded: the main window's own busy guard stops a second import before it reaches the plot.
- **One is not held:** the native core loaded before an import's file is read. Without it, an import before any recording was opened would fail. The core is loaded once a process, and the tests' process has it.

**123 of 129 caught,** two lines removed, three equivalent, one not held.

#### Around the chart in the Avalonia app: the legend, the chips, the menu, the keys and Customize View (plan step 4.4)

Everything the Qt `PlotWidget` puts around its chart, except image export (4.5). The plot window is the chart and nothing else (US4.1): every control is on the right-click menu, on a chip over the chart, or a key. Renders are beside the plan: `plot-chips-legend.png` (the chips and the legend over a zoomed plot), `plot-menu.png` (the menu) and `customize-view.png` (Customize View's SNR tab on step_cal's 48 channels). The Qt application still ships.

**One PR, at the user's choice.** The Qt `PlotWidget` is split up in the port, as planned in 4.3b: 4.3b's `PlotChart` draws, and `PlotView` (`TmDq.App/Views`) holds it with what is around it.

- **`PlotView`**, the chart with two things over it, and only where they are (the rest of the chart still takes the mouse):
  - **The chip bar** at the top left, gathering the on-chart controls:
    - **View Mode:** shown only when the data has both left-axis metrics. It is named for the metric it switches to ("Show Accumulation", "Show Lock %"), with a tooltip saying so.
    - **Reset view:** shown only once the window is narrower than the recording or an axis limit is set. It restores both.
    - With neither chip shown the bar takes no room. The chips are translucent, in the legend's style.
  - **The legend** (`PlotLegend`, the Qt `PlotLegendOverlay`):
    - **Its rows:** a line swatch in the series' colour and its label, for each series shown of the metric in view.
    - **SNR labels:** a short "CH&lt;channel&gt; &lt;L|R|C&gt;_RCVR&lt;n&gt;" label, made from the series' numbers.
    - **Translucent:** white at alpha 185, with a grey border and rounded corners.
    - **Capped:** at 45 % of the chart's width and 60 % of its height, scrolling beyond that. The rows always leave the scroll bar's 16 px free, so it never covers a label.
    - **Placed:** at the top right, and dragged anywhere inside the chart, a margin from its edges. It follows the top right when the chart is resized, until dragged; after that it is kept inside the chart. A press on its scroll bar scrolls rather than drags.
    - **Shown or hidden** from the menu or with L. A hidden legend stays hidden through new data and a new recording.
- **The right-click menu,** rebuilt each time it opens, in the Qt order:
  - **The items:** Set Plot Title; Plot File; View Mode (its key in its title); Customize View; Show Legend (L); Readout; X Axis (Set Time Window, Zoom Back, Reset Span); Y Axes (the left and right minimum and maximum, then Reset); Reset View (R).
  - **Disabled until there is data:** every item that acts on it. Zoom Back is disabled until there is a zoom to go back to. View Mode is disabled unless both metrics exist.
  - **The keys are advertised, not bound:** each item's key is shown on it, but the keys are the chart's own.
  - **Readout:** pins the readout (4.3b) to one of the series shown, or leaves it on the nearest. A pin whose series has been hidden or replaced is dropped when the menu opens.
  - **Export is not on it:** it is a file operation, in the main menu (4.5).
  - **Plot File is disabled:** one recording has nothing to switch between, and batch runs are 4.7's.
- **The prompts** (`PlotCommands` over `IPlotPrompts`, shown by `WindowPlotPrompts` as windows over the main window):
  - **Set Plot Title.**
  - **Set Time Window:** a start and a stop as DDD:HH:MM:SS, seeded with the window shown. Each end is clamped into the recording, and the stop pulled up to the start. Each correction is a goldenrod warning in the log, worded as the Qt one is.
  - **The four axis limits:** each bounded so that it cannot invert its axis. Lock % runs up to 100 and missed frames to 10,000,000, in whole numbers; SNR runs from -999 to 999 dB, to one decimal.
- **The keys,** as the Qt `keyPressEvent` has them:
  - L the legend, V the metric, R both axes;
  - Backspace one zoom back, Home the whole span (keeping a Y limit set);
  - the arrows a tenth of the window, + and - the window about its centre.

  They act only while the chart has focus, which a click gives it: a bare letter taken for the whole window would be lost to every text box. Without data they do nothing.
- **Customize View** (`CustomizeViewWindow` over `CustomizeViewModel`, the Qt `PlotCustomizationDialog`):
  - **The Frame Sync Lock tab:** a row per stream, with a box ("CH &lt;id&gt;") for both its metrics, a colour swatch and its name. Select All and Select None.
  - **The Receiver SNR tab:** one stream at a time, chosen from "CH &lt;id&gt; — &lt;name&gt;". Its receivers are in two columns, each a tristate box over its L, R and C channels, collapsed at first. Expand All / Collapse All, Select All and Select None act on the stream shown. A channel's menu renames or recolours it.
  - **Only OK applies, in one refresh:**
    - a stream's box shows only the metric in view, since the other is on another scale;
    - names and colours reach a stream's other metric too;
    - a series replaced while the dialog was open is skipped.
  - **The colour dialog** is Avalonia's `ColorView`, from **`Avalonia.Controls.ColorPicker` 12.1.4**, a new package: MIT, Avalonia's own, and through the licence check.

**Not ported, or not yet:**
- **Remembering the legend's state between sessions** is 4.8's, with the other preferences and their migration from the Qt app's `QSettings`. Until then it is remembered for the session.
- **The dark theme** is 4.8's. The "Loading..." overlay belongs to CSV import, which is 4.5's.
- **The legend is rebuilt whole,** not reconciled row by row as the Qt one was. That reconciliation spared Qt widget churn over many streams; a rebuild of 48 rows is cheap here.

**Found on the way:**
- **US4.0 says a short SNR label keeps "the full name ... available via tooltip"; the Qt legend has no tooltip.** Its rows are transparent to the mouse, for the drag. The port gives each shortened row its full name as a tooltip, which the drag does not need to give up.
- **The scroll bar covered the labels.** I first reserved 12 px for it, and a test measuring the rendered rows found Fluent's bar is 16 px. That test now holds the theme to it.
- **The colour dialog clipped its own slider** at 300 px wide. It was found by looking at a render, not by a test, and the dialog is now 360 px wide.
- **US4.1's Qt choice that the keys are not application-wide holds here by construction:** a key event goes to the focused control and up, so the plot sees one only while it has focus.

**Each acceptance criterion this step covers**, with the test that holds it:
- **US4.0:**
  - **Every control on the right-click menu, disabled until data:** `TheMenuLeadsWithTheTitleAndHoldsEveryPlotControlAndNoExport`, `TheMenusDataItemsWaitForData`, `ARightClickOnTheChartOpensTheMenu`.
  - **The plot's title:** `TheTitleAndTheTimeWindowAreAskedSeededWithWhatIsShown`.
  - **The time window, clamped with a warning:** `ATimeWindowIsClampedIntoTheRecordingWithAWarningForEachEnd`, `AClampedTimeWindowIsAWarningInTheLog`, `ATypedClockTimeIsElapsedTimeOnThePlotsAxis`.
  - **Overriding either end of either axis:** `EachAxisLimitIsAskedWithinBoundsThatCannotInvertTheAxis`, `TheMenusAxisItemsResetZoomBackAndAsk`.
  - **Showing and hiding series:** `CustomizeViewHasARowPerLockStreamAndTheSnrStreamsByReceiver`, `OkShowsOnlyTheMetricInViewAndAppliesTheNamesAndColours`, `AReceiversBoxFollowsItsChannelsAndSetsThemAll`.
  - **The legend:**
    - floating, top right: `TheLegendFloatsAtTheTopRightWithARowPerSeriesShown`;
    - dragged: `TheLegendIsDraggedAnywhereInsideTheChartAndKeptThere`, `AnUndraggedLegendFollowsTheTopRightWhenTheChartIsResized`;
    - shown and hidden: `TheMenuSetsTheViewModeAndTheLegend`, `AHiddenLegendStaysHiddenUntilShownAgain`;
    - translucent: `TheLegendIsTranslucentSoTheDataBehindItShows`;
    - capped, with a scroll bar: `ADenseLegendIsCappedAndScrollsWithoutCoveringALabel`;
    - short SNR rows, with the tooltip: `TheLegendListsTheSeriesShownOfTheMetricInView`.
  - **Renaming and recolouring:** `ARenameOrRecolourReachesAStreamsOtherMetricAndNoOtherStream`, `OkShowsOnlyTheMetricInViewAndAppliesTheNamesAndColours`, `EachPromptAnswersOnOkAndNothingOnCancel`.
  - **Not yet:** the choice kept across sessions (4.8), and the legend in exported images (4.5).
- **US4.1:**
  - **The chip bar:** `TheChipBarIsOverTheChartAtTheTopLeftAndOnlyWithData`, `TheViewModeChipSwitchesTheLeftAxisAndIsNamedForWhereItGoes`, `TheResetChipAppearsOnlyOnceTheViewHasChanged`.
  - **The menu's order:** `TheMenuLeadsWithTheTitleAndHoldsEveryPlotControlAndNoExport`.
